* **Override of `LoadCoverageData`** – loads coverage data from a directory.  
* **`RemoveUnCoveredFiles`** – cleans up any files that did not receive coverage.  
* **`ReadCMCovFile`** – parses an individual cache‑coverage file, returning success or failure.

@l./Source/CTest/cmParseCoberturaCoverag.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/CTest/cmParseCoberturaCoverag.body: The file implements a Cobertura XML parser. It defines an `XMLParser` class derived from `cmXMLParser` that walks the Cobertura XML tree, collecting file paths and line‑hit counts. When encountering a `<source>` element it records the file path; when it encounters a `<line>` element it records hit counts for the corresponding line number. It resolves relative paths against known source and binary directories, skips files that cannot be opened, and finally stores the results in a `cmCTestCoverageHandlerContainer` map that tracks coverage per file. The top‑level `cmParseCoberturaCoverage` class simply exposes `ReadCoverageXML` to drive this parser.

@l./Source/CTest/cmParseCoberturaCoverag.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/CTest/cmParseCoberturaCoverag.body: The header defines a helper class that takes a test object and a coverage‑handler container, parses the XML emitted by the Cobertura‑style `coverage.py` command, and populates the supplied container with coverage information for each source file. The `ReadCoverageXML` method opens the XML file, walks its elements and extracts file names and hit counts into internal structures that are then used by the test framework to compute per‑file coverage metrics.

@l./Source/CTest/cmParseDelphiCoverage.c.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/CTest/cmParseDelphiCoverage.c.body: The file implements a thin wrapper around a custom coverage‑reader: it creates a small parser class that reads an HTML report produced by the “Delphi” tool, extracts the line numbers from the `<tr class="…">` tags, and marks those lines as covered in an internal coverage vector. The top‑level functions (`LoadCoverageData` and `ReadDelphiHTML`) drive the process by opening each HTML file, invoking the parser, and recording the results in a `cmCTestCoverageHandlerContainer`.

@l./Source/CTest/cmParseDelphiCoverage.h.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/CTest/cmParseDelphiCoverage.h.body: This header defines a small helper class that pulls coverage data out of the HTML output produced by the Delphi coverage tool.  It holds references to a handler‑container and a test object, and offers a constructor plus two helper functions for loading a set of files and for reading individual HTML fragments from disk.  An internal nested `HTMLParser` class is declared to handle the parsing logic.

@l./Source/CTest/cmParseGTMCoverage.cxx.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/CTest/cmParseGTMCoverage.cxx.body: The class walks a directory of “.mcov” files, parses each coverage line to pull out routine, function, line‑number and hit‑count, then locates the corresponding source file. It searches that file for the routine’s first line, uses that offset to index into its internal vector, and accumulates the hit counts. When a routine or file is absent, it logs an error.

@l./Source/CTest/cmParseGTMCoverage.h.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/CTest/cmParseGTMCoverage.h.body:
The header introduces a helper class that pulls GTM coverage data into the system.  
- It inherits from the generic mumps‑coverage parser (`cmParseMumpsCoverage`).  
- Its constructor receives a container of test‑coverage handlers and a test object.  
- It overrides `LoadCoverageData` to read a directory of `.mcov` files.  
- Internally it offers helpers to read a single file, locate a function within a mumps file, and parse individual `.mcov` lines into routine, function, line‑number, and hit‑count information.

@l./Source/CTest/cmParseJacocoCoverage.c.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/CTest/cmParseJacocoCoverage.c.body: The file implements a Jacoco‑coverage XML parser that walks through the XML tags, extracts the package and source‑file names, resolves those file paths by globbing the source directory tree, and records the line‑coverage data into a shared coverage container while reporting errors when files cannot be located.

@l./Source/CTest/cmParseJacocoCoverage.h.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/CTest/cmParseJacocoCoverage.h.body: The header defines a helper that reads JaCoCo XML files, maps each routine to its source file, and prunes the coverage records by dropping any file that reports zero hit counts. It exposes a `LoadCoverageData` function that feeds a list of XML files into the parser, which internally calls `ReadJacocoXML`, `SplitString`, and `FindJavaFile` to resolve file paths, and finally hands the parsed data to the `cmCTestCoverageHandlerContainer`. The class keeps a `RoutineToDirectory` map to map routine names to file paths and holds the `Coverage` container and the test under test for which it collects coverage data.

@l./Source/CTest/cmParseMumpsCoverage.cx.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/CTest/cmParseMumpsCoverage.cx.body:
The file implements the `cmParseMumpsCoverage` helper that loads a coverage specification file, maps routine names to the corresponding `.m` files in the specified package directories, and then parses each `.m` file to populate a per‑file vector of executable line flags (‑1 = non‑executable, 0 = potentially executable, 1 = executed). It exposes three main entry points:  
- **`ReadCoverageFile`** reads a simple two‑line file (`packages:` and `coverage_dir:`) and invokes `LoadPackages`/`LoadCoverageData`.  
- **`LoadPackages`** recursively discovers all `.m` files under the given package path, builds a name‑to‑path map, and calls `InitializeMumpsFile` for each file.  
- **`InitializeMumpsFile`** walks a single `.m` file, marking the first line as non‑executable and then scanning the rest of the file to detect whether a line contains executable code (by detecting labels, whitespace and semicolons).  

The implementation is deliberately compact; it relies on helper classes (`cmSystemTools`, `cmStrCat`, `cmsys::Glob`) for file traversal and string handling. The logic is straightforward and can be extended for larger file sets or alternative file formats.

@l./Source/CTest/cmParseMumpsCoverage.h.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/CTest/cmParseMumpsCoverage.h.body:
This header declares a helper for the Mumps coverage framework.  
The constructor wires a test handler container and a test object, storing them in protected members.  
`ReadCoverageFile` opens a coverage file and hands its path to the pure virtual `LoadCoverageData` implemented by derived parsers.  
`LoadPackages` walks a package directory, populating `RoutineToDirectory` with routine‑to‑mumps‑file mappings.  
`InitializeMumpsFile` prepares per‑file data and `FindMumpsFile` resolves a routine to an actual file path.  
The class is designed to be inherited by concrete parsers that supply the specific file‑format logic.

@l./Source/CTest/cmParsePHPCoverage.cxx.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/CTest/cmParsePHPCoverage.cxx.body: The file implements a parser for PHP‑coverage files produced by the test framework. It opens each coverage file in a directory, reads the serialized format (a header “s:…”, followed by an array of line‑count pairs inside braces), and populates the coverage vector stored in `Coverage.TotalCoverage`. The parser loops through all files in a folder, validates the format, extracts line numbers and counts, and updates the in‑memory data structure accordingly. This enables the test harness to reconstruct which lines of each PHP source were executed during a run.

@l./Source/CTest/cmParsePHPCoverage.h.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/CTest/cmParsePHPCoverage.h.body:
The header declares a small helper that pulls the PHP‐coverage dump emitted by xdebug into in‑memory test‑coverage handlers.  
An instance of `cmParsePHPCoverage` is created with a reference to the container that owns all coverage handlers and a pointer to the test it belongs to. Its public interface exposes two steps: first `ReadPHPCoverageDirectory` scans a filesystem path, loading every dump file it finds, and then `PrintCoverage` walks the in‑memory structure to emit a readable summary. Internally, it reads raw stream data using a handful of helpers (`ReadArraySize`, `ReadInt`, `ReadCoverageArray`, etc.) that consume the binary layout of the xdebug dump, building the nested array of per‑file coverage entries that the container will later query.

@l./Source/CTest/cmProcess.cxx.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/CTest/cmProcess.cxx.body: The file defines a `cmProcess` helper that spawns a child process with libuv, redirects its I/O through pipes, buffers the output, decodes text, and forwards complete lines to a test runner. It tracks run‑time, applies a timeout timer, and interprets exit codes or termination signals as specific failure types (e.g. segmentation fault, signal, or platform‑specific exit codes). The logic also handles graceful kill, custom timeout signals, and reports the result to the test framework.

@l./Source/CTest/cmProcess.h.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/CTest/cmProcess.h.body: The header declares a C++ wrapper that spawns a child process via libuv, tracks its life cycle (starting, executing, expiring, terminating), records exit codes and termination style, and streams its stdout into an internal buffer so callers can pull complete lines or last fragments.

@l./Source/CursesDialog/ccmake.cxx.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/CursesDialog/ccmake.cxx.body: The file implements the main entry point for ccmake, wiring up the curses‑based UI, parsing command‑line arguments, initializing system resources, handling resize signals, launching the internal ccmake engine, reporting progress and errors through callbacks, and finally cleaning up the UI before exit.

@l./Source/CursesDialog/cmCursesBoolWidg.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/CursesDialog/cmCursesBoolWidg.body:
The widget represents a toggleable boolean field in a curses UI.  
On receiving an ENTER or SPACE key it flips its value between the strings “ON” and “OFF”, updates the field’s foreground/background colors accordingly (if a color pair is available), and marks the widget as static. The constructor tags the widget as type `BOOL`, clears the static flag, and defaults the stored value to “OFF”.

@l./Source/CursesDialog/cmCursesBoolWidg.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/CursesDialog/cmCursesBoolWidg.body:
The header declares a Boolean toggle widget that plugs into the larger *cmake* curses UI framework.  
It derives from the generic `cmCursesWidget`, supplies a constructor that takes the widget’s size and position, disables copying, and overrides the `HandleInput()` virtual hook to process key presses when the widget has focus.  
Two helper calls (`SetValueAsBool`/`GetValueAsBool`) expose a single‑bit value that the rest of the GUI can query or modify.

@l./Source/CursesDialog/cmCursesCacheEnt.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/CursesDialog/cmCursesCacheEnt.body:
The file implements a UI helper that constructs a composite widget displaying a cache entry.  
When instantiated it queries the supplied `cmState` to discover the entry’s value type (bool, path, file‑path, or string/option list). It then creates and configures the appropriate `cmCurses…Widget`—`Bool`, `Path`, `FilePath`, `String`, or an option selector—assigning the value so that the widget reflects the cached value immediately. For new entries it adds an “*” marker; otherwise it renders a blank label. The constructor also guards against unknown entry types, emitting an error if an unsupported type is encountered.

@l./Source/CursesDialog/cmCursesCacheEnt.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/CursesDialog/cmCursesCacheEnt.body:
The header declares a small composite widget class used in the curses‑based UI.  
It holds unique pointers to a label widget, an optional “new” flag label, and the entry widget itself.  
The class exposes constructors that accept a key string and size parameters, a `GetValue` accessor, and disables copy semantics while allowing default move semantics.  
It is intended to be used by the main form for displaying cached entries.

@l./Source/CursesDialog/cmCursesColor.cx.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/CursesDialog/cmCursesColor.cx.body: The file provides a small helper that conditionally initializes a set of color pairs in a curses‑based UI. It exposes three static helpers: `HasColors()` checks whether the build configuration supports colors; `InitColors()` sets up a handful of named pairs (BoolOff, BoolOn, String, Path, Choice) by calling `init_pair()` with colors that may come from an environment variable `CCMAKE_COLORS`; and `GetColor()` parses that variable once (using a static unordered_map) and returns either the mapped value or a supplied fallback. The implementation deliberately falls back to no‑color operation when the build macro `HAVE_CURSES_USE_DEFAULT_COLORS` is not defined.

@l./Source/CursesDialog/cmCursesColor.h.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/CursesDialog/cmCursesColor.h.body: The header declares a small helper class that groups a handful of constant identifiers (BoolOff, BoolOn, String, Path, Choice) used by the application to map logical states to terminal color codes. It offers two public helpers: `HasColors` to probe whether the runtime supports color pairs and `InitColors` to seed the curses library with the needed pairs. The protected static helper `GetColor` translates an identifier into the corresponding curses color index, falling back to a supplied fallback code when the mapping is unavailable. This helper is invoked by other parts of the code to request color values for rendering UI elements.

@l./Source/CursesDialog/cmCursesDummyWid.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/CursesDialog/cmCursesDummyWid.body: The file implements a minimal widget class that inherits from `cmCursesWidget`. Its constructor sets the widget’s type to `cmStateEnums::INTERNAL`, and its input handler simply returns `false`, meaning the widget does not process any input.

@l./Source/CursesDialog/cmCursesDummyWid.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/CursesDialog/cmCursesDummyWid.body:
It declares a `cmCursesDummyWidget` class that inherits from `cmCursesWidget`.  
The class is non‑copyable (copy constructor and assignment operator deleted).  
It exposes a constructor that takes width, height, and screen offsets, and it overrides `HandleInput` to process keyboard events when the widget has focus.

@l./Source/CursesDialog/cmCursesFilePath.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/CursesDialog/cmCursesFilePath.body:
The file implements the constructor for the `cmCursesFilePathWidget` class.  
It derives from `cmCursesPathWidget` and simply assigns the widget’s internal type to `cmStateEnums::FILEPATH`. The implementation is minimal—primarily used to signal that this widget should handle file‑path inputs.

@l./Source/CursesDialog/cmCursesFilePath.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/CursesDialog/cmCursesFilePath.body: A class that extends the generic path‑editing widget, exposing only a constructor that takes size and position. It locks the object to single‑instance usage by deleting copy‑ctor and copy‑assignment, and pulls in the necessary project headers via an “include‑what‑you‑use” pragma.

@l./Source/CursesDialog/cmCursesForm.cxx.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/CursesDialog/cmCursesForm.cxx.body: The `cmCursesForm` class encapsulates a ncurses‑style form that opens, renders, and tears down a terminal UI. It keeps a static debug flag and log file to trace form‐level activity, gracefully cleaning up any allocated form when the object is destroyed and re‑initializing the screen whenever the terminal is resized.

@l./Source/CursesDialog/cmCursesForm.h.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/CursesDialog/cmCursesForm.h.body: Provides a thin interface for a curses‑based UI form: pure virtual handlers for user input, rendering a rectangular region, and status‑bar updates; a simple error‑logging hook; and a static debug‑log facility that opens a file when debugging is enabled. It also keeps a global pointer to the current form instance for use by low‑level helpers.

@l./Source/CursesDialog/cmCursesLabelWid.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/CursesDialog/cmCursesLabelWid.body: The file defines a simple label widget that derives from a generic curses‑based widget. The constructor turns off all edit, active, and static flags for the internal field and pushes the supplied text into that field. The destructor is trivial. The widget never processes key events, simply returning `false` to indicate that it is read‑only.

@l./Source/CursesDialog/cmCursesLabelWid.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/CursesDialog/cmCursesLabelWid.body: The header declares a `cmCursesLabelWidget` widget class that inherits from `cmCursesWidget`. It exposes a constructor taking dimensions and a name, a virtual destructor, and a `HandleInput` override that returns whether a key event was consumed. The class is non‑copyable and non‑assignable, and is intended to be dropped into a `cmCursesMainForm` container for rendering labels in a curses‑style UI.

@l./Source/CursesDialog/cmCursesLongMess.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/CursesDialog/cmCursesLongMess.body:
The implementation supplies a single‑field curses form that concatenates a list of strings into one message buffer and draws it line by line.  
The constructor stores a title and message list, and the form’s status bar is refreshed on every input by recomputing the title and version string into a fixed‑width line.  
Input handling centers on the `HandleInput()` loop, which interprets arrow keys, control‑keystrokes (via `ctrl()`), and page‑style scrolling to move the form cursor while keeping the status bar updated.

@l./Source/CursesDialog/cmCursesLongMess.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/CursesDialog/cmCursesLongMess.body: The header declares a `cmCursesLongMessageForm` that inherits from `cmCursesForm`. It stores a list of message strings, a title, and a scrolling mode (no scroll or scroll‑down). The class exposes functions to update the displayed content, handle user input, render the form in a specified window region, and update the status bar. The class also provides helpers for drawing individual messages and manages internal field pointers.

@l./Source/CursesDialog/cmCursesMainForm.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/CursesDialog/cmCursesMainForm.body: `cmCursesMainForm` orchestrates a curses‑based UI for the CMake project configuration tool. It parses command‑line arguments, creates a list of cache entries, and renders them as labeled fields that can be edited, added, or removed by key presses. The main loop handles navigation (arrow keys, page jumps, search), editing (enter, backspace, cursor movement), and command shortcuts (configure, generate, quit, help, show logs). Cache changes are propagated back to the CMake state machine, and progress updates are shown in a status bar. The program also handles dynamic resizing, error reporting, and dialog output for console messages.

@l./Source/CursesDialog/cmCursesMainForm.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/CursesDialog/cmCursesMainForm.body: The header declares the main form for the CMake UI, tying together the cache‑entry widgets, rendering logic, status‑bar updates, and command‑key displays. It also declares the hooks for configuring, generating, and writing cache data, as well as the callbacks for error reporting and progress progress.

@l./Source/CursesDialog/cmCursesOptionsW.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/CursesDialog/cmCursesOptionsW.body: The widget holds a list of string options and cycles through them when the user presses left/right arrows or Ctrl‑b/f keys. When an option is selected it calls `SetValue` to update the field’s visual contents. The field is rendered with either color pairs (if terminal supports colors) or normal attributes, and the widget is marked static via `field_opts_off`. The widget is used in the larger form system as one of several option‑widgets that respond to simple key navigation.

@l./Source/CursesDialog/cmCursesOptionsW.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/CursesDialog/cmCursesOptionsW.body: The `cmCursesOptionsWidget` class implements an option‑selection widget that stores a list of string options, tracks the currently highlighted one, and exposes helper methods (`AddOption`, `SetOption`, `NextOption`, `PreviousOption`) to modify the list or advance the current index. It overrides `HandleInput` to react to keystrokes when the widget has focus, returning whether the event was consumed. The class inherits from `cmCursesWidget` and is instantiated with a fixed geometry.

@l./Source/CursesDialog/cmCursesPathWidg.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/CursesDialog/cmCursesPathWidg.body: The file implements a curses‑based widget that accepts a file‑system path string. It sets foreground and background colors based on whether terminal color support is available, and implements tab‑completion by globbing the typed prefix against the file system. When the user tabs, the widget cycles through matching entries; if the current entry is a directory it appends a trailing slash. The widget inherits from a generic string widget and forwards the usual string‑editing callbacks after handling its own completion logic.

@l./Source/CursesDialog/cmCursesPathWidg.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/CursesDialog/cmCursesPathWidg.body: cmCursesPathWidget is a curses‑based widget that extends cmCursesStringWidget to accept and edit file‑path strings. It supplies specialized handlers for Tab, Return, and typed keys, keeping track of the last entered string, a glob pattern and a cycling flag to shift focus between fields. It is used wherever a form must accept a path input in a terminal UI.

@l./Source/CursesDialog/cmCursesStandard.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/CursesDialog/cmCursesStandard.body:
The header supplies a thin compatibility layer around the *curses* API.  
It pulls in the project‑wide configuration (`cmConfigure.h`) and pulls in the standard `<form.h>` form handling headers.  
The bulk of the file is a set of inline helpers that wrap the raw `move`, `erase`, and `clear` functions from *curses* so they won’t clash with names in the surrounding namespace.  
On HP‑UX systems it guards against the pre‑defining of `_BOOL_DEFINED` and pulls in `<sys/time.h>` when needed.  
The file also tidies up the `__attribute__` macro that a few platforms spill into the global namespace, undefining it to avoid header conflicts.  
Finally, the file concludes by cleaning out the helper macros (`move`, `erase`, `clear`) that were pulled in to provide the wrapper functions.

@l./Source/CursesDialog/cmCursesStringWi.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/CursesDialog/cmCursesStringWi.body:
The file implements a single‑field text widget that plugs into a Curses form. It tracks whether the field is in edit mode and toggles that state on the <Enter> key or the letter “i” (mimicking Vim).  

When the field is edited it logs the change, saves the original buffer, and forces the form to redraw the field by issuing `REQ_NEXT_FIELD`/`REQ_PREV_FIELD` to the form driver. Exiting edit restores the original buffer on **Esc** or a return after a change.  

Key processing is centralized in **HandleInput**: after the initial “enter/return” check it loops reading characters, dispatching them to form handlers (`REQ_*` codes) for navigation, editing, and deletion. Unrecognised keys are forwarded to **OnType**, which forwards the key to the form driver.  

The class offers `SetString`, `GetString`, and `GetValue` to manipulate the internal string, and `PrintKeys` to paint a help line when in edit mode.

@l./Source/CursesDialog/cmCursesStringWi.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/CursesDialog/cmCursesStringWi.body:
cmCursesStringWidget is a simple text‐entry widget that inherits from cmCursesWidget. It stores the entered text in a std::string member (OriginalString) and exposes access via SetString / GetString. A boolean flag (InEdit) tracks whether the widget is in edit mode, which can be toggled by SetInEdit/GetInEdit.  
The widget responds to key events: OnType handles arbitrary character input, while OnTab and OnReturn provide hooks for tab/return actions. The widget implements HandleInput to intercept input when it has focus and overrides PrintKeys to supply its own shortcut keys when applicable. The internal flag Done indicates whether input handling finished.

@l./Source/CursesDialog/cmCursesWidget.c.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/CursesDialog/cmCursesWidget.c.body: The implementation creates an ncurses field object in the constructor, storing it in `Field`, attaching the widget itself as its user pointer, and turning off the `O_AUTOSKIP` option. `Move()` repositions the field and, when requested, flags it as a “new‑page” field. `SetValue()` updates the internal string and writes it into the field buffer. `GetValue()` simply returns the stored string. The destructor frees the field if it was created.

@l./Source/CursesDialog/cmCursesWidget.h.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/CursesDialog/cmCursesWidget.h.body: This header declares a base widget class that stores geometry information, a type tag, and a value string. It exposes a small interface: constructors, a virtual `HandleInput` for subclasses to process key events; a virtual `Move` to change the widget’s position and mark page boundaries; virtual setters/getters for the stored value; a helper `GetType` that reports the widget’s enum type; and a `PrintKeys` hook that subclasses can override to provide toolbar help. The class also manages a page number and a raw field pointer, and forbids copying by deleting copy‑ctor and assignment.

@l./Source/CursesDialog/form/eti.h.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/CursesDialog/form/eti.h.body: The file declares a set of error constants that the rest of the code uses to signal various failure conditions such as a bad argument, lack of a connection, or an unauthorized request. These codes are used throughout the project to check return values and decide control flow. The file also contains the standard copyright and licensing notice that governs its redistribution.

@l./Source/CursesDialog/form/fld_arg.c.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/CursesDialog/form/fld_arg.c.body:
The file defines two utilities used by the form‑handling library.  
`set_fieldtype_arg` accepts a field type descriptor and three optional function pointers – `make_arg`, `copy_arg` and `free_arg` – storing them in the descriptor’s argument slots after validating non‑NULL inputs; it also marks the type as having arguments.  
`field_arg` merely returns the stored argument block for a specific field, after normalising the field structure.

@l./Source/CursesDialog/form/fld_attr.c.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/CursesDialog/form/fld_attr.c.body: The file implements a macro‑driven code generation scheme that produces boiler‑plate setters and getters for field attributes. Each generated setter checks that the supplied attribute value conforms to the predefined attribute set, normalises the field before assignment and, on change, invokes a synchronisation routine to keep auxiliary state consistent. The matching getter simply reads the attribute field after normalising the field, masking the result with the attribute mask. This pattern is repeated for every attribute (foreground, background, …) via the `GEN_FIELD_ATTR_SET_FCT` and `GEN_FIELD_ATTR_GET_FCT` macros.

@l./Source/CursesDialog/form/fld_current.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/CursesDialog/form/fld_current.body: The file implements the logic for switching the active field of a form object. It provides three primary routines: setting a new current field (with validation, hooks, and status checks), retrieving the current field pointer, and querying a field’s index in the form’s internal array. The implementation covers error handling for invalid arguments, non‑selectable fields, and state restrictions while ensuring the form’s hooks are called appropriately.

@l./Source/CursesDialog/form/fld_def.c.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/CursesDialog/form/fld_def.c.body: Defines the core logic for creating, copying, and destroying the argument structures that back a form field type. It provides routines such as `_nc_Make_Argument`, `_nc_Copy_Argument`, and `_nc_Free_Argument` to walk the linked‑argument tree, plus helpers for copying a field’s type data (`_nc_Copy_Type`) and cleaning it up (`_nc_Free_Type`). The file also implements the public API for allocating a new field (`new_field`) and releasing it (`free_field`), using a static `default_field` template that is duplicated into each new instance.

@l./Source/CursesDialog/form/fld_dup.c.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/CursesDialog/form/fld_dup.c.body: The file implements a function that, given a source field and target coordinates, returns a fresh field structure with all attributes copied. It checks that the input field and coordinates are valid, allocates a new structure, copies the original’s content (including its buffer), sets the new row/column, and links the new object into the list. If allocation fails or arguments are wrong, the function cleans up and returns NULL, setting errno accordingly.

@l./Source/CursesDialog/form/fld_ftchoic.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/CursesDialog/form/fld_ftchoic.body: The file implements a helper that registers callbacks for navigating a field‑type enumeration. It receives a pointer to a `FIELDTYPE` structure and two function pointers that determine the next and previous choice for a field. The routine validates that none of the arguments are null, sets a status flag indicating the type has an associated choice routine, stores the supplied callbacks in the structure, and signals success or a bad‑argument error.

@l./Source/CursesDialog/form/fld_ftlink..author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/CursesDialog/form/fld_ftlink..body: The file defines a helper that builds a new field type by joining two existing types. It first checks that both arguments are non‑NULL, allocates a fresh `FIELDTYPE` object, copies a default template into it, and then propagates the presence of arguments and choice flags from either operand. The new type’s `left` and `right` members point to the input types, and the reference counts of those inputs are increased. If allocation fails or arguments are missing, the routine sets an appropriate error code (`E_SYSTEM_ERROR` or `E_BAD_ARGUMENT`). The routine is used elsewhere in the library for composing field types.

@l./Source/CursesDialog/form/fld_info.c.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/CursesDialog/form/fld_info.c.body: The file implements two helper routines that copy a field structure’s dimensional attributes (rows, columns, field‑row offsets, buffer counts, etc.) into caller‑supplied integer pointers. The functions perform a null‑check on the field argument, populate the output parameters when requested, and return either E_OK or E_BAD_ARGUMENT.

@l./Source/CursesDialog/form/fld_just.c.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/CursesDialog/form/fld_just.c.body: The file implements two helpers for manipulating a field’s justification flag. `set_field_just` validates the passed justification value against the allowed constants, normalises the field, updates the flag if the value differs, and then synchronises the field’s attributes. `field_just` simply normalises the field and returns the current justification value. The code relies on `Normalize_Field` and `_nc_Synchronize_Attributes` for consistency and persistence.

@l./Source/CursesDialog/form/fld_link.c.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/CursesDialog/form/fld_link.c.body: The file implements a helper that clones a field structure, copies its geometry and visual attributes into a freshly allocated struct, then hooks the new instance into the original field’s link chain while preserving all buffer references. It uses the custom error‑code logic (`E_BAD_ARGUMENT`, `E_SYSTEM_ERROR`) and a `SET_ERROR` macro to surface failure via `errno`. The conditional that triggers the copy is intentionally obfuscated; in its current form it never succeeds, so the function normally falls back to returning NULL.

@l./Source/CursesDialog/form/fld_max.c.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/CursesDialog/form/fld_max.c.body: The `set_max_field` routine validates the provided field pointer and growth value, then stores the requested maximum size in the field structure. It adjusts internal status flags to reflect whether the field is now eligible for dynamic expansion (based on the current dimensions and the static option) and returns a success or error code accordingly.

@l./Source/CursesDialog/form/fld_move.c.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/CursesDialog/form/fld_move.c.body: The file defines a helper routine that, given a pointer to a `FIELD` structure, attempts to reposition the field in a form when it is not already tied to one. It first validates that the supplied coordinates are non‑negative and that the field structure is present, then checks that the field is not already connected to a form. If those conditions hold it writes the new row/column values into the structure and returns a success code; otherwise it returns the appropriate error code (`E_BAD_ARGUMENT` or `E_CONNECTED`).

@l./Source/CursesDialog/form/fld_newftyp.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/CursesDialog/form/fld_newftyp.body: `fld_newftyp.c` defines the `new_fieldtype` and `free_fieldtype` functions for managing `FIELDTYPE` objects. The module keeps a static default instance and uses reference counting to guard against freeing in-use types, returning error codes such as `E_BAD_ARGUMENT`, `E_CONNECTED`, and `E_OK`.

@l./Source/CursesDialog/form/fld_opts.c.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/CursesDialog/form/fld_opts.c.body:
The file implements four API functions for turning field options on or off.  

* `set_field_opts()` replaces a field’s options with a supplied set after masking it with the complete option mask and then synchronizes the new setting with the internal data structures.  
* `field_opts()` returns the current option mask for a field.  
* `field_opts_on()` merges a supplied mask into the field’s existing options, leaving other bits unchanged.  
* `field_opts_off()` removes bits in a supplied mask from the field’s options.  

All functions perform validity checks against the defined option mask (`ALL_FIELD_OPTS`), call a normalisation routine, then use `_nc_Synchronize_Options()` to apply the change and propagate it to any dependent structures. The return codes signal success, a current‑field error, or a bad‑argument/system‑error situation.

@l./Source/CursesDialog/form/fld_pad.c.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/CursesDialog/form/fld_pad.c.body:
`set_field_pad()` validates that the requested pad character is printable, then assigns it to the field’s `pad` member only when the value actually changes, and propagates the change through `_nc_Synchronize_Attributes`.  
`field_pad()` simply returns the current pad value after normalising the field.

@l./Source/CursesDialog/form/fld_page.c.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/CursesDialog/form/fld_page.c.body:
The file implements the “new‑page” flag on a form field.  
`set_new_page()` sets or clears the `_NEWPAGE` bit in a field’s status when the field is not already connected, and returns a success code.  
`new_page()` simply inspects that bit to report whether the field marks the start of a new form page.

@l./Source/CursesDialog/form/fld_stat.c.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/CursesDialog/form/fld_stat.c.body:
The file implements two small utilities for the form‑handling library.  
`set_field_status()` normalises a `FIELD` instance and then flips the internal “changed” flag in its status word according to the supplied boolean. The helper simply returns the same flag value back. The implementation relies on a single flag constant (`_CHANGED`) and uses the macro `Normalize_Field` to ensure the pointer is valid before any bitwise operation. The functions provide a thin API for other parts of the code to mark a field as dirty or clean without exposing the underlying data structures.

@l./Source/CursesDialog/form/fld_type.c.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/CursesDialog/form/fld_type.c.body: The file implements a small helper that returns the type descriptor for a field object. It pulls the type member from the normalized form of the supplied field and returns it (or NULL if none is defined).

@l./Source/CursesDialog/form/fld_user.c.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/CursesDialog/form/fld_user.c.body: The file implements two helper routines that attach and retrieve a user‑supplied opaque pointer stored in a `FIELD` object. `set_field_userptr` assigns the supplied pointer to the field’s private `usrptr` member (after normalising the field) and returns `E_OK` on success. `field_userptr` simply returns that member, yielding `NULL` when none has been set.

@l./Source/CursesDialog/form/form.priv.h.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/CursesDialog/form/form.priv.h.body:
Defines status bits, constants, and helper macros for handling form fields and their options.  
Provides prototypes for routines that create, copy, free field arguments, synchronize attributes/choices, and set form pages or current fields.  
Declares a default field type pointer and a default‑field/‑form macro for normalising NULL references.

@l./Source/CursesDialog/form/frm_cursor..author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/CursesDialog/form/frm_cursor..body: The file supplies the helper routine `pos_form_cursor` used by the form‑handling library. It validates the supplied form pointer, ensures the form is already posted, and then invokes the internal routine `_nc_Position_Form_Cursor` to move the terminal cursor to the form’s current field. The routine returns `E_OK` on success or an appropriate error code (bad argument, not posted, or system error) otherwise.

@l./Source/CursesDialog/form/frm_data.c.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/CursesDialog/form/frm_data.c.body:
`data_behind` inspects the current field of a `FORM` to see if any part of the field lies off‑screen (below the current row or beyond the beginning column).  
`data_ahead` walks forward from the form’s current field, repeatedly calling `winnstr` to read field contents until it reaches the end of the field. If a non‑pad character is found after the field’s end, it reports that the form has data “ahead”.  
The helper `After_Last_Non_Pad_Position` trims trailing padding characters from a buffer that holds the field content.  
The code uses a small static buffer for small fields and allocates a temporary buffer when the field’s width exceeds the buffer limit. Both functions rely on `winnstr` and `wmove` to fetch field contents and restore the cursor.

@l./Source/CursesDialog/form/frm_def.c.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/CursesDialog/form/frm_def.c.body:
The file implements the core logic for a form‑handling library.  
A global `default_form` structure supplies default zeroed values that a newly allocated `FORM` instance copies at creation.  
Key operations are centered on manipulating a circular list of `FIELD` objects:  

* `Insert_Field_By_Position` – places a new field in a list sorted by row‑then‑column and returns the new list head.  
* `Disconnect_Fields` – severs a form from its fields, clearing the field array and freeing any allocated page structures.  
* `Connect_Fields` – registers an array of fields with a form, counts pages, allocates page structures, and sorts fields into page ranges.  
* `Associate_Fields` – a thin wrapper that invokes `Connect_Fields` and, on success, initializes the current page.  

Higher‑level helpers use those primitives:  

* `new_form` – allocates a `FORM`, copies the defaults, and associates the supplied fields.  
* `free_form` – releases all resources tied to a form, ensuring it isn’t posted.  
* `set_form_fields` – swaps a form’s field array, temporarily disconnecting the old set and restoring it on failure.  

The remaining helpers (`form_fields`, `field_count`) expose the internal field array and count.

@l./Source/CursesDialog/form/frm_driver..author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/CursesDialog/form/frm_driver..body: The file defines a compact form‑editing engine: it implements a set of navigation routines for moving the cursor through fields (row, column, word boundaries), synchronizes field buffers with screen windows, and provides the core editing primitives (insert, delete, wrap, scroll). The implementation relies on a single `Binding_Info` struct, static helpers for buffer manipulation, and a collection of navigation callbacks for page and field traversal. The bulk of the code is composed of static helper functions that perform low‑level buffer and cursor management, all wired into higher‑level public entry points that drive the user interface.

@l./Source/CursesDialog/form/frm_hook.c.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/CursesDialog/form/frm_hook.c.body:
The file supplies a set of thin wrapper functions that store and expose function pointers in a form structure.  
Through two simple macros it creates the four setter functions (`set_*_init`, `set_*_term`) and the corresponding getter functions (`*_init()`, `*_term()`) for both form‑level and field‑level callbacks.  
These hooks are invoked automatically when a form is shown/hidden or a field changes, allowing an application to plug custom routines into the form handling lifecycle.

@l./Source/CursesDialog/form/frm_opts.c.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/CursesDialog/form/frm_opts.c.body:
The file provides four helper functions for manipulating a form’s option mask.  
`set_form_opts` replaces the current option set with a new mask, after validating that only allowed flags are used.  
`form_opts` simply returns the current mask.  
`form_opts_on` and `form_opts_off` add or remove specific flags, respectively, again checking that the supplied flags belong to the defined set.

@l./Source/CursesDialog/form/frm_page.c.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/CursesDialog/form/frm_page.c.body:
The file implements two core operations for the form framework.  
A routine updates the form’s current page number, performing argument validation, invoking field‑ and form‑termination hooks when the page changes, and then refreshes the active field.  
A second routine simply returns that page value.

@l./Source/CursesDialog/form/frm_post.c.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/CursesDialog/form/frm_post.c.body:
The file contains two functions that control the life‑cycle of a form window.  
`post_form` validates the form pointer, ensures the form isn’t already posted, checks that the form’s geometry fits the destination window, initializes the current page, flags the form as posted, and then fires the form‑ and field‑initialization hooks before refreshing the window.  
`unpost_form` performs the inverse: it checks that the form is actually posted and not in a driver hook, calls the field‑ and form‑termination hooks, clears the window, removes its window descriptor, and clears the posted flag.

@l./Source/CursesDialog/form/frm_req_nam.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/CursesDialog/form/frm_req_nam.body:
The module declares a static array of form‑control command names and supplies two lookup routines.  
* `form_request_name` takes a command code, verifies it is within bounds, and returns the matching string from the array.  
* `form_request_by_name` accepts a string, normalises it to upper‑case, then linearly scans the array to return the corresponding code or an error.  
Both functions perform bounds checking, and the small table size justifies the trivial linear search used.

@l./Source/CursesDialog/form/frm_scale.c.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/CursesDialog/form/frm_scale.c.body: The file implements a helper that, given a `FORM` pointer, returns its stored row‑ and column counts via out‑parameters. It validates the input, distinguishes a missing form or disconnected fields, and reports success or the appropriate error code.

@l./Source/CursesDialog/form/frm_sub.c.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/CursesDialog/form/frm_sub.c.body:
The file defines two functions that operate on a form structure:  
• **`set_form_sub`** – assigns a `WINDOW` pointer as the form’s subwindow, but refuses to do so if the form has already been posted (returning `E_POSTED`).  
• **`form_sub`** – returns the current subwindow of a supplied form by delegating to the helper that normalises the form and fetches the window.

@l./Source/CursesDialog/form/frm_user.c.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/CursesDialog/form/frm_user.c.body: The file supplies two small API functions: `set_form_userptr` stores a caller‑supplied pointer in the private `usrptr` member of a `FORM` instance, normalising the form first, and returns the constant `E_OK`; `form_userptr` fetches that pointer (or `NULL` if none has been set). Both are used by the form library to attach arbitrary context to a form instance.

@l./Source/CursesDialog/form/frm_win.c.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/CursesDialog/form/frm_win.c.body:
The source defines two helper routines for the *libnform* window‑form API.  
`set_form_win()` accepts a `FORM` and a `WINDOW`, verifies that the form has not already been posted (using the `_POSTED` flag), and then records the supplied window pointer after normalising the form.  
`form_win()` simply returns the stored window pointer, falling back to the global `stdscr` when none is set. The implementation relies on `Normalize_Form()` to obtain a canonical form instance before manipulating its `win` field.

@l./Source/CursesDialog/form/fty_alnum.c.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/CursesDialog/form/fty_alnum.c.body:
The file defines a lightweight field‑type for the libnform library that stores a single width parameter. It provides four core helpers:  
- **Make_AlphaNumeric_Type** reads a width value from a `va_list` and allocates a `alnumARG` structure.

@l./Source/LexerParser/cmCommandArgument.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/LexerParser/cmCommandArgument.body:
The scanner implements a re‑entrant, Flex‑generated lexer that reads an input stream into a circular buffer. It pulls bytes from the underlying source into a temporary buffer, tracks a read pointer, and maintains a write pointer that wraps around when the buffer becomes full. The lexer runs in three main phases:

* **Initialization** – the scanner is set up with a buffer size, a buffer pointer, and the start conditions. A default start condition is defined and the current condition is stored.

* **Reading** – characters are fetched from the input stream into the buffer. When the end of file is reached, a special EOF token is returned. The scanner automatically manages a lookahead pointer so that token characters can be returned without consuming them.

* **Token building** – The scanner emits tokens according to the current start condition. Transitions between conditions are handled by the scanner’s transition table. When a token is complete, it is returned to the caller. If an error occurs, an error token is emitted; the scanner may also request more input data when necessary.

The implementation also contains helper functions that handle token buffers, buffer sizing, and flushing. Edge‑case handling is built into the logic: empty buffers, partial buffer fills, and the buffer wrapping edge are all dealt with explicitly. Security considerations are implicitly covered by treating all input as a byte stream and not exposing raw pointers to the caller.

The file is a **Flex‑generated scanner** that implements a re‑entrant lexer.  
Key ideas to keep in mind when using or modifying it:

| Topic | What to watch for | Practical tip |
|--------|--------------------|---------------|
| **Buffer management** | 3 buffers (current, next, look‑ahead) are kept in a ring.  Buffer pointers are moved by `yy_push_buff`/`yy_pop_buff`. | Use `yy_init_buffer` to reset a buffer before reusing it. |
| **State stack** | 256‑entry stack (`yy_state_buf`) keeps a history of start conditions. | Push/pop with `yy_push_state` / `yy_pop_state` – never exceed `YY_MAX_STACK_SIZE`. |
| **Input handling** | `yyinput` pulls characters; when the buffer fills it calls `yyrestart_buf` to load more. | Make sure your input file is non‑blocking; otherwise `yyinput` can hang. |
| **Token emission** | `yyreturn` emits a token; `yyinput` may push back characters via `yyunput`. | Keep the stack size in sync – `yyunput` can grow the buffer if too many characters are pushed back. |
| **Error reporting** | On EOF it calls `yyerror`. | If you need a custom message, replace `yyerror` with your own routine. |
| **Macros & helpers** | Convenience macros (e.g., `YY_SCANNER_IS_ACTIVE`, `YY_NEW_LINE`) simplify common patterns. | Use them instead of writing raw code to avoid typos. |

In short: **This code is a re‑entrant lexer that handles input buffers, state changes, token reporting, and error conditions.  When you modify it, keep the buffer‑stack logic intact and guard against stack overflows.

@l./Source/cmAddLibraryCommand.cxx.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmAddLibraryCommand.cxx.body: The `cmAddLibraryCommand` function parses the arguments passed to the `add_library()` command, determines the desired library type (shared, static, module, object, unknown, interface, or alias), processes optional keywords (e.g., `STATIC`, `SHARED`, `INTERFACE`, `ALIAS`, `EXCLUDE_FROM_ALL`, `IMPORTED`, `GLOBAL`), validates the target name, checks for conflicts (duplicate names, incompatible type combinations, and reserved names), and then delegates to the `cmMakefile` instance to create the target—adding an imported target, an alias target, or a normal library target—while emitting warnings or errors when the requested configuration is invalid or unsupported.

@l./Source/cmAddLibraryCommand.h.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmAddLibraryCommand.h.body: The header declares a helper that accepts a list of string arguments and a status object, returning a success flag. It pulls in cmConfigure.h and standard headers, and declares the cmExecutionStatus type for status reporting. This function is used throughout the code to register a library command.

@l./Source/cmAddLinkOptionsCommand.cxx.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmAddLinkOptionsCommand.cxx.body:
The file defines a helper function that registers a set of link‑options strings with the current makefile.  
The routine receives a vector of strings (`args`) and a reference to a `cmExecutionStatus` object. It obtains the current `cmMakefile` from that status instance and then iterates over each string in `args`, invoking `AddLinkOption()` on the makefile for each entry. Finally it returns `true` to indicate that the operation succeeded.

@l./Source/cmAddLinkOptionsCommand.h.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmAddLinkOptionsCommand.h.body:
This header declares a helper that injects link‑options into a build configuration.  
The key pieces are:  

* `cmAddLinkOptionsCommand` – a free function that takes a `std::vector<std::string>` of option strings and a reference to a `cmExecutionStatus` object. It parses the options, applies them to the current configuration, and updates `status` with any problems.  
* The function returns `bool`, true when the options were accepted and applied cleanly, false when something went wrong.  

The file also pulls in `"cmConfigure.h"` and standard containers, and defines the `cmExecutionStatus` type used to report success or failure.

@l./Source/cmAddSubDirectoryCommand.cxx.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmAddSubDirectoryCommand.cxx.body: The file implements the command that adds a source sub‑directory to a makefile. The routine parses the supplied arguments, sets flags for “EXCLUDE_FROM_ALL” and “SYSTEM”, resolves both source and binary paths (normalising relative paths against the current source/binary directories), verifies that the source path actually exists, and finally calls `mf.AddSubDirectory` with the fully‑resolved paths and the flag values. The function returns success or failure through the status object and performs no other side effects.

@l./Source/cmAddSubDirectoryCommand.h.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmAddSubDirectoryCommand.h.body: The header declares a helper routine that takes a list of string arguments and a status object, attempts to create a new sub‑directory in the build tree, and returns a boolean indicating whether the operation succeeded. It pulls in the common configuration header so the routine can query the current build configuration, and relies on a `cmExecutionStatus` instance to surface any errors that occur while creating the directory.

@l./Source/cmAddTestCommand.cxx.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmAddTestCommand.cxx.body: The file implements the “add‑test” command in CMake. It parses the arguments supplied after the command name: the first argument is the test name, the second is the program to run, and the rest are the program’s arguments. It verifies that at least two arguments are present, rejects duplicate tests in the same directory, and distinguishes between the old style (which only creates a test) and the new “name” style that can also specify configurations, a working directory, and whether command arguments should be list‑expanded. The logic ultimately creates or reuses a `cmTest`, assigns the command (and optional properties), and registers a `cmTestGenerator` to make the test executable.

@l./Source/cmAddTestCommand.h.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmAddTestCommand.h.body: The header defines a helper function that takes a list of command‑line arguments and a reference to an `cmExecutionStatus` object and returns a boolean indicating success. It pulls in the build configuration header and standard string/vector types so that callers can pass parsed arguments into the test‑command subsystem without needing to know the underlying implementation. The function is intended to be used by various parts of the system that need to plug in new test commands, updating the shared execution status object in the process.

@l./Source/cmAffinity.cxx.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmAffinity.cxx.body: The file implements a small helper that queries the system for the CPUs the current process may run on. It pulls in the libuv “cpumask” API where available and sets the `cm_cpuset_t` alias to the proper `cpu_set_t` type for Linux vs FreeBSD. The core function, `GetProcessorsAvailable`, walks the bits of the retrieved affinity mask and populates a `std::set<size_t>` with the indices of CPUs that are set. This module is a thin wrapper around the low‑level platform APIs to expose a single `std::set` of processor identifiers.

@l./Source/cmAffinity.h.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmAffinity.h.body: The header supplies a single helper in namespace cmAffinity: a `GetProcessorsAvailable()` function that returns a `std::set<size_t>` describing the processors currently available to the program.

@l./Source/cmAlgorithms.h.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmAlgorithms.h.body: The header supplies a suite of template helpers that operate on generic ranges: rotating iterators to slide a segment to the end, removing a fixed count of elements or a user‑supplied set of indices, removing duplicates while preserving order, and performing a binary search over a range via a small wrapper. It also defines a lightweight binary‑searcher for use in range‑based removal utilities. All helpers work on forward or bidirectional iterators and rely only on standard containers and standard algorithms, with a few lightweight custom types (`cmRange`, `cmListFileBacktrace`).

@l./Source/cmArchiveWrite.cxx.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmArchiveWrite.cxx.body: The file implements a C++ wrapper around the libarchive API that builds an archive on an output stream. It exposes a constructor that takes an output stream, a compression type, format name, compression level, and thread count, configuring the appropriate compression filter and options. The core class offers methods to add paths or files, handling recursion, metadata (timestamps, ownership, permissions) and streaming the file data via a callback. The implementation deals with error handling, timestamp parsing, and ensures correct header and data writing into the archive.

@l./Source/cmArchiveWrite.h.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmArchiveWrite.h.body: This header declares a small C++ helper that writes a “pax”‑style archive to an output stream. The class exposes a single public API: construct with a stream and optional compression level, add files or directories (recursively if desired) while optionally stripping a prefix, and set optional file metadata (UID/GID, names, permissions, timestamp). Errors are stored as a string; the object can be tested for success via bool conversion. Internally it delegates to libarchive‑style routines, keeping optional values wrapped in a tiny helper class.

@l./Source/cmArgumentParser.cxx.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmArgumentParser.cxx.body: The file defines a lightweight argument‑parsing framework that stores keyword‑to‑action mappings in sorted containers, provides helper functions to bind arguments of various types (strings, vectors, optional values) to parsing actions, and contains logic that consumes tokens, tracks required keyword values, and reports missing or duplicate keyword errors.

@l./Source/cmArgumentParser.h.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmArgumentParser.h.body: The header implements a generic command‑line argument parser that maps keyword names to actions and positional arguments to values. It defines a `ParseResult` structure to report parsing errors, a `KeywordActionMap` and `PositionActionMap` for storing keyword and positional handlers, and an `Instance` type that drives the parsing loop. The `cmArgumentParser` class template provides a fluent API to bind keyword names, positional indices, or callbacks to fields or member functions in a result type, and offers overloads for parsing both key/value pairs and positional arguments. The template specialisation for `void` enables simple usage for programs that only need to validate arguments.

@l./Source/cmArgumentParserTypes.h.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmArgumentParserTypes.h.body: The header declares a small namespace of template wrappers that expose the underlying type with its constructors and operations unchanged. When compiled under SunPro’s C++ mode it supplies specializations for `std::string` and `std::vector<T>` so the wrappers use the standard constructors via `using` declarations; otherwise it simply inherits from the provided type `T`. The wrappers (`Maybe`, `MaybeEmpty`, `NonEmpty`) are thin wrappers that forward all functionality of the wrapped type while providing a common type interface for argument‑parsing utilities.

@l./Source/cmAuxSourceDirectoryCommand.c.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmAuxSourceDirectoryCommand.c.body: The routine adds files from a specified template directory to the current makefile. It first verifies it has exactly two arguments, resolves the directory path relative to the current source directory, enumerates every file in that directory, and filters those whose extensions match CMake’s recognised source types. It collects the qualifying file names, sorts them, and appends the resulting list to the makefile definition supplied by the caller.

@l./Source/cmAuxSourceDirectoryCommand.h.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmAuxSourceDirectoryCommand.h.body: The header declares a helper that processes command‑line arguments for an auxiliary source‑directory option. It takes a `std::vector<std::string>` of arguments and a reference to a `cmExecutionStatus` object, which it updates to signal success or failure. The routine returns `true` on successful handling of the arguments, otherwise `false`. It is meant to be used by other modules that need to add a temporary source directory for a build session.

@l./Source/cmBase32.cxx.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmBase32.cxx.body: Implemented in this file is a lightweight Base‑32 encoder that operates on 5‑byte blocks. A static 32‑character lookup table translates 5‑byte chunks into 8 output characters by bit‑shifting and masking. Partial blocks are padded with zero bytes before encoding, and optional padding characters can be appended to preserve the 8‑character alignment.

@l./Source/cmBase32.h.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmBase32.h.body:
The file supplies a small helper that turns raw data into a Base‑32 string according to RFC 4648.  
A single public method, `encodeString`, accepts a pointer and length and produces a `std::string`; it can optionally pad the output with `=` to make the string a well‑formed Base‑32 token.  The class offers a trivial constructor and a default destructor, and exposes only the one encoding routine—no other utilities are defined here.

@l./Source/cmBinUtilsLinker.cxx.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmBinUtilsLinker.cxx.body:
The implementation in this source file simply wires up the `cmBinUtilsLinker` class.  
Its constructor stores a pointer to a `cmRuntimeDependencyArchive` object, and its `SetError` member forwards a string to that archive’s `SetError` method so the error can be reported elsewhere in the system.

@l./Source/cmBinUtilsLinker.h.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmBinUtilsLinker.h.body:
The header declares a small helper class that stores a pointer to a `cmRuntimeDependencyArchive`.  
Its constructor accepts that archive; the class exposes a virtual `Prepare()` that simply returns `true` by default.  
A pure virtual `ScanDependencies()` is provided for derived classes, taking a file name and a target type.  
The protected member `Archive` is exposed, and a helper `SetError()` stores an error string.

@l./Source/cmBinUtilsLinuxELFGetRuntimeD.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmBinUtilsLinuxELFGetRuntimeD.body: The file implements a small helper that keeps a reference to a dependency‑archive object and forwards error messages to it. It exposes a constructor that stores the supplied archive pointer and a `SetError` routine that writes an error string into the archive’s internal state. This helper is employed by other components to propagate error information while handling runtime‑dependency extraction for Linux ELF binaries.

@l./Source/cmBinUtilsLinuxELFGetRuntimeD.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmBinUtilsLinuxELFGetRuntimeD.body: The header declares a helper class that, when constructed with a `cmRuntimeDependencyArchive`, can be queried for the runtime dependencies of a given ELF file. The single pure virtual member `GetFileInfo` expects a file name and fills three vectors—needed libraries, relative‑path resolution tables, and runtime‑search‑path entries—returning success status. The class stores the archive pointer and provides a small `SetError` helper for reporting diagnostic messages.

@l./Source/cmBinUtilsLinuxELFLinker.cxx.author: AI Short Overview

@l./Source/cmBinUtilsLinuxELFLinker.h.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmBinUtilsLinuxELFLinker.h.body: The header defines a Linux‑specific ELF linker helper that integrates with the cmake runtime‑dependency system. It derives from the generic linker interface, implements `Prepare()` to set up any necessary tools, and exposes `ScanDependencies(file,type)` to enumerate and resolve ELF dependencies for a given target type. Internally it keeps a helper for extracting runtime dependency information, a Linux‑specific LD‑config tool, and tracks whether the LD‑config paths have already been fetched. It also offers lower‑level helpers to resolve a single dependency name against a list of search paths and to fetch the appropriate LD‑config paths.

@l./Source/cmBinUtilsLinuxELFObjdumpGetR.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmBinUtilsLinuxELFObjdumpGetR.body: The tool runs the external *objdump* program on a given ELF file, feeding the file path via a “‑p” flag, and parses its output for lines that start with “NEEDED”, “RPATH”, or “RUNPATH”. It extracts the listed strings following those prefixes, splits any colon‑separated lists, and appends them to the corresponding output vectors. If starting *objdump* fails or the process exits non‑zero, the tool records an error and returns false; otherwise it returns true after collecting all dependency names.

@l./Source/cmBinUtilsLinuxELFObjdumpGetR.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmBinUtilsLinuxELFObjdumpGetR.body: The header defines a helper that implements the logic for extracting run‑time dependencies from an ELF file on Linux. It inherits from a generic “get‑runtime‑dependencies” base class, hooks into a `cmRuntimeDependencyArchive`, and overrides `GetFileInfo` to parse the ELF, returning the lists of required files, rpath and runpath strings.

@l./Source/cmBinUtilsMacOSMachOGetRuntim.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmBinUtilsMacOSMachOGetRuntim.body: The file implements a small helper class that wraps a `cmRuntimeDependencyArchive` instance. Its constructor simply stores the archive pointer, and the `SetError` method forwards an error string to the archive’s own error‑handling routine. The rest of the file is dedicated to integration points where this helper is used elsewhere in the project.

@l./Source/cmBinUtilsMacOSMachOGetRuntim.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmBinUtilsMacOSMachOGetRuntim.body: The header declares a small helper class that, given a `cmRuntimeDependencyArchive`, can read a Mach‑O file and populate two vectors—one with the names of dynamic‑link libraries referenced in the file and the other with any runtime‑path entries found in its load‑commands. The class exposes a pure virtual `GetFileInfo` method that concrete subclasses must implement; the base class just stores a pointer to the archive and offers a protected helper to record an error string.

@l./Source/cmBinUtilsMacOSMachOLinker.cx.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmBinUtilsMacOSMachOLinker.cx.body: The file implements a Mach‑O dependency scanner for macOS. It wraps the otool tool to obtain a binary’s library and r‑path lists, caches the results, and resolves each dependency by expanding special “@rpath/”, “@loader_path/”, and “@executable_path/” placeholders into absolute paths. The scanner skips pre‑excluded and post‑excluded paths, tracks unresolved dependencies, and records both resolved and unresolved paths in the associated archive. It uses the cache to avoid repeated otool calls and honours the system library cache for missing dylibs.

@l./Source/cmBinUtilsMacOSMachOLinker.h.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmBinUtilsMacOSMachOLinker.h.body:
cmBinUtilsMacOSMachOLinker implements Mach‑O dependency resolution for Mac OS binaries.  
It extends the generic linker interface, collecting library and r‑path data via an auxiliary GetRuntimeDependencies tool.  
Its helper routines resolve library locations—by loader path, r‑path, or the executable’s own directory—and cache the results in ScannedFileInfo for future reuse.

@l./Source/cmBinUtilsMacOSMachOOToolGetR.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmBinUtilsMacOSMachOOToolGetR.body: The file implements a helper that runs the macOS “otool” utility to discover a binary’s dynamic‑linker dependencies. It builds the command `-l <file>`, spawns the process, and parses the stdout line‑by‑line. Lines beginning with `cmd LC_RPATH` provide a library path and with `cmd LC_LOAD_DYLIB` provide a library name; these are collected into the supplied vectors. The helper reports failure on any process spawn, parsing error, or non‑zero exit status.

@l./Source/cmBinUtilsMacOSMachOOToolGetR.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmBinUtilsMacOSMachOOToolGetR.body:
The header declares a helper tool class that extends the generic runtime‑dependency tool.  
It holds a pointer to a `cmRuntimeDependencyArchive` instance and implements the pure virtual method `GetFileInfo`, which is expected to populate two output vectors: one for library names and one for relative paths. The class is intended to be instantiated by code that needs to resolve a file’s linked libraries at build or install time.

@l./Source/cmBinUtilsWindowsPEDumpbinGet.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmBinUtilsWindowsPEDumpbinGet.body: The implementation spawns the external “dumpbin” utility on a specified PE file, captures its standard‑output, and extracts dependency names via a regular‑expression match; any failure to spawn, wait, or non‑zero exit code results in an error message being recorded and the operation returning false.

@l./Source/cmBinUtilsWindowsPEDumpbinGet.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmBinUtilsWindowsPEDumpbinGet.body: The header declares a concrete implementation of the `cmBinUtilsWindowsPEGetRuntimeDependenciesTool` interface, exposing a constructor that takes a `cmRuntimeDependencyArchive` pointer and an overridden `GetFileInfo` method that fills a `std::vector<std::string>` with the runtime‑dependency data extracted from a Windows PE file.

@l./Source/cmBinUtilsWindowsPEGetRuntime.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmBinUtilsWindowsPEGetRuntime.body: The file implements a small helper that keeps a reference to a `cmRuntimeDependencyArchive` instance and forwards error messages to it. The constructor simply stores the archive pointer, while `SetError` translates a string into the archive’s error‑handling routine. It’s used by other parts of the system to report failure conditions when resolving runtime dependency data.

@l./Source/cmBinUtilsWindowsPEGetRuntime.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmBinUtilsWindowsPEGetRuntime.body:
The header declares a helper class that works with a *cmRuntimeDependencyArchive*.  
It supplies a constructor that stores a pointer to that archive, a virtual destructor, and a pure‑virtual `GetFileInfo()` method that reports whether a given file’s runtime dependencies can be retrieved.  
A protected helper `SetError()` lets derived classes record failure messages.

@l./Source/cmBinUtilsWindowsPELinker.cxx.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmBinUtilsWindowsPELinker.cxx.body: The file implements the Windows‑specific linker for runtime dependency extraction. It chooses between the `dumpbin` and `objdump` tools based on configuration or defaults, then uses those helpers to enumerate needed libraries. For each dependency it walks the search path list (including the current file’s directory, system and Windows directories) to find the file; when a match is found it records the resolved path, optionally recursing into that library unless it is explicitly excluded. This process fills the archive with resolved and unresolved paths for later use.

@l./Source/cmBinUtilsWindowsPELinker.h.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmBinUtilsWindowsPELinker.h.body:
The file implements a Windows‑specific PE‑linker that extends the generic binary‑linker interface. It holds a helper tool for extracting the list of runtime dependencies from a PE file, and provides logic to resolve those names against the dependency archive supplied in the constructor. The key operations are:

* **Prepare()** – performs any one‑time setup required before scanning, such as initializing the helper tool or caching platform specifics.  
* **ScanDependencies(file, type)** – walks the import table of the supplied file, asking the helper tool to enumerate each import. For each name returned it attempts to resolve the import against the archive; if the name cannot be resolved it reports an unresolved dependency.  
* **ResolveDependency(name, origin, path, resolved)** – a helper that maps a dependency name to a concrete file path in the archive and marks whether that resolution succeeded.  

The class sits behind the generic linker to provide the concrete resolution logic needed on Windows systems.

@l./Source/cmBinUtilsWindowsPEObjdumpGet.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmBinUtilsWindowsPEObjdumpGet.body: The file implements a tool that runs the Windows `objdump` utility to harvest the list of DLLs an executable or object file pulls in at load time. It inherits from a generic dependency‑extractor, builds a command line with the `-p` switch, executes the process, parses each line of the output with a regex that matches the “DLL Name:” format, and stores the captured names in the supplied vector. The routine returns success only when the child process exits cleanly and no parse errors occur.

@l./Source/cmBinUtilsWindowsPEObjdumpGet.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmBinUtilsWindowsPEObjdumpGet.body: The header defines a concrete tool that hooks into the existing Windows‑PE dependency framework. It stores a pointer to a cmRuntimeDependencyArchive, and supplies an implementation of `GetFileInfo` that uses the objdump utility to enumerate the runtime libraries required by a PE file.

@l./Source/cmBlockCommand.cxx.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmBlockCommand.cxx.body:
The file implements the “block/​endblock” command for a custom make‑file system.  
A helper class, `BlockScopePushPop`, keeps scoped variables and policies on a stack by holding unique‑pointer pushers that automatically pop when destroyed.  
`cmBlockFunctionBlocker` derives from `cmFunctionBlocker` and defines the two command names. It accepts a set of scopes and a list of variable names; during execution it iterates through captured functions, propagating return flags such as break/continue/return and finally re‑raises any scope changes that occurred.  
The free function `cmBlockCommand` parses a list of string arguments, builds a scope set (defaulting to both variables and policies if none specified), optionally accepts a propagation list, and then creates and registers a `cmBlockFunctionBlocker` instance to enforce the requested scope changes while executing the block’s body.

@l./Source/cmBlockCommand.h.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmBlockCommand.h.body: The header declares a single API for parsing `block()`‑style commands: a function `cmBlockCommand` that consumes a vector of argument strings, updates a `cmExecutionStatus` object, and returns a success flag. It’s the only public entry point in this module.

@l./Source/cmBreakCommand.cxx.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmBreakCommand.cxx.body: The file implements the logic for the BREAK command in the makefile system: it validates that a BREAK is used only within a loop block, consults the policy engine to decide whether the usage is a warning, fatal error, or ignored, emits the corresponding message, and records that a break has been invoked.

@l./Source/cmBreakCommand.h.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmBreakCommand.h.body: The header declares a single helper that performs a break‑out from a surrounding `foreach` or `while` loop. It exposes a `bool cmBreakCommand(const std::vector<std::string>& args, cmExecutionStatus& status)` routine that consumes a list of arguments (typically parsed from a command line) and a status object, returning `true` when the break succeeds and `false` otherwise.

@l./Source/cmBuildCommand.cxx.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmBuildCommand.cxx.body: The file implements the **cmBuildCommand** command used by CMake to generate a shell‑level build command. It parses command‑line arguments, supports both the new multi‑parameter interface and the legacy two‑argument form, determines the target, configuration, and parallelization flag, and then asks the global generator to produce the actual `make` command string. Finally, it writes that string into the makefile as a cache definition under the supplied variable name, while issuing warnings if unused options are supplied.

@l./Source/cmBuildCommand.h.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmBuildCommand.h.body: The header defines a single public entry point for executing a build command. It supplies a function that accepts a list of string arguments, returns a Boolean indicating success, and updates a status object that reports execution results. The file pulls in the common types needed for that interface and pulls in a shared configuration header. This API is exercised throughout the codebase wherever a command needs to be run.

@l./Source/cmBuildNameCommand.cxx.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmBuildNameCommand.cxx.body: The function first checks that an argument list is supplied; it then looks up a cached name for the first argument. If the cached entry contains characters that would be problematic in a makefile definition, those characters are replaced with underscores. When no cached value is present, the routine constructs a default name starting with “WinNT” (replaced by the output of `uname` when the system is identified as Unix), appends the compiler name (after expanding any CMake variables in that string), and finally sanitises the result string by removing slashes and parentheses. The cleaned string is stored back into the makefile’s cache under the given key. This helper is called from other build‑generation routines to supply a consistent build identifier.

@l./Source/cmBuildOptions.h.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmBuildOptions.h.body:
The header declares an enumeration `PackageResolveMode` with four values that control whether package resolution is performed automatically, forced, performed without actual building, or skipped entirely.  
It also defines a plain‑data struct `cmBuildOptions` that holds three options: a `Clean` flag, a `Fast` flag, and a `ResolveMode` member of type `PackageResolveMode`. The struct provides default and copy constructors and a default assignment operator.

@l./Source/cmCLocaleEnvironmentScope.cxx.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmCLocaleEnvironmentScope.cxx.body: The constructor of `cmCLocaleEnvironmentScope` records the current values of the `LANGUAGE`, `LC_MESSAGES`, and `LC_CTYPE` (if present) environment variables, then sets them to the values required by the component. When `SetEnv` is called, the previous value is stored in `EnvironmentBackup`. If an empty string is passed, the variable is removed; otherwise the new value is written using `cmSystemTools`. Finally, the destructor iterates over the backup map and restores every previously‑captured variable to its original value.

@l./Source/cmCLocaleEnvironmentScope.h.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmCLocaleEnvironmentScope.h.body:
The header defines a helper class that scopes changes to process‑wide environment variables.  
When an object is created, the constructor captures current values of the keys it may modify and stores them in `EnvironmentBackup`.  
Destruction restores every captured key to its original value, ensuring the environment is left untouched after the scope ends.  
The class exposes two private helpers, `GetEnv` and `SetEnv`, used internally to read and write the variables it manages. No copy/assignment is allowed to avoid accidental duplication of the internal state.

@l./Source/cmCMakeHostSystemInformationC.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmCMakeHostSystemInformationC.body: This file implements the `cmCMakeHostSystemInformationCommand`, a CMake command that gathers host system data and reports it back to the build system. It queries CPU features, memory totals, OS strings and vendor‐specific identifiers (e.g. whether a CPU supports SSE or MMX) via `cmsys::SystemInformation`. The command can be invoked either directly (`RESULT variable QUERY …`) or through the special `WINDOWS_REGISTRY` syntax, which lets callers read values from the Windows registry (with optional value names, sub‑keys, separators, and an error‑report variable).
