The routine `PrintColumn` performs the actual word‑wrapping, taking into account indentation, line width, and sentence boundaries. `PrintSection` writes a section header and iterates over entries, printing each with an optional custom prefix and aligning under a fixed‑width title. The helper functions `skipSpaces` and `skipToSpace` scan over whitespace to locate word boundaries. The class expects a target `std::ostream` and the text to format.

@l./Source/cmDocumentationFormatter.h.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmDocumentationFormatter.h.body:
The header declares a helper class that writes documentation out to a stream in plain‑text form.  
Its public interface lets a caller set an indentation amount, then call **PrintFormatted** or **PrintSection** to emit a string or a whole section to a stream.  
Internally the formatter splits the text into lines of at most **TextWidth** characters, using the private helpers (**PrintPreformatted**, **PrintParagraph**, **PrintColumn**) to output the content respecting the current indentation level. This file supplies the plumbing needed by the rest of the project to turn comment strings into nicely‑wrapped plain‑text documentation.

@l./Source/cmDocumentationSection.h.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmDocumentationSection.h.body: The header implements a thin wrapper over a `std::vector<cmDocumentationEntry>` that represents a single documentation section. It tracks a name and exposes helpers to test emptiness, clear, and retrieve the entries vector; it also offers `Append` overloads for a single entry or any iterable of entries, and a `Prepend` overload to insert at the front. The class is used by downstream modules to assemble man‑page or HTML‑style output.

@l./Source/cmDuration.cxx.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmDuration.cxx.body: The file defines a template helper `cmDurationTo<T>` that maps a `cmDuration` value into a numeric count by first clamping the value to the bounds of the target type (`std::chrono::duration<T>::max()`/`min()`), then using `std::chrono::duration_cast` to produce a plain count value. Specializations for `int` and `unsigned int` are provided at the bottom for convenience.

@l./Source/cmDuration.h.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmDuration.h.body: The header defines a generic helper that converts a `std::chrono::duration<double, std::ratio<1>>` to any numeric type by clamping the underlying double value to the target type’s representable range. It declares a forward‐declared template function `cmDurationTo<T>` and supplies explicit extern template instantiations for `int` and `unsigned int`. The file relies on `#ifndef CMDURATION_CPP` to avoid redefinition of these instantiations in other translation units. The primary goal is to provide a safe, type‑agnostic cast that avoids overflow or underflow when the source value cannot be represented exactly in the destination type.

@l./Source/cmDynamicLoader.cxx.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmDynamicLoader.cxx.body:
This module maintains a global, in‑memory cache of dynamically‑loaded libraries.  
When a module is requested, the loader first checks the cache; if the handle is already stored it is returned immediately.  
If the library isn’t exist in the map, `OpenLibrary` loads it, inserts the handle into the map, and the new entry survives until `FlushCache()` purges the whole cache or a specific path is evicted.  
The design keeps the library handles in a single `std::map<std::string, Handle>` owned by a thread‑unsafe singleton (`cmDynamicLoaderCache`).

@l./Source/cmDynamicLoader.h.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmDynamicLoader.h.body: cmDynamicLoader.h declares a helper class that exposes two static utilities: OpenLibrary returns a handle that lets callers resolve symbols in a shared‑object, and FlushCache clears any internal caching performed by the underlying loader. It pulls in the platform‑specific loader via an IWYU‑style include of cmsys::DynamicLoader and relies on that implementation for all of its work. The class itself is trivially constructible and disposable, giving no instance state beyond its static methods.

@l./Source/cmDyndepCollation.cxx.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmDyndepCollation.cxx.body: The file implements the logic for collecting and serialising the dependency metadata of C++ modules that are compiled by the CMake system. It walks through the file‑sets attached to a target, extracts the source files, classifies them as either “object and BMI” or “BMI‑only”, and produces a JSON description that is later consumed by the export builder. The code also handles the installation of B‑module files (BMI) and generates scripts that emit CMake property commands for each module, with proper handling of visibility, permissions, and destination paths. The helper functions at the end of the file provide quick queries for whether a module file is private or BMI‑only, simplifying checks in other parts of the system.

@l./Source/cmDyndepCollation.h.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmDyndepCollation.h.body: cmDyndepCollation.h declares a set of helper structures and static utilities for handling runtime‑generated dependency metadata. The main class, `cmDyndepCollation`, exposes functions that inject dependency data into a JSON value, parse export‑information objects, write language‑specific metadata files, and perform checks on module export rules. Callback objects (`cmDyndepGeneratorCallbacks` and `cmDyndepMetadataCallbacks`) provide hooks for deriving file paths and optional module names during the generation process.

@l./Source/cmELF.cxx.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmELF.cxx.body: The source implements a lightweight ELF file reader that reads the primary header, parses the section headers, and extracts the dynamic‐linker section entries.  It supports both 32‑bit and 64‑bit ELF formats via template specializations, handles byte‑order swapping automatically, and exposes helpers to fetch the SONAME/RPATH/RUNPATH strings and to serialize a list of dynamic entries back to a byte stream.

@l./Source/cmELF.h.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmELF.h.body: The header defines a C++ class `cmELF` that wraps parsing of ELF files. Its public interface lets callers query a file’s type, target machine, section count, and retrieve dynamic‑section entries. It exposes string‑table entries (value, position, size, referenced section index) and helpers to encode those entries for the appropriate ELF format. Internally it owns a unique‑pointer to `cmELFInternal` and holds an error string for parsing failures.

@l./Source/cmEnableLanguageCommand.cxx.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmEnableLanguageCommand.cxx.body: The `cmEnableLanguageCommand` function parses a vector of string arguments, treats the token `"OPTIONAL"` as a flag marking the operation as optional, collects the remaining tokens as language identifiers, and finally invokes `Makefile::EnableLanguage` on the collected list while updating the execution status. It returns `true` on successful invocation and sets an error in `status` when no arguments are supplied.

@l./Source/cmEnableLanguageCommand.h.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmEnableLanguageCommand.h.body: This header declares a helper that takes a list of command‑line arguments (as a `std::vector<std::string>`) and a reference to a `cmExecutionStatus`. It parses those arguments, configures the requested language/command via the underlying `cmConfigure` machinery, and returns `true` when the command is enabled successfully, otherwise `false`.

@l./Source/cmEnableTestingCommand.cxx.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmEnableTestingCommand.cxx.body: The file defines a helper that, when invoked, registers the `CMAKE_TESTING_ENABLED` flag in the running makefile by calling `status.GetMakefile().AddDefinition(...)`, thereby signalling that test‑mode is active across the rest of the build system.

@l./Source/cmEnableTestingCommand.h.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmEnableTestingCommand.h.body: The header declares a helper routine that scans a source CMakeLists.txt, expands CMake variables, and emits a “CMakeTestfile” containing only the subdirs() and add_test() invocations that belong to active IF‑blocks. It returns a success flag through the supplied cmExecutionStatus object. This routine is invoked by the build system to wire up a test harness that CTest consumes from the top‑level build directory.

@l./Source/cmEvaluatedTargetProperty.cxx.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmEvaluatedTargetProperty.cxx.body:
The file implements the logic that the build system uses to walk through a target’s property entries, turning them into concrete “evaluated” items that the rest of the generator can consume.  It takes each `TargetPropertyEntry` that already knows its own back‑trace and links, runs the linked item through the current generator’s evaluation routine, then captures the resulting values in an `EvaluatedTargetPropertyEntry` structure. When a property depends on the build context it marks the entry as context‑dependent.  

The two helper routines `EvaluateTargetPropertyEntry` and `EvaluateTargetPropertyEntries` create those entries for a single target or a batch of them.  

The `addInterfaceEntry` routine is responsible for pulling in libraries that implement the requested interface. It constructs a temporary context for the library’s own evaluation and expands its interface property list, storing the result in a temporary entry before pushing it onto the output list. The public `AddInterfaceEntries` routine drives this process for the runtime‑specific and normal library sets and ensures the final entry list reflects whether any of the added entries were context sensitive.

@l./Source/cmEvaluatedTargetProperty.h.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmEvaluatedTargetProperty.h.body: The header defines a lightweight data holder for an evaluated target‑property entry—containing a link item, a back‑trace, a list of value strings and a flag for context‑dependence—plus a pair of functions that compute such entries (individually or in bulk) and a helper that records when a language‑runtime interface should be pulled in.

@l./Source/cmExecProgramCommand.cxx.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmExecProgramCommand.cxx.body: The file implements the `cmExecProgramCommand` helper: it parses a vector of arguments, builds a shell‑style command string, runs that command in a child process (via the internal `cmsysProcess` interface), captures stdout/stderr according to a chosen encoding, and records the exit code and any output in the surrounding `cmExecutionStatus` (adding makefile definitions if requested). It handles platform quirks (quotes on Windows, optional working‑directory change, and output hiding).

@l./Source/cmExecProgramCommand.h.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmExecProgramCommand.h.body: `cmExecProgramCommand` is a helper that registers a new build target using a list of arguments and reports the execution status. It takes a vector of strings and a reference to a status object, returning a Boolean that indicates whether the target was successfully added. The routine is designed for programmatic use of the build system (e.g., adding install or clean targets).

@l./Source/cmExecuteProcessCommand.cxx.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmExecuteProcessCommand.cxx.body: The file implements a C++ helper that runs a sequence of external commands while routing their standard‑output/error streams through supplied files or makefile variables. It parses a custom argument format (e.g. `COMMAND`, `OUTPUT_VARIABLE`, `ERROR_VARIABLE`, `TIMEOUT`) and supports optional features such as quiet output, trailing‑whitespace stripping, and timeout handling. After execution it records exit codes and any exceptions for each child process, exposing them back to the caller via the supplied `cmExecutionStatus` object.

@l./Source/cmExecuteProcessCommand.h.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmExecuteProcessCommand.h.body: The header exposes a single API call that accepts a list of command‑line tokens and a status object to report whether the invocation succeeded.  It relies on a forward‑declared `cmExecutionStatus` type, pulls in the project’s configuration header, and pulls in `<string>` and `<vector>` from the standard library.  The implementation of the function is elsewhere in the KWSys module that actually spawns the requested process.

@l./Source/cmExecutionStatus.h.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmExecutionStatus.h.body: The header declares a lightweight base class used by all concrete command‑status types. It stores a reference to the owning `cmMakefile`, tracks whether a command returned, broke, or continued, and whether an error occurred, including nested errors. Public methods allow callers to record an error message, clear or set return variables, and query each flag. The implementation keeps the internal state simple—no dynamic allocation beyond a `std::vector` of variable names—and exposes read‑only accessors for the stored data.

@l./Source/cmExpandedCommandArgument.cxx.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmExpandedCommandArgument.cxx.body: The file implements a lightweight helper class that stores a command‑line argument value and a flag indicating whether that value was quoted. It supplies a default constructor and a constructor that accepts a string and a bool. The class offers accessors: GetValue(), WasQuoted(), and empty() to inspect the stored value. It also overloads operator== to compare the stored string against a C‑string or another std::string. The code is intended to be a trivial utility used by other parts of the project.

@l./Source/cmExpandedCommandArgument.h.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmExpandedCommandArgument.h.body:
The header declares a tiny helper that holds a parsed argument string and remembers whether it was surrounded by quotes. A constructor accepts a raw string and a flag for “quoted”, and the class exposes:

* `GetValue()` – returns the stored string.  
* `WasQuoted()` – reports the quoted flag.  
* `operator==` overloads that let you compare an instance against a C‑string or a `std::string`.  
* `empty()` – tells whether the value holds any content.  

The implementation keeps the string in a private `std::string Value` and the flag in a private `bool Quoted`. The class is used wherever a command line is broken into individual arguments that must remember their original quoting state.

@l./Source/cmExperimental.cxx.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmExperimental.cxx.body: The file defines a static table of experimental features and helper routines for querying them. It holds a `LookupTable` that maps each experimental feature to its UUID, variable name, description, and a flag that controls whether a warning is issued. A small helper (`DataForFeature`) retrieves the table entry for a requested feature, while `HasSupportEnabled` examines a `cmMakefile` instance to see whether the feature’s variable matches its expected UUID; on the first positive hit it logs an author‑warning and flips the warning flag.

@l./Source/cmExperimental.h.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmExperimental.h.body: The file defines a small interface for querying experimental build‑time features. It declares a `Feature` enum listing supported experimental flags (`WindowsKernelModeDriver`, `Sentinel`), and a `TryCompileCondition` enum that drives whether a particular build flag forces the compiler to skip certain checks. The `FeatureData` struct bundles a human‑readable name, a unique identifier, a variable name used in CMake scripts, a description, and a list of variables that should be considered “try‑compile” variables. Two static helpers are provided: `DataForFeature(Feature)` returns the corresponding `FeatureData` instance, and `HasSupportEnabled(cmMakefile const&, Feature)` reports whether the given makefile actually enables the given experimental feature. This header is the single point of entry for other parts of the code to discover whether a feature is available and what variable names they map to.

@l./Source/cmExportBuildAndroidMKGenerat.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmExportBuildAndroidMKGenerat.body:
The file implements a class that writes the make‑file snippets used by the Android NDK build system.  
Its main job is to emit the header and footer lines that start and finish a generated `.mk` file, and to produce the target‑specific sections that list source files, pre‑compiled libraries, include directories and link options.  
During this emission it checks the CMP0022 policy and emits warnings when an export would fail under the “OLD” setting.  
Finally it writes the include directives that refer to pre‑built shared/static libraries for the target being exported.

@l./Source/cmExportBuildAndroidMKGenerat.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmExportBuildAndroidMKGenerat.body:
This header declares the **`cmExportBuildAndroidMKGenerator`** class, a concrete exporter that writes a makefile in the Android NDK style.  
- It inherits from `cmExportBuildFileGenerator` and implements the virtual hooks that emit header/footer, target, and property blocks for a generated file.  
- A helper static function, `GenerateInterfaceProperties`, walks a target’s imported properties and writes them in the target‑specific format.  
- The nested `GenerateType` enum distinguishes the two export modes (BUILD vs INSTALL), which the generator uses when deciding what target code it produces.  
- The class is used by the `export()` command to produce a prebuilt‑library compatible Android makefile from the internal build tree.

@l./Source/cmExportBuildFileGenerator.cx.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmExportBuildFileGenerator.cx.body: The file implements the logic for emitting export‑build files that describe how individual targets in a CMake configuration expose their build artifacts to other parts of the build. It keeps track of which targets are exported, collects properties for each exported target (sources, includes, compile options, link options, etc.), and writes the corresponding “import‑” snippets used by downstream commands.  It also supports both standard libraries and C++‑module (CXX_MODULES) interfaces, handling the special case of object libraries that have no explicit object‑file location.  The generator walks the export set hierarchy, resolves missing targets with informative errors, and writes the per‑configuration import files and C++‑module configuration files that other targets consume.

@l./Source/cmExportBuildFileGenerator.h.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmExportBuildFileGenerator.h.body: `cmExportBuildFileGenerator.h` defines a concrete exporter that gathers a list of target names, holds a reference to the current export set, and writes a single‑file manifest containing the configuration for every build configuration. Internally it keeps the export set, the local generator, and a directory path for C++ modules, and implements the virtual methods needed to create the main export file, append import‑target sections, and report missing dependencies.

@l./Source/cmExportCommand.cxx.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmExportCommand.cxx.body: The file implements the command that CMake uses to export targets or a set of targets to a file. It parses the command line, distinguishes “EXPORT”‑style arguments (set name, namespace, output file) from “TARGETS” and “ANDROID_MK” options, and verifies that the requested targets are present in the current project. Depending on whether the export is for an Android makefile or a plain file it creates the corresponding generator object, populates it with the chosen configuration list, and registers the generator with the global generator so the exported file is written out. The helper functions handle the special “PACKAGE” mode, storing the current build directory in a registry or registry‑style file, and perform the appropriate registry handling for Windows and other platforms.

@l./Source/cmExportCommand.h.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmExportCommand.h.body: The header supplies the interface for exporting a command‑line request. It declares a single function that accepts a list of argument strings and a mutable status object, returning a Boolean that indicates whether the export succeeded. The file pulls in the project configuration header and the standard string/vector types, and it’s wrapped in a header guard to prevent multiple inclusion.

@l./Source/cmExportFileGenerator.cxx.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmExportFileGenerator.cxx.body: Handles generation of export files for CMake builds, coordinating the mapping of interface properties, resolving target namespaces, and writing the import headers and footers while taking care of include directories, link libraries, and path prefixes.

@l./Source/cmExportFileGenerator.h.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmExportFileGenerator.h.body: The header implements a base class that orchestrates generating an “export” file used to re‑export selected targets (build‑time or installed) to another project. It lets a caller configure the file name, the target namespace, and the list of configurations that should appear in the export. The class stores the set of targets it actually emits and gathers the detailed properties of each target—source directories, include directories, link libraries, and interface metadata—so that subclasses can materialise the actual import code for a specific export type. Subclasses hook into the virtual slots that emit policy headers, footers, target definitions, and link‑property blocks, while the base class supplies the plumbing to collect and format these properties, resolve references in generator expressions, and write the requisite version checks. The interface of the class therefore exposes simple “Set…”, “AddConfiguration”, “GenerateImportFile” style functions, while the derived classes supply the concrete code generation logic for build‑vs‑install export files.

@l./Source/cmExportInstallAndroidMKGener.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmExportInstallAndroidMKGener.body: The source implements cmExportInstallAndroidMKGenerator, a subclass that emits Android‑style makefile fragments for installing exported targets. It pulls the set of exported targets from the InstallExportGenerator, writes out the necessary import prefix and path information, and generates the import and target entries for each target (skipping interface libraries). The class also takes care of interface properties and cleans up temporary variables while writing the final install script.

@l./Source/cmExportInstallAndroidMKGener.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmExportInstallAndroidMKGener.body: This header introduces a concrete generator for Android NDK installation fragments. The class `cmExportInstallAndroidMKGenerator` derives from `cmExportInstallFileGenerator` and implements the various virtual hooks required to emit a makefile fragment that the NDK build system consumes. It supplies methods that write the import header/footer, target definitions, property mappings, and checks for missing targets. The generator orchestrates the temporary staging of files and cleans up the generated content afterward. The class is used by the `INSTALL(EXPORT_ANDROID_MK)` command to create the appropriate make‑file snippets for an Android build.

@l./Source/cmExportInstallFileGenerator..author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmExportInstallFileGenerator..body: The source file implements the core logic for CMake’s install‑export mechanism. It walks through an export set, writes the import prefix and per‑configuration import files, and emits the target‑specific export entries. The code also handles C++‑module support, missing‑target diagnostics, and writes the auxiliary configuration and module include files needed by the generated export scripts.

@l./Source/cmExportInstallFileGenerator..author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmExportInstallFileGenerator..body: The `cmExportInstallFileGenerator` class extends the generic export‑file generator to create temporary “import” files for install‑exported targets. It records per‑configuration mappings to the import files, C++ module files, and target module files generated during the install phase, and implements the logic to produce the main install script and the per‑config import scripts that load the exported targets after installation.

@l./Source/cmExportLibraryDependenciesCo.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmExportLibraryDependenciesCo.body: The file defines a command that gathers the link‑library dependencies of all library targets in a project and writes them into a file that is later read by CMake. It determines whether to emit new‑style dependency entries based on the CMake version and writes the information in a conditional format.

@l./Source/cmExportSet.cxx.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmExportSet.cxx.body: The file implements a small helper that tracks a named export set. It stores a list of target‑export objects and a list of installation exporters, and exposes methods to add these objects. The central routine, `Compute`, walks through the stored target exports, resolves each target by name, and checks that every file set mentioned in the target’s interface list is actually present in the set’s internal mapping, signalling a fatal error if not. The class also supplies a map-like access operator that lazily creates a new export set entry when a name is first requested.

@l./Source/cmExportSet.h.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmExportSet.h.body:
The header declares a container that groups exported targets.  
* `cmExportSet` stores a name, a list of `cmTargetExport` objects, and a list of installer generators.  
* It offers `AddTargetExport()` and `AddInstallation()` to add entries, and a `Compute()` that processes the contained targets.  
* The mapping type `cmExportSetMap` inherits `std::map` and overloads `operator[]` to return a reference to the set for a given name.  
* The code uses `std::unique_ptr`, `std::vector`, and standard containers, and explicitly deletes copy/move semantics to avoid accidental copies.

@l./Source/cmExportTryCompileFileGenerat.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmExportTryCompileFileGenerat.body: The file implements the logic for generating export‑target definitions used by CMake’s exported make‑files. It walks the graph of targets, parses each target’s generator expressions to discover and register all dependencies, then emits the appropriate CMake statements for those targets. For each target it records its properties, evaluates any link‑library lists, and writes the resulting interface information into the output stream, taking care to honour install‑name directories when enabled.

@l./Source/cmExportTryCompileFileGenerat.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmExportTryCompileFileGenerat.body: This header declares a class that implements the export‑generation logic for “try‑compile” targets. It inherits from cmExportFileGenerator, overrides the virtual methods to produce the main export file, populate target properties, and emit configuration files for the specified languages. The class keeps a configuration string, a list of target names, and the set of supported languages, and provides a helper routine to locate targets that match a given property.

@l./Source/cmExprParserHelper.cxx.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmExprParserHelper.cxx.body: This helper implements a small parsing utility for expression evaluation. It holds the current input buffer, tracks line numbers and positions, and reports errors or warnings when parsing fails or encounters unexpected characters. The core workflow feeds the buffer into a lexer (`cmExpr_yylex_init`), runs the generated parser, and translates any failures into human‑readable error messages stored in the helper’s error string. The class also exposes simple getters and setters for the parsing result and error state.

@l./Source/cmExprParserHelper.h.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmExprParserHelper.h.body:
The header defines a helper class for turning a C‑style string into a 64‑bit integer that the parser uses as its token value.  
The class keeps an input buffer, an output buffer, and line counters to feed a scanner.  
It supplies hooks for the lexer (`LexInput`), for reporting syntax problems (`UnexpectedChar`, `Error`, `SetError`), and for storing the final numeric result (`SetResult`, `GetResult`).  
Internal state includes the current buffer position, current line number, and optional warning text.  
The macro definitions expose the helper’s `ParserType` structure as the Yacc/Bison value type and provide an extra pointer (`YY_EXTRA_TYPE`) for the scanner.

@l./Source/cmExternalMakefileProjectGene.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmExternalMakefileProjectGene.body:
The file implements an *external Makefile project generator* class that supplies three main interfaces:

- **`EnableLanguage`** – a placeholder that is currently a no‑op; it is intended to wire language‑specific rules into a `cmMakefile` instance.  
- **`CreateFullGeneratorName`** – combines an extra generator string with a global generator, inserting “ - ” between them; if either argument is empty it returns either the supplied string or an empty string.  
- **`Open`** – a stub that always reports failure (returns `false`), signalling that the generator cannot create a project directly in this implementation.

The code also declares a **factory** (`cmExternalMakefileProjectGeneratorFactory`) that keeps a name, documentation string, and a list of supported global generators. It exposes getters for those fields and an `AddSupportedGlobalGenerator` to append entries.

@l./Source/cmExternalMakefileProjectGene.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmExternalMakefileProjectGene.body: The header declares a base class for generators that create IDE project files for projects that already have makefiles. It exposes virtual methods to enable languages, set a global generator, and retrieve the list of supported global generators, plus a pure virtual Generate() function that concrete subclasses must implement. A factory base class and a template factory helper are also provided to instantiate concrete generator types via `unique_ptr`.

@l./Source/cmExtraCodeBlocksGenerator.cx.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmExtraCodeBlocksGenerator.cx.body:
This source implements the CodeBlocks‑specific export of a CMake project.  
The class `cmExtraCodeBlocksGenerator` walks the internal project model, collects every target type (utility, executable, libraries, etc.), maps compiler identifiers and target kinds to CodeBlocks’s IDs, and emits a CodeBlocks‑compatible XML project file. The helper structures construct a virtual folder tree (the “CMake Files” virtual folder), while a small utility routine creates a dummy placeholder for OBJECT‑library targets so CodeBlocks can resolve them. The generator also takes care of external‑file exclusions controlled by the `CMAKE_CODEBLOCKS_EXCLUDE_EXTERNAL_FILES` flag, and handles different makefile back‑ends (Ninja, MinGW, etc.) for the final build command strings.

@l./Source/cmExtraCodeBlocksGenerator.h.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmExtraCodeBlocksGenerator.h.body:
The header implements a generator for Makefile‑based projects.  
It derives from `cmExternalMakefileProjectGenerator` and implements the required `Generate()` override.  
The implementation supplies helpers that:  
* collect targets of a local generator into `CbpUnit` vectors,  
* create or extend project files via `CreateProjectFile` and `CreateNewProjectFile`,  
* generate placeholder target files with `CreateDummyTargetFile`,  
* lookup the compiler ID for a `cmMakefile` (`GetCBCompilerId`) and classify the target type (`GetCBTargetType`),  
* assemble a make command string (`BuildMakeCommand`),  
* and finally write target information into XML using `AppendTarget`.  
These routines coordinate the creation of the Makefile code blocks that are required for downstream build tools.

@l./Source/cmExtraCodeLiteGenerator.cxx.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmExtraCodeLiteGenerator.cxx.body: This implementation supplies a generator that scans a CMake workspace and emits a CodeLite‑compatible workspace definition. For every target it gathers source files, pairs them with any matching headers, and writes a structured XML representation that describes project layout, compiler options, and custom build commands. The code is organized into helper functions that split source files into implementation and non‑source categories, build virtual directory trees, and output the final project descriptors needed by CodeLite projects.

@l./Source/cmExtraCodeLiteGenerator.h.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmExtraCodeLiteGenerator.h.body: This header implements a specialized project‑generation helper that inherits from the common external‑makefile generator. It holds configuration data such as a name, workspace path, and default CPU count. Core responsibilities include computing the compiler and configuration names for a particular makefile, assembling the correct build/clean/rebuild commands for a target, and collating source files into a compact list. It also walks through source files to discover matching header files and emits XML entries that describe source and header locations. Finally, it offers public entry points for creating the new project files—either from a list of local generators or a single target—by writing the appropriate folder and file structures into the output XML.

@l./Source/cmExtraEclipseCDT4Generator.c.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmExtraEclipseCDT4Generator.c.body: The file implements a CMake‑to‑Eclipse CDT 4 project generator. It examines the CMake project configuration, determines the desired build type, target platform, and compiler toolchain (MSVC, Intel, GCC, etc.), and then writes the requisite Eclipse metadata files (.project, .cproject, .settings). It also configures the appropriate error‑parser for the chosen compiler, ensuring that build‑output errors are correctly interpreted by Eclipse.

@l./Source/cmExtraEclipseCDT4Generator.h.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmExtraEclipseCDT4Generator.h.body: The header declares a concrete generator for Eclipse CDT 4 that writes a project file, a settings‑pref file and a C‑project file for a Makefile‑based project. It supplies helpers to emit resource links (virtual folders, target files or folders), include directories, scanner profiles and build‑environment variables. The class keeps track flags for C/C++ support, virtual‑folder and error‑parser handling and stores the generated source‑project and linked‑resource lists used during file creation.

@l./Source/cmExtraKateGenerator.cxx.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmExtraKateGenerator.cxx.body: The `cmExtraKateGenerator` class implements a CMake generator that emits a lightweight `.kateproject` file describing the build. It determines the project name from the project name, build type, and binary directory, and writes a JSON list of source files plus a set of target definitions that include global, utility, executable, and library targets. The generator differentiates between Ninja‑based and Makefile‑based back‑ends, adding specialized “quick” rules for legacy Kate versions. It produces a dummy project file containing only a comment header for easy identification.

@l./Source/cmExtraKateGenerator.h.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmExtraKateGenerator.h.body:
The header declares a concrete implementation of the external‑makefile generator that emits *Kate* project files for Makefile‑ or Ninja‑based builds.  
Key responsibilities are:  

* `Generate()` – implements the virtual routine to emit the project file, delegating to helper methods.  
* `CreateKateProjectFile()` and `CreateDummyKateProjectFile()` – construct the full project file or a minimal placeholder respectively.  
* `WriteTargets()` and `AppendTarget()` – iterate the generator’s target list and serialize each target, its configs, and the build command into the output stream.  
* Helper utilities (`GenerateFilesString()`, `GetPathBasename()`, `GenerateProjectName()`) build file strings and normalize paths.  

A `ProjectName` string and a `UseNinja` flag drive whether the output targets the Ninja or Makefile format. The class is instantiated through a factory (`GetFactory()`), returning a singleton factory pointer that registers this generator for the “Kate” tool.

@l./Source/cmExtraSublimeTextGenerator.c.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmExtraSublimeTextGenerator.c.body: The file implements a CMake generator that emits Sublime Text 2 project files. It collects global settings, parses source‑file flags and defines, and writes a JSON‑style “.sublime‑project” file that lists targets, build commands, and include/define information for each project. The generator supports a handful of build systems (MinGW, NMake, Ninja, Unix Makefiles) and builds the appropriate make‑file command strings for each target.

@l./Source/cmExtraSublimeTextGenerator.h.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmExtraSublimeTextGenerator.h.body:
A `cmExtraSublimeTextGenerator` class is a concrete implementation of an external‑makefile project generator.  
It supplies a *factory* via `GetFactory()` and implements the required `Generate()` routine to emit Sublime Text 2 project files for projects that use a Makefile.  
Key helpers include:

* `CreateProjectFile()` / `CreateNewProjectFile()` – construct project files, optionally writing a new file.
* `AppendAllTargets()` – walks all local generators, collecting targets, include dirs, and compiler flags for insertion into the generated file.
* `BuildMakeCommand()` – produces the shell command that drives the make invocation for a given target.
* `AppendTarget()` – writes an individual target entry into the file, flagging whether it’s the first target.
* `ComputeFlagsForObject()`, `ComputeDefines()`, `ComputeIncludes()` – compute per‑language compiler options, macros and include paths, usually pulled from a `LanguageFlagsVarName()` variable.

The class exposes a `bool ExcludeBuildFolder` toggle and a string of environment settings.  
The implementation works through the `cmMakefile` representation, flushing results to a `cmGeneratedFileStream` instance.

@l./Source/cmFLTKWrapUICommand.cxx.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmFLTKWrapUICommand.cxx.body:
The module implements the `cmFLTKWrapUICommand` command used by the CMake build system.  
It parses a target name and a list of source files, then for each source generates a `.cxx` and header file by invoking the external “fluid‑ui” executable.  
The generated sources are registered as dependencies of that target, and a helper `FinalAction` is attached to the generator to verify the target exists and emit a warning if it was missing.

@l./Source/cmFLTKWrapUICommand.h.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmFLTKWrapUICommand.h.body: The header declares a single helper that receives a list of string arguments, executes the corresponding UI command, and records the outcome in a `cmExecutionStatus` object, returning `true` on success (or `false` on failure).

@l./Source/cmFSPermissions.cxx.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmFSPermissions.cxx.body: The file implements a helper that converts a string description of a permission flag into the corresponding bitmask in a `mode_t` value. It recognises the standard textual names for owner, group, and world read/write/execute bits as well‑known macro constants (`mode_owner_read`, … `mode_world_execute`) and the special set‑UID/set‑GID bits. When a string matches one of the supported names it ORs the appropriate flag into the supplied `mode_t` variable; if none of the recognised names match it returns `false` to signal an invalid argument. The routine is used by other modules to build up a full permission mask from a list of string identifiers.

@l./Source/cmFSPermissions.h.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmFSPermissions.h.body: The header declares a series of file‑system permission constants that differ between Windows and POSIX builds; these are exposed under the `cmFSPermissions` namespace. The sole public API is the helper `stringToModeT`, which parses a string representation of permission bits into a `mode_t` value.

@l./Source/cmFileAPI.cxx.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmFileAPI.cxx.body: The implementation implements a CMake‐driven file API that discovers and parses query files in a predefined query directory, constructs JSON representations for each supported object kind (CodeModel, ConfigureLog, Cache, CMakeFiles, Toolchains, InternalTest), writes those representations to temporary files and atomically moves them into a reply directory, and keeps an internal index of the generated objects so that subsequent requests can be answered quickly. The API also exposes a “capabilities” report, allows adding project queries, and tracks which queries have been successfully processed so old reply files can be cleaned up.

@l./Source/cmFileAPI.h.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmFileAPI.h.body:
A minimal interface is provided to manage a file‑based request/response protocol for the **cmake** tool.  
The `cmFileAPI` class reads a query directory tree (looking for a `query.json` file and any object files), builds a JSON reply index and a per‑client reply payload for each requested object kind/version, and writes the reply files while remembering which replies have already been emitted so that duplicate writes are avoided.

@l./Source/cmFileAPICMakeFiles.cxx.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmFileAPICMakeFiles.cxx.body: The file defines a helper class that gathers make‑file metadata into a JSON structure. It records source and build directories, walks the global generator’s local generators to collect every file listed in the makefile’s file list, and annotates each entry with flags indicating whether the file resides in a CMake module, is outside the source tree, or is a generated build artifact. The resulting JSON object has two top‑level fields—`paths` with source/build paths, and `inputs` as an array of file objects carrying the file path and the corresponding flag bits.

@l./Source/cmFileAPICMakeFiles.h.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmFileAPICMakeFiles.h.body: The header declares a single class `cmFileAPI` and an `extern` helper that dumps an instance to a `Json::Value`. It pulls in the project‑wide configuration header and the JSON value type, and the license notice is at the top. The only public API exposed is the `cmFileAPICMakeFilesDump` function, which the rest of the code uses to serialize file‑API data.

@l./Source/cmFileAPICache.cxx.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmFileAPICache.cxx.body:
The source implements a helper that serialises the current file‑cache state into a JSON value.  
A `Cache` object is constructed with a `cmFileAPI` reference and a version stamp; it pulls the global cache state from the `cmState` instance and, on request, emits a JSON object containing an “entries” array. Each entry is a JSON object recording the entry’s name, type (converted to string), value (safe‑exposed), and any attached properties. The public helper function `cmFileAPICacheDump` simply creates this `Cache` instance and returns the serialised JSON.

@l./Source/cmFileAPICache.h.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmFileAPICache.h.body: The header declares the `cmFileAPI` type and supplies a single helper—`cmFileAPICacheDump`— that serializes a `cmFileAPI` instance into a `Json::Value`. It pulls in the needed configuration header and the JSON value type. The helper takes a reference to the API object and a numeric version tag and returns a JSON representation of the cache state, which callers can use for diagnostics or persistence.

@l./Source/cmFileAPICodemodel.cxx.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmFileAPICodemodel.cxx.body: The source file implements a framework for serializing a build‑time description into JSON. It defines a hierarchy of classes that capture targets, directories, source groups and compile groups, and a set of helpers that build compile data structures, merge them, and emit JSON fragments for paths, dependencies, and command fragments. The code focuses on dumping configuration details—paths, includes, defines, and dependencies—into a structured JSON output for downstream consumption.

@l./Source/cmFileAPICodemodel.h.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmFileAPICodemodel.h.body: The header exposes a single helper function that serialises a `cmFileAPI` instance into a `Json::Value`. It pulls in the shared configuration and the JSON value type, then declares `cmFileAPI` and the function `cmFileAPICodemodelDump`. The function takes the object by reference and a `unsigned long` to tag the output with a version identifier. No implementation details are included; the file only supplies the necessary declarations for downstream code.

@l./Source/cmFileAPICommand.cxx.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmFileAPICommand.cxx.body:
Handles the **QUERY** sub‑command for CMake.  
When invoked it parses the keyword‑value lists for API, code‑model, cache, CMake‑files, and toolchains, validates that each version string is a positive integer pair, and that the API version is 1.  
If any list contains an unsupported or malformed version it reports an error; otherwise it returns success.

@l./Source/cmFileAPICommand.h.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmFileAPICommand.h.body: The header declares a single API function that returns a success flag. It pulls in the project‑wide configuration through `cmConfigure.h`, uses the standard string and vector containers, and forwards a `cmExecutionStatus` type that is defined elsewhere. The `cmFileAPICommand` function takes a `std::vector<std::string>` of command‑line arguments and a reference to a `cmExecutionStatus` object that the caller must populate to reflect the result of the operation. In the codebase this function is used by various modules that dispatch file‑based commands, each module passing its own argument vector and receiving status feedback.

@l./Source/cmFileAPIConfigureLog.cxx.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmFileAPIConfigureLog.cxx.body: The file supplies a small helper that, given a `cmFileAPI` instance and a version number, produces a JSON object describing the current configure‑log. It pulls the output directory from the file‑API instance, builds an array of event‑kind names that is tailored to the supplied version (so older versions produce a limited set of names), and packages these into a JSON object with the keys `"path"` and `"eventKindNames"`.

@l./Source/cmFileAPIConfigureLog.h.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmFileAPIConfigureLog.h.body: The header declares the external helper that serialises a `cmFileAPI` instance into a JSON value. It pulls in the project‑wide configuration header, pulls in the standard JSON value type, and exposes a single overload that accepts a reference to a `cmFileAPI` and a version tag. The implementation elsewhere will turn the API’s state into a `Json::Value` that callers can inspect or persist.

@l./Source/cmFileAPIToolchains.cxx.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmFileAPIToolchains.cxx.body: The file implements a small helper that, given a `cmFileAPI` instance and a version number, serializes the current CMake toolchain information into a JSON value. It builds a `Toolchains` object that walks through each enabled language in the current CMake instance, collects both explicit and implicit compiler variables (paths, ids, versions, targets, include and link directories, libraries), and emits them as a JSON array of objects keyed by the variable names. The single exported function `cmFileAPIToolchainsDump` returns this JSON representation.

@l./Source/cmFileAPIToolchains.h.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmFileAPIToolchains.h.body:
The header declares a helper for serialising a `cmFileAPI` instance’s tool‑chain metadata.  
A single API – `cmFileAPIToolchainsDump()` – accepts a `cmFileAPI` reference and a version tag, then returns a `Json::Value` that contains the file’s tool‑chain configuration in JSON form.  The file defines the `cmFileAPI` type and pulls in the JSON value type for the output.

@l./Source/cmFileCommand.cxx.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmFileCommand.cxx.body: The file implements a command‑line tool that performs file‑system operations – reading, writing, appending, copying, deleting, renaming, setting permissions, creating links, and handling archives – all routed through a common argument‑parsing infrastructure. It also hooks in libcurl progress callbacks to report download/upload status and exposes helper classes for progress‑text and guard handling of curl handles.

@l./Source/cmFileCommand.h.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmFileCommand.h.body: The header declares an interface for executing a file command: it declares a `cmFileCommand` function that accepts a vector of strings and a reference to a `cmExecutionStatus` object. The function returns a boolean indicating success, while the status reference is filled with detailed outcome information. The file is guarded by an include guard and pulls in the standard `<string>` and `<vector>` headers, along with a project‑specific configuration header.

@l./Source/cmFileCopier.cxx.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmFileCopier.cxx.body: The code implements a command‑line file installer that parses a list of filenames and destination targets, applies user‑supplied glob or regex matching rules, then copies or recreates files, directories, or symlinks into the target tree. It sets permissions, preserves timestamps, and respects options such as “follow‑symlink‑chain”, “use‑source‑permissions”, and optional overrides for file or directory permissions. The class encapsulates matching logic, permission handling, and the actual file‑system operations for copying, creating directories, and recreating symlinks.

@l./Source/cmFileCopier.h.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmFileCopier.h.body: The header‐style `cmFileCopier` is a helper that copies files or directories into a destination tree while applying optional regex‑based rules that can override file permissions or skip files. It keeps a list of `MatchRule` objects that match file names against regular expressions; matched entries may change the effective permissions or exclude the file from copying. The main entry point is `bool Run(std::vector<std::string> const& args)` which parses command‑line‑style arguments (keywords such as `--perm`, `--pattern`, etc.) and then performs the copy or symlink installation for each source file, calling virtual hooks (`ReportCopy`, `ReportMissing`) that derived classes may override for logging or progress reporting. The class supports installing symlink chains when `FollowSymlinkChain` is set. It also supports using source file permissions or supplied directory/file permissions when `UseGivenPermissionsFile/Dir` are true. The `cmFileCopier` encapsulates the copy logic; derived classes can override `InstallFile`, `InstallDirectory`, or `Install` for custom copy mechanisms while still reusing the parsing and rule‑matching machinery.

@l./Source/cmFileInstaller.cxx.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmFileInstaller.cxx.body: The class implements an installer that copies files or creates symbolic links into a target directory while maintaining a manifest of installed files. It reads installation options from command‑line arguments and environment variables (e.g. `CMAKE_INSTALL_MODE`, `CMAKE_INSTALL_ALWAYS`), supports optional renaming, optional relative links, and can fall back to copying when link creation fails. The installer updates the makefile definitions and reports progress and errors through the `cmExecutionStatus` interface, handling permissions and directory creation automatically.

@l./Source/cmFileInstaller.h.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmFileInstaller.h.body:
`cmFileInstaller` is a concrete installer that extends the generic copier interface.  
It stores the mode and type of installation (copy, rename, etc.), tracks whether the operation is optional or whether user‑visible messages should always appear, and keeps a manifest of all files processed.  
The class offers plumbing for parsing CLI arguments, matching files against user‑specified patterns, and reporting copy status to the caller. It also handles permission defaults and resolves the target type string before performing the actual copy operation.

@l./Source/cmFileLock.cxx.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmFileLock.cxx.body:
The file implements a RAII‑style file‑lock helper that stores a file descriptor and the file name.  
It provides a move constructor and move assignment operator, and a `Lock` method that opens the file and applies a timeout‑aware lock.  
When the object is destroyed the lock is released and the internal result is asserted to be successful.

@l./Source/cmFileLock.h.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmFileLock.h.body:
A `cmFileLock` object keeps a file descriptor (an `int` on POSIX or a `HANDLE` on Windows) and the file name in a `std::string`.  
It offers `Lock`, `Release` and `IsLocked` methods.  
Internally it uses `fcntl` on Unix‑like systems and `LockFileEx`/`UnlockFileEx` on Win32.  
Copy construction is deleted; the class supports move semantics.  
The operation status is conveyed by a `cmFileLockResult` return type.

@l./Source/cmFileLockPool.cxx.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmFileLockPool.cxx.body: The file implements a hierarchical lock‑pool that tracks file locks per‑function, per‑file and a global process scope. It exposes `LockFunctionScope`, `LockFileScope` and `LockProcessScope` to grant a lock only if no higher‑level lock already holds the file; otherwise it returns an error. The pool keeps three separate stacks of scopes (`FunctionScopes`, `FileScopes`, and a single `ProcessScope`) and forwards lock/unlock requests to the current active scope. Upon release, it cascades the unlock request through all scopes, returning the first failure. The implementation uses a simple `ScopePool` container that stores `cmFileLock` objects and queries them via `IsLocked`. The public interface is minimal: `PushFunctionScope/PopFunctionScope`, `PushFileScope/PopFileScope`, and the lock/release helpers.

@l./Source/cmFileLockPool.h.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmFileLockPool.h.body: `cmFileLockPool.h` defines a helper that tracks file‑level locks in a structured, scoped manner. It exposes a public `cmFileLockPool` type with three categories of locking scopes—function, file, and process—each with corresponding `Lock…Scope()` and `Release()` functions. Internally, a `ScopePool` implementation keeps a `std::vector<cmFileLock>` of active locks, offering helpers to lock, release, and detect re‑locking attempts. The interface lets callers nest lock scopes cleanly: `PushFunctionScope()/PopFunctionScope()` and `PushFileScope()/PopFileScope()` manage a stack of scopes, while `Lock…Scope()` performs the actual lock with a timeout mechanism, and `Release()` removes a lock. The design ensures no copy/move operations on the pool or pool pools, preserving lock consistency.

@l./Source/cmFileLockResult.cxx.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmFileLockResult.cxx.body: The file defines a set of static factory functions that construct and return a `cmFileLockResult` object with a specific result type and optional error code – e.g., `MakeOk()` yields an OK result, while `MakeSystem()` captures the current system error. The implementation uses `errno` or the Win32 `GetLastError()` depending on the target platform and supplies a `GetOutputMessage()` routine that maps each result type back to a human‑readable string, pulling system messages on Windows via `FormatMessageA`.

@l./Source/cmFileLockResult.h.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmFileLockResult.h.body:
cmFileLockResult represents the outcome of a file‑locking operation.  
It exposes static factory methods – MakeOk, MakeSystem, MakeTimeout, MakeAlreadyLocked, MakeInternal, and MakeNoFunction – that return corresponding result objects.  
The public interface lets callers query success via IsOk() and obtain a human‑readable message with GetOutputMessage().  
Internally, the enum ErrorType records the reason code (OK, SYSTEM, TIMEOUT, ALREADY_LOCKED, INTERNAL, NO_FUNCTION), and the object holds the error value when relevant.

@l./Source/cmFileLockUnix.cxx.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmFileLockUnix.cxx.body: This source defines a `cmFileLock` class that opens a file, applies an exclusive lock with optional retry‑and‑timeout logic, and releases the lock when finished, reporting success or system errors via a custom result type.

@l./Source/cmFilePathChecksum.cxx.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmFilePathChecksum.cxx.body:
The class computes a deterministic identifier for a file path.  
During construction it records the real absolute paths of the current and project source‑ and binary directories.  
When `get()` is called, it finds the nearest of those recorded parents that encloses the requested file, builds a relative path from that parent, concatenates it with a seed string specific to that parent, hashes the result with SHA‑256, and returns the hash as a Base32 string.  
`getPart()` simply truncates that string to a requested length.

@l./Source/cmFilePathChecksum.h.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmFilePathChecksum.h.body:
The header defines a helper class that, given a file’s path relative to a project’s source or binary tree, produces a deterministic checksum string for that file’s immediate parent directory.  
The class can be configured through a constructor or a separate `setupParentDirs` call, and exposes `get()` and `getPart()` to retrieve the full or truncated checksum.

@l./Source/cmFileSet.cxx.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmFileSet.cxx.body: The file implements a *file‑set* abstraction used by CMake to group source files and directories under a named set. It stores a name, type, and visibility flag, and keeps separate collections of directory and file entries. The class provides facilities to append entries, clear collections, and to compile each entry into a `cmCompiledGeneratorExpression` by parsing it as a generator expression. Once compiled, the set can be evaluated against a particular configuration and generator target to produce a list of concrete file paths, with sanity checks to ensure directories are not nested sub‑directories of each other and that each file resolves to a subpath of one of the base directories. The helper functions translate visibility enums to string names and back again, perform validity checks on names, and expose a static helper for checking whether a file‑set type can be included.

@l./Source/cmFileSet.h.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmFileSet.h.body:
The header defines a helper class that represents a collection of source files and directories destined for a particular build target.  
It lets callers add or clear entries, copy another set’s contents, compile those entries into executable generator expressions, and evaluate the compiled expressions against a local generator to produce final build artifacts.  
Static helpers translate visibility values to names and back, and helper predicates check whether a visibility is meant for the current target or its interface.

@l./Source/cmFileTime.cxx.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmFileTime.cxx.body:
The file implements a `cmFileTime` class that exposes a `Load` method.  
The method reads a file’s last‑modified timestamp using the platform‑specific API in play: on POSIX it calls `stat`, converting the `struct stat` fields into a 64‑bit epoch value; on Windows it calls `GetFileAttributesExW` and packs the 64‑bit FILETIME into the class’s `Time` member. The function returns `true` only when the read succeeds; otherwise it returns `false`.

@l./Source/cmFileTime.h.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmFileTime.h.body:
cmFileTime keeps a 64‑bit timestamp in nanoseconds and offers a Load() function to read a file’s modification time.  
It supplies comparison helpers (Older, Newer, Equal, Differ) and second‑resolution versions (OlderS, NewerS, EqualS, DifferS) to determine whether one time precedes, follows, or matches another.

@l./Source/cmFileTimeCache.cxx.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmFileTimeCache.cxx.body:
The file implements a small in‑memory cache that maps file names to their modification times.  
`Load` first checks the cache, falls back to reading the time from the file system, and stores the result.  
`Remove` simply erases an entry.  
`Compare` and `DifferS` both read the two times (via `Load`) and then perform a time comparison, returning the result.

@l./Source/cmFileTimeCache.h.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmFileTimeCache.h.body:
The header implements a small, read‑only cache that maps file names to timestamps.  
It offers three core helpers: **Load** – look up a file’s time (from the map or, if missing, ask the file system); **Remove** – delete an entry; and two comparison utilities, **Compare** (returning –1, 0, +1) and **DifferS** (returns false only if both files exist and their times differ by less than a second).  
Copy construction and assignment are disabled to keep the cache single‑instance and thread‑safe.

@l./Source/cmFileTimes.cxx.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmFileTimes.cxx.body: cmFileTimes is a thin wrapper around OS‑specific file‑time APIs. It exposes a simple interface to load a file’s timestamps into an internal `Times` object and to apply those timestamps to another file. Internally it uses a small RAII wrapper (`WindowsHandle`) to own the Windows HANDLE and automatically close it in its destructor, and a `Times` struct that holds either a `FILETIME` triple on Windows or a `utimbuf` on POSIX. The `Load` and `Store` methods perform the platform‑specific system calls (`GetFileTime`, `SetFileTime` or `stat`/`utime`) and return a `cmsys::Status` status code. The helper `Copy` simply loads the source file times and writes them to the target file.

@l./Source/cmFileTimes.h.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmFileTimes.h.body:
The header declares a small utility class, `cmFileTimes`, that wraps a unique‑pointer to a private `Times` structure. Its public API consists of:

* a default constructor and a string‑named constructor that immediately calls `Load` – returning `IsValid()` to indicate success;  
* `Load` and `Store` that return a `cmsys::Status` result and touch only when the internal `times` pointer is non‑null.  
* a static `Copy` helper that copies a file’s timestamps to another.  
* On Windows builds, a nested `WindowsHandle` is forward declared under `_WIN32`.  

The file keeps the usual includes (`<memory>`, `<string>`, `cmsys/Status.hxx>`) and pulls in `cmConfigure.h` via the IWYU pragma. The implementation relies on the `Times` helper and the unique‑pointer mechanism for safe resource cleanup.

@l./Source/cmFindBase.cxx.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmFindBase.cxx.body: The file implements a helper class that processes the `find_*` commands in CMake. It parses the command line arguments, sets up the search configuration (search paths, suffixes, caching, validator), performs the search for a named item, validates the result if requested, and stores the final value in the cache or as a normal definition according to the current policy. It also provides debugging hooks that record where a search succeeded or failed.

@l./Source/cmFindBase.h.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmFindBase.h.body:
`cmFindBase.h` defines the shared functionality for all “find” commands.  
The `cmFindBase` class parses arguments, checks that a discovered path satisfies an optional validator, expands search paths, stores results in the cache (and optionally in a user‑defined variable), and exposes helper methods for debugging and state reporting. A small helper class, `cmFindBaseDebugState`, records where a search succeeded or failed, assisting diagnostics.

@l./Source/cmFindCommon.cxx.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmFindCommon.cxx.body: The implementation manages path resolution for CMake find modules. It defines path labels for package roots, CMake, environment, hints, system environments, and guess paths, populates search groups, and configures search ordering. It handles debug flags, root‑search modes, and ignored‑path filtering, while normalising slashes and adding suffixes.

@l./Source/cmFindCommon.h.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmFindCommon.h.body: cmFindCommon is a helper class that other FIND_* command classes inherit from. It keeps track of which search directories are active, builds the actual search list, and applies ignore rules from the environment. It also stores and reports debug‑mode flags that child classes query. The class owns maps of labeled path groups, suffixes, and a registry view that controls whether Windows registry entries are considered.

@l./Source/cmFindFileCommand.cxx.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmFindFileCommand.cxx.body:
The file implements a command that resolves a file name into a full path.  
It declares a `cmFindFileCommand` class inheriting from the generic path‑search base.  
During construction it marks that the file itself should be pulled into the runtime
path (`IncludeFileInPath = true`) and declares the variable type as a simple
file‑path.  
The public helper `cmFindFile` simply invokes the command’s `InitialPass` routine
with the supplied arguments, returning the success flag that indicates whether the
file was located. This module is therefore a thin wrapper over the generic path‑search
logic, adding the semantic meaning that the result is a file path to be used later.

@l./Source/cmFindFileCommand.h.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmFindFileCommand.h.body: The header defines a command class `cmFindFileCommand` that inherits from `cmFindPathCommand`. The constructor takes a reference to a `cmExecutionStatus` object; the class represents a CMake command that searches the system PATH for an executable matching one of the supplied names. A free‑standing function `cmFindFile` performs the search, returning a boolean result and reporting status through the supplied `cmExecutionStatus`. The implementation details are in the corresponding source file.

@l./Source/cmFindLibraryCommand.cxx.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmFindLibraryCommand.cxx.body: The file implements the CMake `find_library` command. It parses the command arguments, decides whether the search is for framework, normal, or framework‑only libraries, and then builds a list of candidate library names. A helper class uses regular‑expression matching against the prefixes/suffixes supplied by the build system to pick the best match, preferring earlier prefixes/suffixes and higher‑version numbers on OpenBSD‑style libraries. The search walks the search paths, applies architecture‑specific suffixes (`lib32`, `lib64`, `libx32`), and records the first acceptable file, optionally emitting debug messages.

@l./Source/cmFindLibraryCommand.h.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmFindLibraryCommand.h.body: The header declares the `cmFindLibraryCommand` class, a helper for CMake that walks through architecture‑specific directories to locate a library file, offering both normal and framework‑style search routines and a free helper function `cmFindLibrary`.

@l./Source/cmFindPackageCommand.cxx.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmFindPackageCommand.cxx.body: The file implements the FindPackage command’s core logic for CMake: it resolves search paths, parses and validates package configuration files, distinguishes between module and config modes, and manages search order and fallback to user‑defined prefixes and system registry.

@l./Source/cmFindPackageCommand.h.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmFindPackageCommand.h.body: `cmFindPackageCommand` implements the logic for the cmake `find_package` command. It parses the arguments passed to the command, loads and merges package configuration files from various registries (user‑, system‑, and build‑based), and resolves the package name, version, and location. The class maintains a map of original variable definitions so it can restore the environment after the search, and it keeps track of supported version ranges and special flags such as quiet mode or required. The static `Sort` helper performs ordering of candidate folders based on the chosen order and direction. The implementation also handles the “module” and “config” search modes, stores the chosen module in the `DeprecatedFindModules` map, and reports back whether the package was found or not.

@l./Source/cmFindPathCommand.cxx.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmFindPathCommand.cxx.body: The file implements a command that scans a set of search paths for header files. It handles both ordinary and framework‑style headers, using a glob‑based search to locate framework directories. It reports the found path or a relative path when the *IncludeFileInPath* flag is set.

@l./Source/cmFindPathCommand.h.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmFindPathCommand.h.body: The header declares a helper class that implements the “find‑path” command used by CMake. It inherits from a generic find base, exposes a constructor that records the global execution status, and implements a public `InitialPass` routine that parses a list of directories and file names to resolve the first matching location. Internally it exposes helper functions that search for headers in either a plain directory or in a framework package, returning the full path when found. A free‑standing function `cmFindPath` is also declared, providing a convenience wrapper around the class logic.

@l./Source/cmFindProgramCommand.cxx.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmFindProgramCommand.cxx.body: The file implements CMake’s `find_program` command, orchestrating searches of executable names across user‑specified paths, handling platform‑specific extensions (Windows .com/.exe, macOS bundles), and policy rules that govern when a file is considered executable (CMP0109). It uses a helper structure to iterate through candidate names and directories, reports matches via a debug interface, and falls back to legacy bundle handling on macOS.

@l./Source/cmFindProgramCommand.h.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmFindProgramCommand.h.body: The header defines a command that, when invoked, scans the system’s executable search path (typically the `PATH` environment variable) for a file matching any of the supplied candidate names. It resolves the full path of the first match it finds and stores that value in a CMake variable, making the executable discoverable for subsequent build logic.

@l./Source/cmForEachCommand.cxx.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmForEachCommand.cxx.body: This source implements the logic for the `foreach` command in cmake. It parses the command’s arguments, supports `IN`‑based syntax, and distinguishes the three possible iteration modes (lists, items, zip‑lists). A dedicated `cmForEachFunctionBlocker` class manages the loop body: it stores the iteration variables, expands lists, tracks variable definitions, and restores the original state after the loop. The implementation uses helper utilities such as `cmMakeRange`, `cmList`, and optional types to handle list expansion, and reports errors via the `cmExecutionStatus` mechanism. The file assembles the blocker into the makefile’s execution pipeline, enabling nested and conditional execution of collected commands.

@l./Source/cmForEachCommand.h.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmForEachCommand.h.body: The header supplies the interface for a helper that processes a list of argument strings in a “foreach‑…endforeach” style construct. It declares a lightweight status object (`cmExecutionStatus`) and a single function, `cmForEachCommand`, which takes a vector of arguments and a status reference, executes the command sequence, and returns a boolean indicating overall success. The implementation (in the corresponding .cpp) fills the status with any relevant execution details, allowing callers in other modules to invoke the command loop without needing to know the underlying plumbing.

@l./Source/cmFortranParser.h.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmFortranParser.h.body: The header declares a thin C++ interface for a Fortran‑style parser. It defines a forward‑declared parser object type, a stack of files for handling nested includes, and a set of helper functions to push/pop files and collect string literals. Callback hooks are provided for reporting parsing events such as uses, includes, modules, defines, undefines, and conditional directives, and a small lexer interface is wired in via a custom `YYSCAN` setup.

@l./Source/cmFortranParserImpl.cxx.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmFortranParserImpl.cxx.body: Handles Fortran source preprocessing by managing a file‑stack and a custom buffer system, tracks macro definitions, and tracks preprocessor branches. It parses include directives, tracks required modules, and records the set of included files. It maintains the state of conditional directives and updates the include path stack as needed.

@l./Source/cmFunctionBlocker.cxx.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmFunctionBlocker.cxx.body: The source implements the runtime logic that detects and validates “logical block” delimiters in a list‑file. As each opening and closing command is parsed it increments or decrements a depth counter; when a closing command reduces depth to zero it performs a sanity‑check on the arguments supplied at the opening and closing lines, emits warnings on mismatches, and finally re‑plays the collected function fragments so that the block’s body is executed.

@l./Source/cmFunctionBlocker.h.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmFunctionBlocker.h.body:
The header defines a helper type used in the CMake tool‑chain to decide whether a particular “function” in a CMake file should be suppressed during execution.  
It declares the `cmFunctionBlocker` class, which exposes a public `IsFunctionBlocked` routine that, given a `cmListFileFunction` instance and an execution status object, returns whether the function should be skipped. The class also lets a caller supply the context in which the blocker operates (`SetStartingContext`/`GetStartingContext`). Internally the class relies on a handful of virtual hooks (`StartCommandName`, `EndCommandName`, `EndCommandSupportsArguments`, `ArgumentsMatch`, `Replay`) that derived classes override to customize the blocking logic. The header stores the starting context, a list of functions to block, and a scope depth counter. This brief layout gives the essential outline of the helper’s role in the build‑system framework.

@l./Source/cmFunctionCommand.cxx.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmFunctionCommand.cxx.body: The file implements the CMake system’s “function” command. It defines a helper class that, when invoked, expands the supplied arguments, records synthetic variables (ARGC, ARGV0‑…, ARGN, ARGV), records the function’s formal parameters, and then executes every function gathered in the current block, propagating return and error status. A separate blocker class exposes the command’s start/end names, checks argument compatibility, and, via its Replay method, records the collected functions into the runtime state by adding a script‑registered command.

@l./Source/cmFunctionCommand.h.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmFunctionCommand.h.body: `cmFunctionCommand.h` declares the `cmFunctionCommand` function that takes a vector of argument strings and a `cmExecutionStatus` reference, performs the corresponding function‑level command, and returns a boolean indicating success. The header pulls in the necessary configuration and standard string/vector utilities, and is used by various parts of the code to trigger function‑specific execution blocks.

@l./Source/cmGccDepfileLexerHelper.cxx.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmGccDepfileLexerHelper.cxx.body: The helper reads a GCC‑style dependency file, tokenizes it with a generated lexer, and builds an in‑memory vector of `cmGccStyleDependency` objects. It keeps a simple state machine (`Rule`, `Dependency`, `Failed`) to decide whether a new token belongs to a rule list or a dependency list, and pushes the parsed strings into the corresponding vector. After parsing, it normalizes Windows paths (removing backslashes after drive letters) and removes duplicate or empty entries. The result is a clean, sorted list of dependencies that can be queried by the rest of the system.

@l./Source/cmGccDepfileReader.cxx.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmGccDepfileReader.cxx.body: The implementation reads a GCC‑generated dependency file, parses each rule it contains, and normalises the file paths that it records. It prepends a supplied prefix to any relative paths when the caller requests it, collapses redundant path components, and converts all paths to long‑form before returning an optional‐wrapped content object that lists the parsed rules and paths.

@l./Source/cmGccDepfileReader.h.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmGccDepfileReader.h.body:
The header declares a helper that parses a GCC‑generated dependency file.  
The exported routine `cmReadGccDepfile` accepts a file path, an optional prefix string, and a flag indicating whether to prepend the prefix to every relative path in the whole file or only the `deps` section. It returns an `cmGccDepfileContent` wrapped in `cm::optional` to signal success or failure of the parsing operation.

@l./Source/cmGccDepfileReaderTypes.h.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmGccDepfileReaderTypes.h.body:
Defines a lightweight representation used by the rest of the system to describe a single dependency entry.  
A `cmGccStyleDependency` contains two vectors of strings – one for rule identifiers and one for file paths – that together express a rule‑path mapping. The type alias `cmGccDepfileContent` is simply a vector of those structures, which the dep‑file reader populates. This header is pulled in by other modules that iterate over the returned vector to resolve build rules and paths.

@l./Source/cmGeneratedFileStream.cxx.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmGeneratedFileStream.cxx.body: The file implements a temporary‑file stream that writes the supplied data to a unique temporary file. When the stream is closed it optionally compresses the data (to a .gz file) and atomically replaces the destination file only if the data has changed or compression is requested. The stream also supports writing in UTF‑8 with an optional BOM header and handles locale conversion via the codecvt helper.

@l./Source/cmGeneratedFileStream.h.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmGeneratedFileStream.h.body:
`cmGeneratedFileStream.h` implements an atomic file‑write helper.  
It defines a base class that manages a temporary file and renames it atomically on success, and a public wrapper (`cmGeneratedFileStream`) that extends `cmsys::ofstream`.  
The wrapper offers constructors that open a temporary file, optional compression, copy‑if‑different logic, and a `WriteAltEncoding` helper to emit data in a specific encoding.  
Its public interface exposes `Open`, `Close`, `Set*` helpers, and a `WriteAltEncoding` routine for alternate encodings.

@l./Source/cmGeneratorExpression.cxx.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmGeneratorExpression.cxx.body: The file implements a lightweight engine for parsing and evaluating generator expressions used by the build system.
