It tokenises the input, builds evaluators for each expression, and evaluates them in context, handling special syntax such as build/ install and local interfaces while stripping redundant delimiters and adding install‑prefixes where needed.

@l./Source/cmGeneratorExpression.h.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmGeneratorExpression.h.body: This header declares the core API for parsing and evaluating generator‑expressions at generate‑time. It exposes a front‑end that parses raw string expressions, applies context‑dependent preprocessing (e.g. stripping or interface transforms), and then executes them against the current generator configuration, while collecting dependency information (targets seen, property names, and language‑specific conditions). The implementation keeps internal state for recursive evaluation and supports various evaluation modes (build‑system, install, interface), providing a clean interface for the rest of the build system to use.

@l./Source/cmGeneratorExpressionContext..author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmGeneratorExpressionContext..body: The constructor simply stores the supplied parameters into member fields so that later stages of the generator can access the current target, language, and configuration strings, the back‑trace information, and the flags controlling verbosity and evaluation mode. It also records whether the build‑system evaluation path is active.

@l./Source/cmGeneratorExpressionContext..author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmGeneratorExpressionContext..body:
The header file defines a helper structure used during generator‑time expression evaluation.  
`cmGeneratorExpressionContext` bundles all pieces that a property evaluator needs: a back‑trace stack, collections of targets that the expression touches (both source‑sensitive and all targets), bookkeeping of seen properties, and bookkeeping flags that mark whether an error has been observed, whether the evaluation is context‑sensitive, whether the head target is sensitive, and whether the link language is sensitive. It also stores the source generator (`cmLocalGenerator`), configuration string, language name, and the flags that control verbosity (`quiet`) and whether the current target is being evaluated for the build system. The struct’s fields provide the context for the various helper functions that walk targets and propagate property changes across the dependency graph.

@l./Source/cmGeneratorExpressionDAGCheck.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmGeneratorExpressionDAGCheck.body: The file implements a dependency‑graph checker for generator expressions in CMake. It wraps a target‑specific context and tracks the property being checked, building a chain of nested checks that can detect self‑references or cycles. The `Check()` routine walks up the parent chain, returning either `SELF_REFERENCE`, `CYCLIC_REFERENCE`, or `DAG` (no cycle). On failure it reports detailed diagnostics, walking back through the chain to list each step in the loop. The helper macros and property‑specific methods enumerate which properties trigger special handling (e.g. `LINK_LIBRARIES`, `COMPILE_DEFINITIONS`, etc.), while a small template helper (`additionalTest`) allows extensible tests for other properties. The overall design keeps the graph walk and reporting logic tightly coupled, with a simple `Top()` helper to find the root of the current chain.

@l./Source/cmGeneratorExpressionDAGCheck.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmGeneratorExpressionDAGCheck.body:
The header implements a DAG‑check routine for generator expressions.  
It declares a `cmGeneratorExpressionDAGChecker` struct that receives a back‑trace, a target, a property string and a pointer to the expression content. The checker walks the dependency graph, using a `Seen` map to avoid revisiting nodes, and flags whether a transitive‑only pass is in effect.  
It exposes a `Check()` routine that validates self‑, cyclic‑, and duplicate references, and reports problems through `ReportError`.  
A macro system (`CM_FOR_EACH_TRANSITIVE_PROPERTY`) generates a set of “EvaluateXxx” methods for each transitive property (include dirs, compile options, sources, etc.), enabling the checker to query the appropriate properties on demand.

@l./Source/cmGeneratorExpressionEvaluati.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmGeneratorExpressionEvaluati.body: The class implements the logic for evaluating generator expressions that produce configuration‑specific output files. It reads an input file (or literal content), applies a condition expression, and if the condition succeeds, evaluates the main expression for each enabled language and configuration. The resulting content is written to a target file, with careful handling of relative paths, file permissions, and duplicate‑write avoidance. The class also registers the created files with the build system to ensure proper dependency tracking and rule generation.

@l./Source/cmGeneratorExpressionEvaluati.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmGeneratorExpressionEvaluati.body:
The class encapsulates the logic for generating a single output file from a compiled expression.  
Its constructor stores the source file name, target identifier, the expression producing the file, an optional condition expression, and flags for content handling, line‑ending style, file‑mode, and policy status.  

`Generate()` is the entry point for a `cmLocalGenerator`; it parses the supplied configuration string, resolves the actual file names (via `GetInputFileName()` and `GetOutputFileName()`), writes the file with the configured permissions, and records the filename in the `Files` vector.  

`CreateOutputFile()` performs the actual file write, delegating to the helper `Generate()` that handles different language sections and path roles.  

The private utilities `FixRelativePath()` and `GetOutputFileName()` ensure any relative paths are resolved against the generator’s context and that the generated file’s name reflects the target and language settings.

@l./Source/cmGeneratorExpressionEvaluato.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmGeneratorExpressionEvaluato.body: The source implements a `GeneratorExpressionContent` helper that parses the text of a generator expression, walks its child nodes, evaluates each sub‑expression in order, and validates the number and type of parameters expected by the underlying `cmGeneratorExpressionNode`. It collects the string results, reports errors if literals are required or if the parameter count is wrong, and ultimately hands the collected arguments to the node’s `Evaluate()` routine. The code is heavily guarded for boot‑strap mode, tracks profiling entries, and performs error handling via the context object.

@l./Source/cmGeneratorExpressionEvaluato.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmGeneratorExpressionEvaluato.body:
The header declares a polymorphic evaluator hierarchy.  
`cmGeneratorExpressionEvaluator` defines an interface that concrete evaluators expose a `GetType()` flag (Text or Generator) and an `Evaluate()` routine that consumes a context and a DAG‑checker.  

Two concrete evaluators are provided:  
* **TextContent** – a simple wrapper over a raw C‑string that returns its content unchanged.  
* **GeneratorExpressionContent** – a richer node that owns child evaluators (identifier and parameter lists), exposes `SetIdentifier()`/`SetParameters()`, and implements `Evaluate()` to resolve a generator expression at run‑time, producing a string from its children.  

The file relies on `std::unique_ptr` and `std::vector` containers for child ownership, and uses a context object (`cmGeneratorExpressionContext`) to drive the evaluation.  
Overall, the file supplies the plumbing for parsing and evaluating generator expressions in the larger system.

@l./Source/cmGeneratorExpressionLexer.cx.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmGeneratorExpressionLexer.cx.body:
The file implements a simple lexer that walks a raw expression string and splits it into a sequence of `cmGeneratorExpressionToken` objects.  
It keeps a running pointer `c` and a `upto` marker that indicates the start of the current literal run. Whenever it encounters a special character (`$`, `>`, `:`, or `,`) it first flushes the text chunk that precedes that character via the helper `InsertText`, then emits a token representing the corresponding boundary (e.g., `BeginExpression`, `EndExpression`, `ColonSeparator`, `CommaSeparator`).  
The lexer also tracks whether a “begin expression” marker has been seen (`SawBeginExpression`) to know when an `EndExpression` token has closed a previously opened expression.  
The helper `InsertText` simply pushes a `Text` token onto the result vector if the two pointers differ.  
The overall flow is linear: scan the string once, emit tokens for known delimiters, and return the vector of tokens.

@l./Source/cmGeneratorExpressionLexer.h.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmGeneratorExpressionLexer.h.body: The header defines a lightweight lexical analyser for “generator expression” fragments. It introduces a token struct that records a type identifier (via an enum), a C‑style content pointer and the token length. The lexer class exposes a public Tokenize method that consumes a std::string and emits a vector of tokens, and a query accessor that reports whether any generator expression tokens were encountered during tokenisation. Internally it keeps two boolean flags – SawBeginExpression and SawGeneratorExpression – to remember whether the beginning or any generator‑expression marker has been seen. The implementation is intentionally minimal; no elaborate tokenisation states are exposed beyond those flags and the token list.

@l./Source/cmGeneratorExpressionNode.cxx.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmGeneratorExpressionNode.cxx.body:
The file **`cmGeneratorExpressionNode.cxx`** implements the core infrastructure for building and evaluating expression‑based nodes used in the build‑system generator. It defines a suite of node classes (e.g. `cmGeneratorExpressionNode`, `cmGeneratorExpressionNodeList`, `cmGeneratorExpressionNodeIf`, `cmGeneratorExpressionNodePath`, etc.) each representing a distinct expression construct. The file contains:

* helper functions for parsing and normalising expression strings,  
* evaluation hooks that resolve node values at build time,  
* code‑generation routines that emit the appropriate target‑specific syntax, and  
* utility wrappers used by the higher‑level generator to assemble complex expressions.

In short, the file supplies the node types, parsing logic, and code‑generation helpers that together enable the generator to construct and evaluate the script fragments that drive the build process.

@l./Source/cmGeneratorExpressionNode.h.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmGeneratorExpressionNode.h.body:
The header provides a base class for every expression node in the generator.  
It declares a virtual `Evaluate` that subclasses override, a handful of helper flags (e.g., `DynamicParameters`), and a static lookup that resolves a node by its identifier.  
Typical concrete nodes supply the required parameter‑count logic and the parameter evaluation logic.

@l./Source/cmGeneratorExpressionParser.c.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmGeneratorExpressionParser.c.body: The file implements a recursive‑descent parser that walks a sequence of generator‑expression tokens, building an AST of evaluator objects. It keeps track of nesting level, groups consecutive text tokens into single content nodes, and emits parameter lists for nested expressions by recursively parsing sub‑expressions. The parser merges adjacent text fragments that would otherwise be split by commas or colons, ensuring the final evaluator vector contains compact, properly‑nested content representations.

@l./Source/cmGeneratorExpressionParser.h.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmGeneratorExpressionParser.h.body: Defines a parser that consumes a vector of tokens and produces a vector of unique‑pointer evaluators, exposing a `Parse` entry point while keeping internal helpers and a nesting counter private.

@l./Source/cmGeneratorTarget.cxx.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmGeneratorTarget.cxx.body: The file implements the core logic of CMake’s target handling. It defines the `cmGeneratorTarget` class, which stores configuration data for a build target, and provides a suite of helper classes and functions such as `TargetPropertyEntry*`, `cmTargetCollectLinkLanguages`, `cmTargetTraceDependencies`, etc., to manage target properties, collect link languages, and trace dependencies during the build process.

@l./Source/cmGeneratorTarget.h.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmGeneratorTarget.h.body:
`cmGeneratorTarget.h` implements the core “target generator” logic for the build system.  
At its heart is the `cmGeneratorTarget` class, which orchestrates the translation of configuration data into concrete compile‑ and link‑command strings. It keeps a number of internal caches (e.g., `IncludeDirectoriesCache`, `CompileOptionsCache`, `LinkOptionsCache`) to avoid recomputing frequently‑used data and stores per‑source information such as source flags, language settings, and dependency maps.  

The file exposes a rich set of policies (`PolicyMap`, `PolicyWarnedCMP0022`, `PolicyReportedCMP0069`) that drive conditional behaviour; the various `GetPolicyStatus` helpers expose the current status of a specific policy.  
The code also bundles helper structs (`SourceEntry`, `LookupLinkItemScope`, `HeadToLinkImplementationMap`) that streamline the mapping between source files, link roles, and implementation choices.  

In short, the header wires together configuration sources, policy checks, and per‑source compile/link information to produce the final makefile fragments used by the CMake engine.

@l./Source/cmGetCMakePropertyCommand.cxx.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmGetCMakePropertyCommand.cxx.body: The file implements the command that retrieves a requested CMake property value during script execution. It validates that at least two arguments are provided, treats the first argument as the target variable name, and then looks up the requested property in the current makefile. Depending on the second argument it fetches one of the standard property sets – VARIABLES, MACROS, COMPONENTS – or otherwise queries a named global property. The result string is recorded in the makefile’s definition table so that subsequent commands can access it. The routine returns a success flag and reports any errors via the provided `cmExecutionStatus`.

@l./Source/cmGetCMakePropertyCommand.h.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmGetCMakePropertyCommand.h.body: The header declares a helper routine that takes a list of string arguments together with a status object and returns a bool indicating success or failure. It pulls in the configuration header and standard string/vector utilities, and relies on the forward‑declared `cmExecutionStatus` class to report execution details. This routine is called from several other modules to fetch a CMake property command.

@l./Source/cmGetDirectoryPropertyCommand.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmGetDirectoryPropertyCommand.body: The file implements the *cmGetDirectoryPropertyCommand* that accepts a list of arguments, optionally a directory name, and a property name. It resolves the requested directory (defaulting to the current source directory if none is supplied), validates that a property was requested, obtains the property value from that directory’s `cmMakefile`, and writes the value into the current makefile as a definition. It also supports special requests such as “DEFINITION” for a single definition and “DEFINITIONS” for the list of all definitions, handling deprecated policy cases accordingly.

@l./Source/cmGetDirectoryPropertyCommand.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmGetDirectoryPropertyCommand.body: The header declares a helper that parses a list of path strings (`args`) and populates a `cmExecutionStatus` object with information about the target directory. It returns `true` on success and `false` if the directory cannot be accessed or the queried property is absent.

@l./Source/cmGetFilenameComponentCommand.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmGetFilenameComponentCommand.body: The `cmGetFilenameComponentCommand` routine parses a vector of arguments to pull out a requested part of a file name (full path, base name, extension, or a real‑path after expanding registry placeholders and 64‑bit view rules). It first validates the argument count, then checks for an existing cached value before resolving the filename via the registry‑expansion logic. Depending on the third argument it returns the appropriate component (e.g. name, extension, last extension, or absolute path), optionally storing the result back into the makefile’s cache.

@l./Source/cmGetFilenameComponentCommand.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmGetFilenameComponentCommand.body: The header declares a single utility routine that, given a list of string arguments and a status object, extracts a requested part of a file name – path, name, extension, or the name stripped of its extension – and reports success via its Boolean return value.

@l./Source/cmGetPipes.cxx.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmGetPipes.cxx.body: The file defines a helper that creates a pipe and returns two file‑descriptor handles through the supplied array. It uses the platform‑specific API: on Windows it calls the internal `CreatePipe` routine and converts the resulting handles to file descriptors with `_open_osfhandle`; on POSIX it falls back to the standard `pipe` call. In either branch it marks the descriptors as close‑on‑exec and translates any system error into an error code via `uv_translate_sys_error`. On success it leaves the two descriptors open and returns `0`; on failure it cleans up and returns the translated error.

@l./Source/cmGetPipes.h.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmGetPipes.h.body: The header defines a single routine that accepts a pointer to an int array and returns an integer status (or count). It is meant to expose the plumbing that fills that array with file‑descriptor values for the pipes used elsewhere in the system.

@l./Source/cmGetPropertyCommand.cxx.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmGetPropertyCommand.cxx.body: cmGetPropertyCommand.cxx implements the `cmake` command to retrieve property values from the various scopes supported by CMake. It parses a list of arguments, determines the requested scope (global, directory, target, source file, test, variable, cache, or install), and dispatches the request to a dedicated handler for that scope. Each handler queries the appropriate data structure (the global state, the current directory’s generator, a target, a source file, a test, or a cached entry) and stores the value in the output variable, optionally converting it into a “0/1” flag or string as requested. The file also supports brief/brief/full documentation queries and “defined‑only” checks, handling the special cases of alias targets and installed files.

@l./Source/cmGetPropertyCommand.h.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmGetPropertyCommand.h.body: The header declares a helper that parses a list of strings, updates a `cmExecutionStatus` instance and returns success status. It pulls in `cmConfigure.h`, the standard `<string>` and `<vector>` headers, and uses a `#pragma once` guard. The function prototype is the only public interface shown.

@l./Source/cmGetSourceFilePropertyComman.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmGetSourceFilePropertyComman.body: The function parses a command that asks for a property of a source file. It first validates the argument count – three normal arguments or five when an optional “DIRECTORY” or “TARGET_DIRECTORY” flag is supplied. When the flag appears it records the directory name to search in, then either searches the source file’s own scopes or the target directory’s scopes. It converts the file name to an absolute path if necessary, then locates the corresponding source file object in the first Makefile that contains it. If the source file isn’t already present and the requested property is “LOCATION”, it creates the source file. Finally, if the property exists, the value is written into the main Makefile’s definitions; otherwise “NOTFOUND” is defined. The routine returns success status and updates the execution status object accordingly.

@l./Source/cmGetSourceFilePropertyComman.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmGetSourceFilePropertyComman.body:
The header declares a single helper routine used by the build‑system code to retrieve metadata for a source file.  
The routine receives a vector of argument strings (typically parsed from the command line) and a reference to a status object. It returns true on success and false on failure, and reports the outcome through the status object. This interface is invoked by various parts of the system that need to query file properties before further processing.

@l./Source/cmGetTargetPropertyCommand.cx.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmGetTargetPropertyCommand.cx.body: The routine parses three arguments – a variable name, a target name, and a property identifier – verifies they’re supplied, then looks up the target in the current makefile. If the target is an alias it reports the alias status; otherwise it attempts to read the requested property from the target’s computed or explicit property tables. On success it records the value in the makefile’s definitions, otherwise it logs a warning or fatal error depending on the policy setting. The function returns true on any definition written (even if the property is missing, it marks the variable as “‑NOTFOUND”).

@l./Source/cmGetTargetPropertyCommand.h.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmGetTargetPropertyCommand.h.body:
The header declares a single helper function:

```cpp
bool cmGetTargetPropertyCommand(std::vector<std::string> const& args,
                                cmExecutionStatus& status);
```

The function accepts a list of arguments and a status object, and returns a boolean indicating whether the requested property was successfully retrieved. It relies on the `cmConfigure.h` include and standard string/vector utilities. The function is used across the project wherever target‑specific property values need to be queried.

@l./Source/cmGetTestPropertyCommand.cxx.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmGetTestPropertyCommand.cxx.body: The function parses a three‑or‑five‑argument command that specifies a test name, a target variable name, and an optional “DIRECTORY” flag followed by a test‑directory path. It resolves the test from the current makefile, looks up the requested property (the second argument), and if that property exists, it writes a new definition for the target variable in the current makefile. If the property is not found it defines the variable with the literal string “NOTFOUND”. The routine returns a Boolean indicating whether the operation succeeded or failed (e.g., due to bad arguments or missing property).

@l./Source/cmGetTestPropertyCommand.h.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmGetTestPropertyCommand.h.body:
The header declares a single helper function used by the build‑system code.  
`cmGetTestPropertyCommand` takes a list of string arguments (`args`) and a reference to a `cmExecutionStatus` object, and returns a `bool` indicating whether the request succeeded. The function is meant to fetch a property value (typically a test‑property string) that was supplied to the build system and record the outcome in the supplied status object. No implementation details are present in the header; the declaration is only an interface used throughout the project.

@l./Source/cmGhsMultiGpj.cxx.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmGhsMultiGpj.cxx.body: The file implements a simple tag‑lookup for different project‑types. It defines a static array of string tags and exposes two functions: one that maps a `Types` enum value to the corresponding string and another that writes that string to an output stream.

@l./Source/cmGhsMultiGpj.h.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmGhsMultiGpj.h.body: The header supplies a lightweight helper that emits a tag string for the various kinds of GPJ entities (integrity‑application, library, project, program, reference, subproject, custom target). The public static helpers—`WriteGpjTag` and `GetGpjTag`—are invoked throughout the build system to label emitted sections or log entries, ensuring a consistent tag format for downstream processing.

@l./Source/cmGhsMultiTargetGenerator.cxx.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmGhsMultiTargetGenerator.cxx.body: This file implements a CMake generator that emits the “GHS” project files for each build target. It pulls configuration data from the local generator, resolves source‑group mappings, emits target‑specific options (compiler flags, linker flags, include paths, definitions), and generates auxiliary scripts for any custom commands attached to the target. It orchestrates the creation of the main project file and any per‑group subsidiary files, handling both normal and custom targets, and finally writes the build scripts for pre‑/post‑build events.

@l./Source/cmGhsMultiTargetGenerator.h.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmGhsMultiTargetGenerator.h.body:
The header declares a helper that turns a *GeneratorTarget* into a makefile target.  
- **Constructor/Destructor**: store the target and the local‑generator context.  
- **Generate()**: drives the whole generation pass – it pulls data from the global generator, formats compiler flags, writes source listings, emits custom command sections, and finally emits the target‑specific makefile entry.  
- **Flag/define helpers**: helper routines (`WriteCompilerFlags`, `WriteCompilerDefinitions`) pull the language‑specific flag string from the maps and write them into the output.  
- **Custom‑command ordering**: `ComputeCustomCommandOrder()` walks the dependency graph of source files to produce an order for custom commands.  
- **Utility helpers**: `WriteTargetSpecifics`, `WriteIncludes`, `WriteTargetLinkLine()` and the helpers for writing custom‑command lines provide the plumbing that emits the various pieces that the target needs.  
- **State**: keeps maps of flags/defines per language, the real target name, and a tag type.  
- **Integrity check**: `DetermineIfIntegrityApp()` indicates whether this target is an “integrity” application target.

@l./Source/cmGlobVerificationManager.cxx.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmGlobVerificationManager.cxx.body: The file implements the **cmGlobVerificationManager**, which caches glob expressions during a CMake run, writes a verification script (`VerifyGlobs.cmake`) that recreates the globbed list of files and writes a stamp file to flag any mismatch, and provides facilities to add or reset cache entries. It keeps track of recursion depth, whether to list directories, whether to follow symlinks, and relative path handling, emitting the appropriate `file(GLOB…)` command in the generated script. When a new glob is added it checks for existing entries with differing file lists and emits a fatal‑level error if the contents differ. The implementation writes the stamp file after the script and records the file names for subsequent `file(TOUCH_NOCREATE …)` checks.

@l./Source/cmGlobVerificationManager.h.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmGlobVerificationManager.h.body:
The `cmGlobVerificationManager` class manages a cache of glob expressions used during a build.  
When a glob is discovered it records the expression, whether it recurses or lists directories, and the files matched. This information is stored in a map keyed by a `CacheEntryKey` that captures the flags and pattern. The manager can flush the cache (`Reset`) and can generate a CMake verification script (`SaveVerificationScript`) that will be invoked before the project’s makefile runs to confirm that the expected files still exist. The private `Cache` map is accessed only by the `cmState` helper; external code must request verification via the public API.

@l./Source/cmGlobalCommonGenerator.cxx.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmGlobalCommonGenerator.cxx.body: The file implements the `cmGlobalCommonGenerator` class, which is responsible for generating top‑level build rules that apply to all directories in a CMake instance. It collects the directory‑level targets derived from the local generators, honors the “EXCLUDE_FROM_ALL” flag to exclude or propagate exclusions, and builds a data structure (`DirectoryTarget` map) that is later consumed by the makefile writer. The class also supplies logic to determine the correct editor command for the `edit_cache` target (choosing either a GUI or curses helper based on generator type) and a routine for cleaning up stale export‑file artifacts in the Clang tidy export directories.

@l./Source/cmGlobalCommonGenerator.h.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmGlobalCommonGenerator.h.body: The header wires the common infrastructure shared by the makefile‑ and ninja‑based global generators. It exposes a `cmGlobalCommonGenerator` class that tracks directory targets, their exclusions, and helper methods for clang‑tidy export‑fix handling and edit‑cache support. It supplies utilities for computing target mappings, testing exclusion rules, and maintaining the sets of directories and files subject to export‑fixes.

@l./Source/cmGlobalGenerator.cxx.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmGlobalGenerator.cxx.body: The file implements the core global generator logic: it drives creation of global build commands, manages target ordering and dependency resolution, handles language enablement, and writes rule hashes and summary files.

@l./Source/cmGlobalGenerator.h.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmGlobalGenerator.h.body:
The file defines the central *cmGlobalGenerator* class that drives the entire build tree.  
It holds and indexes all directories, targets, and target‑dependency graphs, and drives the creation of per‑directory *cmLocalGenerator* objects.  
The class exposes hooks for language activation, compiler resolution, and link‑line construction while coordinating the build‑file generation through its virtual *Generate* and *Compute* routines, which internally orchestrate the dependency traversal and target‑ordering logic.  
Security‑related checks, such as warning generation for duplicate targets, are mediated via the internal warning‑sets.  
The design is intentionally encapsulated; the public interface focuses on configuration and generation orchestration, while the implementation details—including file‑lock pooling, rule‑hash maintenance, and path resolution—are hidden behind protected helpers.

@l./Source/cmGlobalGeneratorFactory.h.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmGlobalGeneratorFactory.h.body: The header declares an abstract factory type `cmGlobalGeneratorFactory` that exposes virtual functions for creating `cmGlobalGenerator` objects, retrieving documentation entries, and querying generator names and platform support flags. A helper template `cmGlobalGeneratorSimpleFactory<T>` derives from it and implements the factory logic by delegating to static traits on the concrete type `T`. The file contains only interface declarations and a small template implementation; it does not perform any concrete generator creation itself.

@l./Source/cmGlobalGhsMultiGenerator.cxx.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmGlobalGhsMultiGenerator.cxx.body: The file implements the Green Hills Multi GHS CMake generator. It derives from the base global generator class, hooks into the build system to resolve toolsets, writes project files and custom rule/target definitions, and orchestrates the target dependency graph to emit top‑level projects and the special ALL_BUILD target.

@l./Source/cmGlobalGhsMultiGenerator.h.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmGlobalGhsMultiGenerator.h.body:
The `cmGlobalGhsMultiGenerator` class implements the Green Hills MULTI build system as a concrete `cmGlobalGenerator`.  Its constructor receives a `cmake*` instance and stores a reference to it.  The public interface provides the standard generator API: `CreateLocalGenerator` produces a `cmLocalGenerator` tied to a particular `cmMakefile`, while `Generate` is called during a build‑file pass to emit the appropriate GHS‑MULTI directives.  

Key static helpers expose the generator’s identity (`GetActualName`, `GetDocumentation`) and advertise that it supports both toolsets and platforms.  The class defines a custom dependency ordering mechanism: the nested `TargetCompare` functor and `OrderedTargetDependSet` multiset resolve target build order during the `ComputeTargetBuildOrder` phase, ensuring that dependent targets are built in a correct sequence.  

Auxiliary utilities such as `AddCheckTarget`, `AddAllTarget`, and stamping logic (`StampFile`) are used to generate “all” and “check” targets in the generated makefile.  The file also includes helper routines for writing the header disclaimer, top‑level project blocks, macros, and custom rules sections, all of which are emitted by the various `Write…` methods in the implementation.

@l./Source/cmGlobalNinjaGenerator.cxx.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmGlobalNinjaGenerator.cxx.body: The file implements the core logic that turns the project’s internal dependency graph into Ninja‑style build rules. It reads a *cmake* configuration, walks targets, and emits rules for compilation, linking, custom commands, and clean targets. It handles cross‑configuration builds, dynamic dependency lists, and the special “dyndep” files that record source‑to‑output bindings for incremental rebuilds. The heavy lifting is performed in a handful of helper lambdas that format paths, encode literals, and write out‑of‑the‑box metadata. The implementation is organized around a handful of public helpers (e.g. `WriteBuild`, `AddCustomCommandRule`) and a few protected virtual hooks that subclasses can override for language‑specific behavior.

@l./Source/cmGlobalNinjaGenerator.h.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmGlobalNinjaGenerator.h.body: This header defines the Ninja‑based generator that emits a single `build.ninja` (and a rules file) for a project.  The generator inherits from the common generator base and implements the logic for serialising targets, dependencies and outputs into Ninja’s rule syntax.  It supplies helpers for encoding rule names, literals, paths and for writing rule, variable, include, and default‑target sections into the output stream.  It also manages the special Ninja variables `$in` and `$out` and keeps a cache of paths to avoid repeated conversions.  The class contains facilities for handling custom commands, per‑config outputs, and for tracking assumed source dependencies that may be required when output files are not explicitly listed.  The multi‑config variant (`cmGlobalNinjaMultiGenerator`) extends this behaviour to emit a separate Ninja file per configuration, using the common infrastructure defined in this file.

@l./Source/cmGlobalUnixMakefileGenerator.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmGlobalUnixMakefileGenerator.body: The file implements a Unix‑style makefile generator for CMake that produces the main build scripts and all helper rules. It creates directory‑level targets, handles path escaping for both Unix and Windows, records progress for each target, and writes rules for normal, fast, relink and clean builds. The generator also serialises build commands in JSON for later use and emits a help target that lists all available targets.

@l./Source/cmGlobalUnixMakefileGenerator.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmGlobalUnixMakefileGenerator.body:
The header file defines a generator class that produces Unix‑style makefiles for a CMake project.  
The class inherits from a common generator base and implements the interface required by the generator‑factory.  
Key responsibilities:

* **Target creation** – creates a `cmLocalGenerator` for each directory, populating a set of rules that drive the build from that tree’s root.  
* **Dependency handling** – supports both short‑line and compiler‑generated dependency files; provides hooks to emit the appropriate `-o`/`-MD` flags.  
* **Rule generation** – emits top‑level “all”, “clean”, “install”, etc., and a convenient “help” rule for listing available targets.  
* **Progress tracking** – keeps a map of per‑target progress counters used to report build status.  
* **Special‑case hacks** – supplies empty‑dependency or empty‑command stubs for targets that otherwise would produce an empty rule; this satisfies a handful of older make programs that reject rules without commands.  
* **Extensibility** – exposes virtual helpers such as `AllowNotParallel()` and `AllowDeleteOnError()` so that derived generators can alter the behaviour of the underlying make program.  

Overall the file wires together the pieces that turn a CMake project description into a set of Unix makefiles that can be invoked by a normal `make`.

@l./Source/cmGlobalWatcomWMakeGenerator..author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmGlobalWatcomWMakeGenerator..body: The file implements a generator that emits makefiles for the Watcom WMake system. It subclasses the Unix‑style generator, configuring various build flags (e.g., `MakeSilentFlag = "-h"`, `ForceUnixPaths = false` on Windows, `LineContinueDirective = "&\n"`). During construction it sets up the environment to use the Watcom find‑script (`CMakeFindWMake.cmake`) and registers Watcom‑specific definitions (like `CMAKE_GENERATOR_CC = "wcl386"`). The generator overrides language handling to expose WMake‑compatible variables, and it disables parallel build support by emitting a warning when a parallel build level is requested. The rest of the file wires these settings into the common Unix‑make generation logic.

@l./Source/cmGlobalWatcomWMakeGenerator..author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmGlobalWatcomWMakeGenerator..body: The header defines a `cmGlobalWatcomWMakeGenerator` class that derives from the base Unix‑Makefile generator. It supplies the factory hook for creating instances, exposes the generator name (“Watcom WMake”) and documentation entry, and implements a few essential overrides: setting the target system name, enabling language support (optionally), and restricting deletion or parallelism. The core of the class is the `GenerateBuildCommand` routine that assembles the actual make invocation string and the `PrintBuildCommandAdvice` helper that writes concise usage tips.

@l./Source/cmGraphAdjacencyList.h.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmGraphAdjacencyList.h.body:
The header implements a lightweight adjacency‑list graph representation.  
A `cmGraphEdge` holds the destination vertex, two flags (one for “strong”, one for “cross”), and a `cmListFileBacktrace` that records the origin of the edge.  
`cmGraphEdgeList` derives from `std::vector<cmGraphEdge>`, and the graph itself is a `std::vector<cmGraphEdgeList>`. The file’s purpose is to provide a compact, flag‑aware adjacency list for use in the rest of the project.

@l./Source/cmGraphVizWriter.cxx.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmGraphVizWriter.cxx.body: The file implements a visitor that walks a build‑dependency graph and emits a GraphViz‑compatible dot file. It assigns a unique node name to each target, chooses a shape according to the target type (executable, static/shared/module/… libraries, utilities, unknown), and writes connections with an edge style that depends on the dependency type (public, interface, private). The class supports per‑target subgraphs and a global legend cluster, and it lets the user filter out certain targets via regexes or by target type flags. The logic is split into header/legend/footer writing and a two‑phase traversal that first writes the global graph and then, if requested, writes per‑target connections.

@l./Source/cmGraphVizWriter.h.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmGraphVizWriter.h.body: The class in this header implements a visitor that walks the dependency graph and writes out GraphViz‑compatible (.dot) files. It collects the source‑target pairs (direct and indirect links), groups them per target, and produces one or many output files depending on the flags. The writer uses a small helper struct for each edge, tracks node names in a map, and offers filtering hooks to exclude certain targets or target types (e.g. executables, static, shared, module, interface, etc.). It also writes a small legend section and handles escaping of names so that the dot output remains syntactically correct.

@l./Source/cmHexFileConverter.cxx.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmHexFileConverter.cxx.body: The file implements a lightweight utility that reads Intel‑HEX or Motorola SREC formatted files, parses the data bytes from each line, and writes the extracted binary payloads to an output file. It exposes a single public routine (`TryConvert`) which first probes the input file to decide the record type, then streams the file line‑by‑line converting the encoded hex characters into raw bytes using helper routines (`ConvertIntelHexLine` / `ConvertMotorolaSrecLine`). The implementation performs only basic structural checks (prefix, record type, line length, hex‑digit validation) and writes the decoded bytes directly without checksum verification.

@l./Source/cmHexFileConverter.h.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmHexFileConverter.h.body: The header exposes a single‑class helper that determines whether a file is Intel HEX, Motorola S‑record, or already binary, and then hands off the file to a routine that streams the appropriate binary data out. The two static methods are the sole interface: `DetermineFileType` returns the enum value based on file extension or content sniffing, and `TryConvert` performs the actual conversion, returning success status.

@l./Source/cmIfCommand.cxx.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmIfCommand.cxx.body: The file implements the logic for CMake’s if‑style conditional blocks. It defines a `cmIfFunctionBlocker` that tracks whether a branch should execute, handles the nesting depth of nested if/endif statements, evaluates conditions via `cmConditionEvaluator`, and reports fatal errors for malformed `else`/`elseif` usage. The `cmIfCommand` routine expands arguments, evaluates the condition, and, if true, installs the blocker to block or allow the enclosed commands accordingly.

@l./Source/cmIfCommand.h.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmIfCommand.h.body: The header declares a helper function for the build‑script engine: `cmIfCommand` takes a vector of `cmListFileArgument` objects and a reference to a `cmExecutionStatus` instance, returning a bool that indicates whether an `if` block was successfully opened. It also pulls in `cmConfigure.h` and the standard `<vector>` header, and declares the supporting types used by this helper.

@l./Source/cmImportedCxxModuleInfo.cxx.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmImportedCxxModuleInfo.cxx.body: The file implements a lightweight lookup service for imported C++ modules. It parses a comma‑delimited list of “name=source,paths” entries, builds a map from source path to `ImportedCxxModuleInfo` (containing the module name and a vector of BMI paths), and keeps a secondary map that lazily constructs and caches a BMI file name for a given source path. The BMI name is derived by SHA‑3‑512 hashing of either the module name or the path itself, truncated to 12 hex‑characters, and appended with “.bmi”. The service exposes an `Initialized()` query, an `Initialize()` routine that populates the maps, and a `BmiNameForSource()` helper that returns the cached or freshly computed BMI name.

@l./Source/cmImportedCxxModuleInfo.h.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmImportedCxxModuleInfo.h.body:
The header declares a lightweight lookup facility for C++ module imports.  
It defines three small value‑type structures:  

* `ImportedCxxModuleInfo` – holds a module’s name and a vector of BMIs that the module can provide.  
* `ImportedCxxModuleGeneratorInfo` – records a single BM‑module name that can be instantiated.  
* `ImportedCxxModuleLookup` – contains two maps keyed by module name: one mapping to `ImportedCxxModuleInfo`, the other to `ImportedCxxModuleGeneratorInfo`. It offers  
  * `Initialize` to parse a comma‑separated list of module names,  
  * `BmiNameForSource` to retrieve the BM‑name for a given source path, and  
  * `Initialized` to check if initialization has already run.  
The implementation simply stores the parsed data in the maps and performs look‑ups; it is used by other parts of the system to resolve module‑to‑BM mappings.

@l./Source/cmIncludeCommand.cxx.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmIncludeCommand.cxx.body: Interprets an `include()` request, validates and normalizes the supplied arguments (including optional flags for `OPTIONAL`, `RESULT_VARIABLE`, and `NO_POLICY_SCOPE`). It resolves the target file name (handling deprecated module names), checks for existence, and loads the file’s content into the current makefile, optionally storing the result path in a user‑provided variable. It emits warnings or errors according to policy status and file‑access failures.

@l./Source/cmIncludeCommand.h.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmIncludeCommand.h.body:
This header declares a helper that parses an `#include`‑style directive.  
The function `cmIncludeCommand` receives a list of argument strings and updates a `cmExecutionStatus` object to indicate success or failure.  
The file pulls in the common configuration header (`cmConfigure.h`) and the standard `<string>` and `<vector>` headers, and exposes only this single interface.

@l./Source/cmIncludeDirectoryCommand.cxx.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmIncludeDirectoryCommand.cxx.body: The file implements the command that adds include directories to a makefile. It parses the supplied arguments, optionally honoring a leading “BEFORE”/“AFTER” flag that dictates whether directories are appended before or after the current include list. Paths are trimmed of surrounding whitespace, normalized (whitespace removed, slashes converted to UNIX style) and relative paths are resolved against the current source directory. Empty strings are rejected. Directories marked “SYSTEM” are collected separately and later added to the system‑include list. The command finally updates the makefile’s include sets for both normal and system directories, respecting the before/after ordering.

@l./Source/cmIncludeDirectoryCommand.h.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmIncludeDirectoryCommand.h.body: The header supplies a single helper routine that consumes a list of string arguments (typically `-I` style flags or raw directory paths) and writes the parsed result into a `cmExecutionStatus` object. It returns a boolean flag to signal whether the include‑directory was processed successfully. The implementation that actually resolves paths, normalises relative segments, and populates the status object lives in the accompanying source file.

@l./Source/cmIncludeExternalMSProjectCom.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmIncludeExternalMSProjectCom.body: The file implements the `cmIncludeExternalMSProjectCommand` command that is invoked by a CMake `INCLUDE_EXTERNAL_MSPROJECT` command. It validates that at least two arguments are supplied; otherwise it reports an error via `cmExecutionStatus`. On Windows (`_WIN32`) the routine parses the remaining arguments into a list of dependencies and optional “TYPE”, “GUID” and “PLATFORM” switches that assign a custom project type, GUID, or platform mapping. It then creates a new utility target, stores the path in the target’s `EXTERNAL_MSPROJECT` property, optionally records the GUID in the cache, and applies any custom type or platform mapping via `VS_PROJECT_TYPE` / `VS_PLATFORM_MAPPING`. It also attaches any specified dependencies to the target. The code is guarded so that non‑Windows builds skip this logic entirely.

@l./Source/cmIncludeExternalMSProjectCom.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmIncludeExternalMSProjectCom.body:
The header declares a helper that attempts to add an external Microsoft‑style project to the build system.  
It takes a list of arguments (typically the path or name of the project) and a status object that will receive any error information.  
The function returns `true` if the inclusion succeeded, otherwise `false`.  
The declaration is referenced in several other translation units.

@l./Source/cmIncludeGuardCommand.cxx.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmIncludeGuardCommand.cxx.body: The file implements an internal command that creates a unique include‑guard variable for the current list file and sets that variable in the appropriate scope (local definition, directory property, or global property). It generates the guard name from an MD5 hash of the file path, checks whether the guard is already present up the directory chain, and then records the guard by adding a definition, a property, or a global property as requested. The command accepts an optional scope argument (“DIRECTORY” or “GLOBAL”) and returns early if the guard is already set.

@l./Source/cmIncludeGuardCommand.h.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmIncludeGuardCommand.h.body: The header declares a helper that evaluates a list of arguments to decide whether a file should be included. It returns a boolean and writes the result into a `cmExecutionStatus` object. The helper supports three modes: GLOBAL (check global properties), DIRECTORY (use a directory property), and VARIABLE (no arguments, treating the call as a simple guard). It is meant to replace the traditional `#pragma once`/include‑guard pattern in cmake‑based builds.

@l./Source/cmIncludeRegularExpressionCom.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmIncludeRegularExpressionCom.body: The file implements a command that accepts up to two arguments: the first argument becomes the pattern used for include directives, and the optional second argument specifies a pattern for the complaint string. It validates the argument count, updates the current makefile’s settings via `SetIncludeRegularExpression` and `SetComplainRegularExpression`, and reports success or error via the supplied `cmExecutionStatus`.

@l./Source/cmIncludeRegularExpressionCom.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmIncludeRegularExpressionCom.body:
The header declares a helper routine used throughout the cmake engine.  
It declares `bool cmIncludeRegularExpressionCommand(std::vector<std::string> const& args, cmExecutionStatus& status);` which parses a list of arguments, runs a command that matches a regular‑expression rule, and records the result in the supplied status object. The function returns `true` when the command succeeds and `false` on failure, allowing callers to handle errors uniformly.

@l./Source/cmInstallCommand.cxx.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmInstallCommand.cxx.body: The file implements the core logic for CMake’s install command. It defines a Helper class that resolves destination paths, checks for errors, and produces install generators for files, targets, and directories. A suite of handler functions—HandleScriptMode, HandleTargetsMode, HandleImportedRuntimeArtifactsMode, HandleDirectoryMode, and HandleRuntimeDependencySetMode—parse command‑line arguments and build the appropriate installation generators. The code also keeps track of runtime dependencies via a RuntimeDependenciesArgs structure and a runtime‑dependency set that gathers library, runtime, and framework components. The helper utilities provide path resolution, error handling, and file‑set construction to support the various install modes.

@l./Source/cmInstallCommand.h.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmInstallCommand.h.body:
The header declares the public API for installing a command in the “cmake” system. It pulls in the core configuration header (`cmConfigure.h`) and the standard `<string>`/`<vector>` headers, then exposes a single function:

```cpp
bool cmInstallCommand(const std::vector<std::string>& args,
                      cmExecutionStatus& status);
```

which processes a list of string arguments and reports the outcome through a `cmExecutionStatus` reference, returning `true` only when the installation succeeds.

@l./Source/cmInstallCommandArguments.cxx.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmInstallCommandArguments.cxx.body:
The file defines the core argument‑parsing logic for the *cmake* install command. It binds a predefined set of keyword names—such as DESTINATION, COMPONENT, NAMELINK_COMPONENT, EXCLUDE_FROM_ALL, RENAMe, PERMISSIONS, CONFIGURATIONS, OPTIONAL, NAMELINK_ONLY, NAMELINK_SKIP, and TYPE—to internal members and supplies a uniform fallback hierarchy that propagates values from a generic argument source when a particular value is missing.  

Core responsibilities include:

* Storing and normalizing a destination path (converting slashes to Unix form).  
* Keeping a list of explicit permission strings in a static table and validating that any supplied permission string matches one of those entries.  
* Supporting optional flags such as “optional”, “exclude‑from‑all”, “namelink‑only”, and “namelink‑skip” via Boolean getters that cascade to any generic argument object.  
* Providing a small, dedicated set of argument parsers for include‑directories (converting each to Unix format) and a file‑set argument that prefixes its parsing with the literal “FILE_SET”.  

The class is designed to be lightweight, thread‑safe, and easily testable; it performs no I/O of its own and only manipulates in‑memory string objects.

@l./Source/cmInstallCommandArguments.h.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmInstallCommandArguments.h.body:
The header defines three classes that handle arguments for a CMake install command.  
`cmInstallCommandArguments` holds and parses the generic arguments (destination, component name, optional flags, permission strings, and configuration lists). It supplies accessor methods and a `Finalize()` routine that resolves and validates the destination path, checks permissions, and applies default component names.  
`cmInstallCommandIncludesArgument` parses and stores include‑directory arguments.  
`cmInstallCommandFileSetArguments` derives from the base class and adds support for parsing a file‑set argument.

@l./Source/cmInstallCxxModuleBmiGenerato.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmInstallCxxModuleBmiGenerato.body: The file implements a generator class that resolves a target name to a specific generator target, then produces a path for a CMake script that will install a C++ module’s Bmi file. It builds that path using the target’s support directory and the supplied configuration name (falling back to “noconfig” if empty). It writes a single line to the output stream that includes the generated script, optionally marked as optional. The constructor sets whether the generator is optional and stores file permissions; the Compute method attaches the relevant target, and GetDestination evaluates the destination path against the current configuration. The class does not perform any heavy processing; its role is simply to emit the include directive for installing the module.

@l./Source/cmInstallCxxModuleBmiGenerato.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmInstallCxxModuleBmiGenerato.body:
The header declares an implementation for generating installation rules for a C++ module’s “BMI” (Binary Module Interface) files.  
The class inherits from a generic install‑generator and offers a constructor that receives the target name, destination directory, file‑permission string, a list of configuration strings, the component name, a message‑level flag, and flags for excluding the file from a master list and for optional installation.  

The key public interface includes:
* `Compute(cmLocalGenerator*)` – performs the rule generation, returning success or failure.  
* Accessors (`GetFilePermissions()`, `GetDestination()`, `GetScriptLocation()`, `GetTarget()`, `GetOptional()`, `GetMessageLevel()`) that expose internal state.  
* The protected helper `GenerateScriptForConfig(std::ostream&, const std::string&, Indent)` that emits the actual rule snippet per configuration.  

Internally the class stores the target name, a pointer to the target, a pointer to the local generator, the file‑permission string, and an optional flag. The implementation relies on the base class `cmInstallGenerator` for common install logic.

@l./Source/cmInstallDirectoryGenerator.c.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmInstallDirectoryGenerator.c.body: The file implements a directory‑install generator that, given a list of source directories and a destination, produces the install rules for each configuration. It examines the source paths for generator expressions; if any are present it sets a flag so that per‑configuration actions are emitted. When generating the script, it expands those expressions against the current configuration and the current makefile, ensuring absolute paths before emitting the rule via `AddInstallRule`. It handles optional installs, file and directory permissions, and supports literal arguments for the install command.

@l./Source/cmInstallDirectoryGenerator.h.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmInstallDirectoryGenerator.h.body:
The header declares a `cmInstallDirectoryGenerator` class that stores a list of source directories, a destination path, permission strings, and a flag indicating whether the installation is optional.  
It implements the `Compute` routine that produces installation rules, and supplies helpers for generating installation scripts and querying the stored configuration (e.g., the directory list and destination).

@l./Source/cmInstallExportGenerator.cxx.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmInstallExportGenerator.cxx.body: The file implements a CMake generator that writes installation rules for export sets. It creates a temporary directory, writes an import file for each configuration (or for a single configuration if none are provided), and generates the necessary install rules to replace any old export files. It supports both standard and Android‑specific generators, and handles C++‑module export files per configuration. The class also hashes the destination path to keep the temporary directory name short.

@l./Source/cmInstallExportGenerator.h.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmInstallExportGenerator.h.body:
The class orchestrates the creation of export‑generation scripts.  
It holds an export set and a local generator, and implements the virtual `Compute` method to assemble the script.  
Key responsibilities include:

* Constructing a destination directory and file name from the provided parameters.  
* Producing the main import file via `GenerateImportFile`.  
* Writing the script files through the protected overrides `GenerateScript`, `GenerateScriptConfigs`, and `GenerateScriptActions`.  
* Exposing accessors such as `GetExportSet()`, `GetLocalGenerator()`, `GetNamespace()`, `GetMainImportFile()`, `GetDestination()`, and related helpers for temporary directories and C++ module paths.

@l./Source/cmInstallFileSetGenerator.cxx.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmInstallFileSetGenerator.cxx.body: The cmInstallFileSetGenerator class takes a file‑set description and a target name to produce install rules. During Compute it resolves the target generator in the current or global scope, then collects the file entries associated with that target. CalculateFilesPerDir produces a mapping of directories to the file lists that belong in each directory; GenerateScriptForConfig writes installation commands that install those files into the destination path, respecting the optional flag and any specified file permissions. The class manages optional installation and permission handling while delegating rule generation to its base generator.

@l./Source/cmInstallFileSetGenerator.h.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmInstallFileSetGenerator.h.body: cmInstallFileSetGenerator implements an installation generator that takes a predefined file set and installs it into a target location. It stores the target name, permissions, and optional flag, and on Compute() pulls the set’s files per configuration, producing a script that creates the necessary directories and copies each file to the destination.

@l./Source/cmInstallFilesCommand.cxx.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmInstallFilesCommand.cxx.body: The file implements the CMake install‑file command. It validates the provided arguments, resolves source paths (preferring binary tree when available), and registers an appropriate install generator. It handles both explicit file lists prefixed by the `FILES` keyword and implicit glob patterns supplied as arguments.

@l./Source/cmInstallFilesCommand.h.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmInstallFilesCommand.h.body: The header declares a helper that parses a list of file‑paths supplied in `args` and orchestrates their installation, reporting any errors or successes through the supplied `cmExecutionStatus` instance. It pulls in the common configuration header and standard containers, leaving the actual installation logic to be implemented elsewhere.

@l./Source/cmInstallFilesGenerator.cxx.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmInstallFilesGenerator.cxx.body:
Handles installing files by evaluating generator expressions for destination, rename and individual file names.  
When any expression is found it triggers per‑configuration file handling.  
Finally it writes install rules honoring optional flags, program type and specified file permissions.

@l./Source/cmInstallFilesGenerator.h.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmInstallFilesGenerator.h.body: The header declares a helper class that owns a list of files, a destination path, and flags for optional installs and program‑type handling. It implements `Compute()` to emit the installation logic, exposes helpers to read the destination, rename and file list for a given config, and generates the shell snippets that add the appropriate install rules. The class keeps a pointer to a local‑generator, a file list, permissions, and rename string, and offers a public interface for optional handling and back‑trace support.

@l./Source/cmInstallGenerator.cxx.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmInstallGenerator.cxx.body: The file implements the `cmInstallGenerator` helper that emits CMake install‑style rules. It holds configuration data, a destination path, and a component filter; it writes conditional install blocks that respect component tests and tweak logic (renaming, permissions, etc.). It produces the appropriate `file(INSTALL …)` commands with optional arguments, emits warnings or errors for absolute paths, and supports both per‑file and per‑config install entries.

@l./Source/cmInstallGenerator.h.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmInstallGenerator.h.body:
This header declares a helper class that emits installation rules for a build system.  
The `cmInstallGenerator` class derives from `cmScriptGenerator` and contains logic for deciding whether an install should be emitted (`HaveInstall()`), building install commands with options (`AddInstallRule()`), and tailoring the script with tweaks for specific configurations. It keeps track of the target directory (`Destination`), component name, message level, and flags controlling exclusion of components. It also supplies utilities for normalizing paths (`ConvertToAbsoluteDestination()`), selecting message verbosity from settings (`SelectMessageLevel()`), and extracting back‑trace information (`GetBacktrace()`). The class exposes a small public API: constructors, destructors, a virtual override of `GenerateScript()`, and helpers (`CreateComponentTest()`, `AddTweak()`). All of this is geared toward generating script fragments that perform the actual install step during a build.

@l./Source/cmInstallGetRuntimeDependenci.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmInstallGetRuntimeDependenci.body: The file implements a generator that emits a CMake‑style script block that declares which executables, libraries, modules, and directory patterns must be installed for each configuration. It builds the argument lists for those entries, applies regular‑expression filters, writes the appropriate `POST_EXCLUDE_FILES` directives, and adds optional `RPATH_PREFIX` handling when the install path flag is set.

@l./Source/cmInstallGetRuntimeDependenci.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmInstallGetRuntimeDependenci.body:
The class implements the logic for collecting the set of runtime dependencies that must be present when a target is installed.  
It receives a *runtime dependency set* object and a collection of search‑directories together with include/exclude regular‑expressions and file lists that control which libraries or frameworks are considered.  
During the *Compute* step it walks the supplied directories, applies the include/exclude filters in order (pre‑, post‑, file‑based) and populates the dependency set.  
When the script generation phase is reached, it emits shell commands that `install` the identified libraries, with optional path prefixes and flags for “no‑install‑rpath” mode.  
The class mainly serves as a plug‑in to the overall install generator, providing the dynamic dependency resolution and script output used by the rest of the system.

@l./Source/cmInstallImportedRuntimeArtif.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmInstallImportedRuntimeArtif.body: The file implements a generator that, given a target name and destination path, resolves the target either in the local or global generator scope, then emits install rules tailored to the target’s type. It uses a regular‑expression based path parser to detect Apple‑specific framework or bundle layouts and generates corresponding `cmInstallType_*` rules (executable, shared library, module library), applying the supplied file‑permission string and optional‑installation flag. The generator marks that each configuration is processed separately (`ActionsPerConfig = true`).

@l./Source/cmInstallImportedRuntimeArtif.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmInstallImportedRuntimeArtif.body: The header declares a lightweight installer generator that, given a target name, destination path, file permissions, and a list of configuration strings, constructs a sequence of installation commands for a specific runtime component. It exposes helpers to report its target, whether the operation is optional, and to resolve a configuration’s destination directory, while internally it keeps the target name, file permissions, and optional flag for script generation. The class ultimately implements the virtual methods `Compute` and `GenerateScriptForConfig` to populate the install script for each configuration.

@l./Source/cmInstallMode.h.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmInstallMode.h.body: The header declares an enumeration that the rest of the project uses to decide whether a file should be copied, symlinked, or both. The values cover absolute and relative path cases and combinations of the two operations.

@l./Source/cmInstallProgramsCommand.cxx.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmInstallProgramsCommand.cxx.body: The file implements a command that registers an “install” target, collects the list of program files to be installed—either supplied explicitly or discovered via a glob expression—resolves each path to a build‑tree file, and finally creates an install‑generator instance that copies the chosen files into the configured installation prefix.

@l./Source/cmInstallProgramsCommand.h.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmInstallProgramsCommand.h.body: The header declares a single function template that accepts a vector of string arguments and a mutable status object; it forwards those to the implementation that performs the installation logic and signals success via its boolean return. The function relies on `cmConfigure.h` for configuration context and on a forward‑declared `cmExecutionStatus` for reporting outcomes.

@l./Source/cmInstallRuntimeDependencySet.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmInstallRuntimeDependencySet.body: The file implements a helper class that collects runtime dependency items for an install target. It exposes methods to add executables, libraries, and modules, maintaining separate lists for each type. A special routine guarantees only a single bundle‑executable is recorded; attempts to add a second one are rejected. The class also computes the transitive closure of dependencies for a target via a recursive helper that walks the direct dependency graph, filtering out cross‑target and non‑linkable targets, and only retaining those that are executable, shared library, or module targets. The logic further supplies utilities for determining the full filesystem path of a target item for a given configuration.

@l./Source/cmInstallRuntimeDependencySet.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmInstallRuntimeDependencySet.body: The class represents a collection of runtime artifacts that must be present when a built target is installed. It holds three distinct lists—executables, libraries and modules—plus an optional bundle executable. Items are added through factory‑style `Add…` methods that wrap raw generator objects in the appropriate `Item` subclass (`TargetItem` or `ImportedTargetItem`). The base `Item` interface supplies the artifact path and an optional hook for adding post‑exclude files. The set exposes read‑only accessors to the three lists and a flag for emptiness, while internally tracking per‑target dependency sets in a map.

@l./Source/cmInstallRuntimeDependencySet.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmInstallRuntimeDependencySet.body: The file defines the **cmInstallRuntimeDependencySetGenerator** class, which takes a collection of runtime dependency paths, evaluates them for a given configuration, and emits CMake script snippets that create install rules for each dependency. It distinguishes between library and framework types, applies optional stripping logic, and produces the proper CMake commands to copy, link, or rename the files while handling path prefixes and install‑name prefixes.

@l./Source/cmInstallRuntimeDependencySet.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmInstallRuntimeDependencySet.body: The header declares a specialized generator that, given a set of runtime dependencies, produces the shell‑script snippets needed to wire those dependencies into a macOS build. It keeps track of whether the dependencies are ordinary libraries or frameworks, stores the list of “real‑path” install locations, and has helper routines that emit the Apple‑specific `install_name` or `strip` commands needed to make the build sandbox‑compatible. The class inherits from the generic `cmInstallGenerator`, overriding the core `GenerateScriptForConfig` routine to emit the correct Apple‑style install commands for each configuration passed to it.

@l./Source/cmInstallScriptGenerator.cxx.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmInstallScriptGenerator.cxx.body:
The file implements the `cmInstallScriptGenerator` helper that produces install‑time scripts for a component.  
On construction it scans the supplied script for generator expressions; if any are found it flags `ActionsPerConfig`.  
During `Compute()` it checks the current policy state: when the required‑genex policy is in effect it sets `AllowGenex` to true so that the generator expressions will be expanded at runtime.  
The `GetScript()` routine performs the actual replacement of the install‑prefix and evaluates the expressions using the current configuration.  
Finally, the public helpers (`AddScriptInstallRule`, `GenerateScriptActions`, `GenerateScriptForConfig`) emit the appropriate rule into a CMake file, either as a plain script block or an `include()` statement depending on the `Code` flag.

@l./Source/cmInstallScriptGenerator.h.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmInstallScriptGenerator.h.body: cmInstallScriptGenerator is a concrete implementation of the abstract cmInstallGenerator. It stores the raw script text, a flag indicating whether code should be emitted, and a pointer to a cmLocalGenerator that drives the actual generation. The class overrides the core generation hooks (Compute, GenerateScriptActions, GenerateScriptForConfig) and supplies helper utilities such as AddScriptInstallRule and GetScript. The constructor receives the script text, flags, component configuration and optional back‑trace information; the destructor cleans up associated resources.

@l./Source/cmInstallSubdirectoryGenerato.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmInstallSubdirectoryGenerato.body: The file implements a specialized install generator that, when a sub‑directory is requested for installation, emits the necessary script fragments to pull in that directory’s `cmake_install.cmake`. It consults the CMP0082 policy to decide whether the legacy‑style inclusion or the new‑style policy‑guarded include should be used, and writes the corresponding guard‑check and `include` line into the generated makefile.

@l./Source/cmInstallSubdirectoryGenerato.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmInstallSubdirectoryGenerato.body:
The header declares a concrete `cmInstallSubdirectoryGenerator` that specializes the generic install‑generator base.  
Its constructor receives the owning `cmMakefile`, the destination directory string, and a back‑trace object; the destructor cleans up.  
The class exposes the standard install‑generator interface: `HaveInstall()`, `CheckCMP0082()`, `Compute()`, and an internal `GenerateScript()` that writes the actual install rules to a stream.  
Internally it stores the makefile reference, the target directory string, and a pointer to a `cmLocalGenerator` that drives the rule emission.

@l./Source/cmInstallTargetGenerator.cxx.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmInstallTargetGenerator.cxx.body: For each target type (executable, library, framework, bundle, etc.) it computes the set of source files that need to be copied into the install tree, generates the actual install rules, and handles special cases such as namelinks, Apple frameworks, and runtime‑path changes. It produces the install‑name mapping, writes the RPATH change scripts, applies strip/ranlib steps when needed, and finally emits any required warnings (e.g. CMP0095).

@l./Source/cmInstallTargetGenerator.h.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmInstallTargetGenerator.h.body: `cmInstallTargetGenerator.h` declares a helper class that, for a build target, orchestrates the mapping of source files to install locations, calculates the final install names (including special handling for import libraries), and emits the shell‑script snippets that implement the install rules. It exposes hooks for tweaking file paths before and after replacement, for generating patch rules, and for emitting rules for stripping, running libraries, and universal install handling.

@l./Source/cmInstallTargetsCommand.cxx.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmInstallTargetsCommand.cxx.body: The function `cmInstallTargetsCommand` is called with a vector of target names and a reference to a status object. It first verifies that at least two arguments were supplied; otherwise it records an error and fails. It then retrieves the current `cmMakefile` and turns on the global install flag. For every target name supplied, it locates that target in the makefile’s target map. If found, it writes the given installation directory (defaulting to “/bin” or a value following the special keyword `RUNTIME_DIRECTORY`) into the target’s install path and runtime path fields, and marks the target as having an install rule. If a requested target cannot be found, an error message is produced. Finally the function adds the default install component to the global generator before returning success.

@l./Source/cmInstallTargetsCommand.h.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmInstallTargetsCommand.h.body:
The header declares a helper routine used throughout the project to perform the “install‑targets” step of the build system.  
`cmInstallTargetsCommand` takes a list of target names (as a `std::vector<std::string>`), performs whatever actions are necessary to materialize those targets, and reports success or failure via the `cmExecutionStatus` object.  The implementation resides in the corresponding source file; this header simply exposes the function’s interface and the type used to capture the outcome.

@l./Source/cmInstallType.h.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmInstallType.h.body: Defines an enumeration of the various installation targets used throughout the project – executables, static and shared libraries, module libraries, generic files or programs, and directories. The enum is leveraged by other modules to tag or branch logic based on the type of artifact being installed.

@l./Source/cmInstalledFile.cxx.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmInstalledFile.cxx.body: The file defines the implementation of the cmInstalledFile class used by CMake. It stores a file name and a map of named properties. Each property keeps a list of parsed generator expressions. The class offers APIs to set the file name (parsing it with a generator expression), query the name, add or replace properties, and retrieve property values. Property values are parsed into lists of strings using cmList and converted to boolean strings via cmIsOn. The implementation relies on cmGeneratorExpression to interpret expressions from the current makefile and on back‑trace utilities for context.

@l./Source/cmInstalledFile.h.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmInstalledFile.h.body: The header defines a class that models a file destined for installation. It stores a file name together with a compiled expression for that name and a map of arbitrary properties that can be attached to the file. The interface allows adding, removing, and querying properties, including convenient helpers for appending string values (with an optional “as string” flag). Copying of the class is deliberately disabled. Internally it relies on `std::unique_ptr` to own the compiled expression objects and uses standard containers (`std::map`, `std::vector`) for storage.

@l./Source/cmJSONHelpers.cxx.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmJSONHelpers.cxx.body: The file implements a set of small helper routines that construct and report JSON‑parsing errors. Each helper is a lambda‑style generator that, when invoked, inspects a supplied `Json::Value` and a parsing state, and records an explanatory error at the appropriate location. The helpers cover common type mismatches (string, bool, integer, unsigned‑integer), the absence of required fields, and the presence of unexpected fields. The code uses a small `ObjectError` enum to classify the error type and a shared routine that fabricates an error message string from a supplied name‑generator; this allows callers to supply a context‑specific name while reusing the same error‑formatting logic. The module is deliberately light‑weight and pure‑utility, with no side‑effects beyond populating the `cmJSONState` error list.

@l./Source/cmJSONHelpers.h.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmJSONHelpers.h.body: Provides a collection of templated helper functions that convert a cmake JSON Value into native C++ types and verify their validity. The helpers expose simple delegates for strings, integers, booleans, vectors, maps, and optional values, each returning a boolean success flag and invoking an error callback on mismatch. A small builder class (`cmJSONHelperBuilder::Object`) lets callers bind struct members to JSON fields, automating required‑field checks and tracking excess fields. All utilities report errors through the `JsonErrors` namespace, which collects specific error types such as missing required fields, extra fields, or type mismatches.

@l./Source/cmJSONState.cxx.author: AI Short Overview
