It maintains a stack of nested includes, applies search‑and‑replace rules, and handles indentation trimming of multiline blocks. The module focuses on parsing these directives in a controlled fashion so that all emitted markup is syntactically correct for downstream consumers.

@l./Source/cmRST.h.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmRST.h.body:
The header declares a helper class that walks through reStructured‑Text files, looking for a small set of CMake‑specific directives (e.g. `.. literal`, `.. code`, `.. replace`, `.. toc_tree`).  
When a file is passed to `ProcessFile`, the class reads it line‑by‑line, recognizes those directives, and emits either literal text, code blocks, or generated table‑of‑contents entries into an output stream.  
It keeps a small state machine (the `Include`, `Markup`, `Directive` enums) to know whether it’s inside a normal paragraph, a literal block, or a code block, and it performs substitutions for back‑references (`.. replace ..`) via the `Replace` map.  
The result is a flattened, console‑friendly help string that can be sent directly to the command‑line help output.

@l./Source/cmRange.h.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmRange.h.body: cmRange.h declares a generic range view that stores a begin and end iterator and offers utility operations. It defines FilterIterator and TransformIterator adapters that allow a range to be lazily filtered or mapped by a predicate or function. The main cmRange class supports bidirectional iteration, size and emptiness checks, and provides convenience helpers such as cmMakeRange, cmReverseRange, and predicate queries (all_of, any_of, none_of).

@l./Source/cmRemoveCommand.cxx.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmRemoveCommand.cxx.body:
The file implements the **cmRemoveCommand** helper, which removes a supplied list of arguments from a variable’s definition. It does so by:

1. Reading the current value of the variable from the makefile.  
2. Expanding that value into its constituent arguments.  
3. Removing each argument that matches an entry in the supplied list.  
4. Re‑assembling the remaining arguments into a new definition string.  
5. Adding that new definition back to the makefile.  
6. Returning success (true) regardless of the operation’s outcome.

@l./Source/cmRemoveCommand.h.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmRemoveCommand.h.body: The header defines a single function `cmRemoveCommand`. The function takes a list of string arguments and a status object and returns a boolean indicating whether the remove command succeeded. It is used by other components of the CMake system to invoke the remove command, relying on the configuration defined in `cmConfigure.h`.

@l./Source/cmRemoveDefinitionsCommand.cx.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmRemoveDefinitionsCommand.cx.body: The implementation simply iterates over the supplied argument strings, calling `RemoveDefineFlag` on each flag name against the current `cmMakefile` instance obtained from the `cmExecutionStatus`. It then returns `true` unconditionally, signalling that the command succeeded regardless of whether any definitions were actually removed. This helper is invoked by other modules that need to wipe specific definition switches from a running makefile state.

@l./Source/cmRemoveDefinitionsCommand.h.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmRemoveDefinitionsCommand.h.body:
The header declares the central routine for the “remove‑definitions” command in the cmake tool.  
`cmRemoveDefinitionsCommand()` takes a list of argument strings and a mutable `cmExecutionStatus` object. The function parses the arguments, removes the requested definitions from the current configuration, updates the `status` with any diagnostics, and returns `true` on success or `false` if the operation fails.

@l./Source/cmReturnCommand.cxx.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmReturnCommand.cxx.body: The code implements the handling of the CMake `return` command. It inspects the supplied arguments against the current policy `CMP0140`; on mismatch it emits a warning or fatal error and marks a fatal condition in the system tools. When the command is correctly invoked with the `PROPAGATE` argument, it records the arguments in the execution status and reports success.

@l./Source/cmReturnCommand.h.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmReturnCommand.h.body: The header declares a single entry point: `cmReturnCommand`, a helper that accepts a collection of argument strings and a mutable `cmExecutionStatus` object, invokes the underlying command machinery, and reports success via the returned Boolean flag.

@l./Source/cmRulePlaceholderExpander.cxx.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmRulePlaceholderExpander.cxx.body: The file implements a rule‑placeholder expander used by CMake. It holds mappings from variable names to concrete values (compiler options, paths, flags, etc.) and expands a rule string by replacing known placeholders (e.g. “TARGET”, “FLAGS”, “LINK_FLAGS”, etc.) with the corresponding runtime values. When a placeholder refers to a compiler command, the expander builds the command string by appending arguments such as external tool‑chain options and system‑root flags, adding a launcher if required. If the placeholder does not match any predefined name it is returned unchanged. The class also supports quoted/unquoted expansion for the target name and supports language‑specific overrides. The logic is exposed via `ExpandVariable`, `ExpandRuleVariables` and the constructor that stores the compiler and variable mappings.

@l./Source/cmRulePlaceholderExpander.h.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmRulePlaceholderExpander.h.body: The header declares a helper class that injects concrete values into rule strings used by the CMake system. It stores mappings for compilers, variable names, and system‑root paths, and exposes a single public routine that replaces placeholders in a supplied string with the real values supplied in a `RuleVariables` structure. Internally it overrides the base‐class variable‑expansion routine to perform the substitution logic. The class is instantiated by various parts of the build engine to turn template rules into fully‑resolved command lines.

@l./Source/cmRuntimeDependencyArchive.cx.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmRuntimeDependencyArchive.cx.body: This file implements a `cmRuntimeDependencyArchive` class that coordinates the detection of executable, library and module dependencies for a generated binary. It loads platform‑specific linkers (ELF, PE, MachO) based on a `CMAKE_GET_RUNTIME_DEPENDENCIES_PLATFORM` definition, scans each supplied file via the chosen linker, and filters candidates through include/exclude regular‑expression lists. The class tracks resolved and unresolved paths, records the search locations of each dependency, and exposes helper functions to locate tools such as `objdump` on Windows by probing common Visual Studio installation directories.

@l./Source/cmRuntimeDependencyArchive.h.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmRuntimeDependencyArchive.h.body:
The header declares a helper that scans a list of search directories, applies pre‑ and post‑filter regular expressions, and records which executables, libraries and modules can be resolved.  
After construction, `Prepare()` builds a link‑tool (via `cmBinUtilsLinker`) and populates internal maps of resolved and unresolved paths.  
`GetRuntimeDependencies()` queries that map to return which components need inclusion, while the add‑path helpers update the resolved set or flag unresolved names.  
Static `PlatformSupportsRuntimeDependencies()` lets callers guard against unsupported platforms.

@l./Source/cmScanDepFormat.cxx.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmScanDepFormat.cxx.body: The file implements a lightweight JSON parser/writer for a custom dependency format (P1689). It defines parsing helpers that validate and populate a `cmScanDepInfo` object with information about primary output, extra outputs, provided/required modules, and lookup strategies, and a writer that serializes the same structure back to JSON.

@l./Source/cmScanDepFormat.h.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmScanDepFormat.h.body: The header declares a minimal dependency‑description format used in the build system. It defines a simple enum (`LookupMethod`) for how module names map to source files and two structs (`cmSourceReqInfo` and `cmScanDepInfo`) that describe the required and provided modules for a given target. Two helper routines expose parsing and serialising of that format, returning a truthy flag or populating a `cmScanDepInfo` object. The file is a thin wrapper around the core logic in the scan‑dependency tool; it is included wherever the build scripts need to read or write the P1689 dependency lists.

@l./Source/cmScriptGenerator.cxx.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmScriptGenerator.cxx.body: The file implements a helper class that emits shell‑style scripts conditioned on the current build configuration. It stores the runtime config variable and a list of target configurations and, during generation, produces a test string that matches the current configuration using a simple regex‑style encoding. The generator then emits `if/elseif/else/endif` blocks around the corresponding actions, handling both single‑configuration and per‑configuration cases via `GenerateScriptActionsOnce` and `GenerateScriptActionsPerConfig`.

@l./Source/cmScriptGenerator.h.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmScriptGenerator.h.body: The file defines a small framework for emitting install‑/test‑scripts: an indentation helper (`cmScriptGeneratorIndent`) that writes a specific number of spaces, and a base class (`cmScriptGenerator`) that stores the runtime‑config name, the list of configurations and flags controlling whether actions are emitted once or per‑config. The base class supplies pure virtual hooks (`GenerateScript`, `GenerateScriptConfigs`, `GenerateScriptActions`, `GenerateScriptForConfig`, etc.) that derived generators override to emit the appropriate shell snippets. The class also exposes a small utility API (`Generate`, `GeneratesForConfig`, `CreateConfigTest`, `CreateComponentTest`) to help subclasses decide when a rule is required and to produce the required test strings.

@l./Source/cmSearchPath.cxx.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmSearchPath.cxx.body: The file implements a helper that gathers executable search paths for a CMake build. The `cmSearchPath` class holds a list of paths together with an optional prefix. It extracts paths from the project’s registry, environment variables, and CMake variables, expands any globbed patterns, and normalises them to Unix‑style separators. It filters out paths whose names or prefixes are in supplied ignore sets. The class supports adding simple paths, user‑specified paths, prefixed paths, and suffix‑augmented paths, while collapsing duplicate entries and ensuring “/bin”/“/sbin” paths are substituted with their parent directories. The public API supplies `AddPath`, `AddUserPath`, `AddCMakePath`, `AddEnvPath`, `AddCMakePrefixPath`, `AddEnvPrefixPath`, `AddSuffixes`, `AddPrefixPaths` and `ExtractWithout` for filtering. The implementation uses `cmSystemTools::CollapseFullPath`, `GlobDirs`, `ExpandExpression`, and `cmWindowsRegistry` to resolve Windows registry values.

@l./Source/cmSearchPath.h.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmSearchPath.h.body:
The header declares a lightweight container for managing a list of search‑path entries.  
The public interface lets callers push individual paths or ranges of environment‑, CMake‑, and user‑supplied prefixes, optionally stripping a trailing “/bin” component.  
Internally it keeps the entries in a `std::vector` of a small `PathWithPrefix` struct that orders items first by the real path string and second by the associated prefix.  
A single helper, `AddPathInternal`, implements the common logic for all “add” methods.  
The `ExtractWithout` routine returns every stored path that does not match any string in the supplied ignore sets, with an optional flag to empty the internal collection after extraction.

@l./Source/cmSeparateArgumentsCommand.cx.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmSeparateArgumentsCommand.cx.body: The file implements the `cmSeparateArgumentsCommand` command which processes a list of arguments supplied to a Makefile variable. It validates that at least one argument is present, then parses flags such as `UNIX_COMMAND`, `WINDOWS_COMMAND`, `NATIVE_COMMAND`, `PROGRAM`, and `SEPARATE_ARGS`. Based on those flags it determines the target platform (Unix or Windows) and whether the input is a program path or just a command string. The routine then finds the executable (checking existence or using a system search), splits the command into individual arguments using appropriate parsing logic, escapes semicolons in each piece, and finally stores the resulting argument list back into the Makefile under the given variable name. If any parsing rule or requirement is violated, it reports an error through `cmExecutionStatus`.

@l./Source/cmSeparateArgumentsCommand.h.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmSeparateArgumentsCommand.h.body: The header declares a helper that parses a list of tokens supplied to a CMake invocation. The exported `cmSeparateArgumentsCommand` function receives that vector, inspects it, and returns `true` only if every token can be mapped into the expected argument structure; otherwise it reports a failure through the `cmExecutionStatus` reference. The implementation is invoked by several front‑end components that need the parsed argument list before they can construct the internal representation.

@l./Source/cmSetCommand.cxx.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmSetCommand.cxx.body: The file implements the core logic for the `SET` command in the build system, interpreting the supplied arguments to assign, remove, or modify variables in the makefile or environment. It supports optional caching, forcing, and parent‑scope changes, handling all cases of simple assignment, clearing, or cache‑based updates while validating argument combinations and reporting errors or warnings as needed.

@l./Source/cmSetCommand.h.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmSetCommand.h.body: The header declares a CMake variable‑setting helper exposed as `bool cmSetCommand(const std::vector<std::string>& args, cmExecutionStatus& status)`. It pulls in the common configuration header, pulls in C++ standard containers, and promises that the supplied arguments are expanded before assignment. The declaration returns a `bool` indicating success, while forwarding any run‑time diagnostics through the `cmExecutionStatus` reference.

@l./Source/cmSetDirectoryPropertiesComma.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmSetDirectoryPropertiesComma.body: The file implements a helper that parses a list of arguments received by the “SET_CMAKE_PROPERTIES” command. It first verifies that the argument list has an odd length (the first argument being the command name, followed by property/value pairs), then iterates through each pair. For each property it checks whether it is a protected keyword (like “VARIABLES” or “MACROS”) and rejects such attempts with a specific error message. Otherwise it forwards the property/value pair to the current make‑file via `SetProperty`. This routine returns a success flag and records any error in a `cmExecutionStatus` object.

@l./Source/cmSetDirectoryPropertiesComma.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmSetDirectoryPropertiesComma.body: The header declares a single function `cmSetDirectoryPropertiesCommand` that takes a vector of string arguments and a reference to a `cmExecutionStatus` object, returns a bool indicating success, and is used to apply directory‑level settings in the project’s configuration system.

@l./Source/cmSetPropertyCommand.cxx.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmSetPropertyCommand.cxx.body: The file implements the *Set Property* command in CMake, parsing the command’s arguments, determining the scope (GLOBAL, DIRECTORY, TARGET, SOURCE, TEST, CACHE, or INSTALL), and then dispatching to the appropriate handler. Each handler sets or appends the named property on the relevant object—be it the global makefile, a directory’s CMake instance, a target, a source file, a test case, a cache entry, or an installed file. Special handling is provided for the *GENERATED* flag on source files, where policy CMP0118 rules apply. The code also validates argument counts, scopes, and handles absolute‑path conversion for source file references. The implementation is split into helper functions inside the anonymous namespace to keep the dispatch logic tidy.

@l./Source/cmSetPropertyCommand.h.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmSetPropertyCommand.h.body: The header implements a command that processes a list of command‑line arguments to set, remove, or append properties on source files within a CMake build. It parses the arguments, resolves source file directories (both source and target directories), validates whether the relevant options are enabled, and applies the requested operation (Set, Append, AppendAsString, or Remove) to each target file via the helper function `HandleAndValidateSourceFilePropertyGENERATED`. The code also handles test‑directory scopes and ensures all file paths are absolute before modification.

@l./Source/cmSetSourceFilesPropertiesCom.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmSetSourceFilesPropertiesCom.body: The file implements the core logic for the **`SET_SOURCE_FILES_PROPERTIES`** command in the CMake toolchain. It parses the argument vector into a list of target source files and a list of property/value pairs, handling both the legacy “old‑style” keywords (ABSTRACT, GENERATED, WRAP_EXCLUDE, COMPILE_FLAGS, OBJECT_DEPENDS, PROPERTIES) and the newer “new‑style” property assignments. It performs sanity checks on the directories specified by the `DIRECTORY` and `TARGET_DIRECTORY` options, resolves any relative paths to absolute ones, and finally iterates over each specified source file, invoking the `SetPropertyCommand` helpers to apply the requested properties to the internal `cmSourceFile` objects.

@l./Source/cmSetSourceFilesPropertiesCom.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmSetSourceFilesPropertiesCom.body:
The header declares a single helper function that applies a list of property assignments to a set of source files.  
The function accepts a vector of string arguments and a mutable status object, returning `true` when the operation succeeds and `false` otherwise.  
It relies on the `cmConfigure` infrastructure for interpreting the arguments and on the `cmExecutionStatus` type for reporting success or failure.

@l./Source/cmSetTargetPropertiesCommand..author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmSetTargetPropertiesCommand..body: The function parses a list of arguments, checks that a valid number of name/value pairs follows a “PROPERTIES” marker, then for each target name it locates the target in the current makefile, assigns each specified property key to the target’s property value, verifies that assignment succeeds, and reports any errors or missing targets.

@l./Source/cmSetTargetPropertiesCommand..author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmSetTargetPropertiesCommand..body:
This header declares a single helper function `cmSetTargetPropertiesCommand`.  
The function receives a vector of string arguments (the command‑line tokens supplied to the command) and a reference to a `cmExecutionStatus` object that will be populated with the result of executing the command.  
The function returns a bool indicating whether the command succeeded (`true` for success, `false` for failure).  
The header pulls in the common configuration header (`cmConfigure.h`) and pulls in standard `<string>` and `<vector>` headers to enable the string collection used in the command parsing.  
The implementation in the corresponding source file performs the actual parsing, validation, and application of the properties to the target; the header merely provides the declaration and required includes for downstream modules.

@l./Source/cmSetTestsPropertiesCommand.c.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmSetTestsPropertiesCommand.c.body: The file implements the `cmSetTestsPropertiesCommand` function that parses a list of test names and property/value pairs supplied on the command line, resolves the target makefile (optionally following a directory argument), validates the input, and then iterates over the named tests to apply each provided property to the corresponding `cmTest` objects. It reports any missing tests or invalid arguments via the `cmExecutionStatus` interface and returns a boolean indicating success.

@l./Source/cmSetTestsPropertiesCommand.h.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmSetTestsPropertiesCommand.h.body: The header declares a single entry point for the “set‑tests‑properties” command in the cmake toolchain. Its public interface is a function that receives a vector of string arguments and a mutable status object, parses those arguments to adjust test‑related properties in the current configuration, and returns a success flag. The function is meant to be called by the command‑dispatch code once the command has been parsed, and it uses the `cmExecutionStatus` type to surface any errors that arise during the property‑setting process.

@l./Source/cmSiteNameCommand.cxx.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmSiteNameCommand.cxx.body: The `cmSiteNameCommand` function checks that a single argument (the desired variable name) is supplied. It queries the current makefile cache; if the variable is already defined it returns success. Otherwise, it attempts to discover the host’s name: on Windows it reads the computer name from the registry; on other platforms it runs the `hostname` command (looking in a predefined list of standard directories). After trimming any leading/trailing whitespace, it stores the resolved name as a cache entry in the makefile with a descriptive comment and marks the entry as a string. The routine finally returns success.

@l./Source/cmSiteNameCommand.h.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmSiteNameCommand.h.body: The header declares the `cmSiteNameCommand` function that implements the `site_name` command in CMake. It pulls in the project‑wide configuration (`cmConfigure.h`), pulls in `string` and `vector` from the standard library, and forward‑declares a `cmExecutionStatus` type that represents the outcome state of a command. The function prototype returns a `bool` signalling success or failure and takes a `const std::vector<std::string>&` of arguments together with a reference to a `cmExecutionStatus` object that callers can use to inspect detailed status after execution. The file is used by other parts of the build system to invoke the command.

@l./Source/cmSourceFile.cxx.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmSourceFile.cxx.body: The file implements a `cmSourceFile` class that represents a source file in the CMake build system. It tracks the file’s path, extension, language, and whether it is generated, and manages properties such as compile options, definitions, and include directories. The class stores these values in lists that remember back‑trace information. It exposes methods to mark the file as generated, resolve the full path (including handling of missing files and policy variations such as CMP0115/0118), and to query and set properties that may affect the build. Internally it uses helper utilities like `cmSystemTools::FileExists` and `cmMakefile` state to perform the necessary look‑ups, and caches the computed properties to avoid recomputation.

@l./Source/cmSourceFile.h.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmSourceFile.h.body:
The header implements the `cmSourceFile` class, which models a source file described in a CMake makefile.  
Its responsibilities include:

* Storing the file’s name, location, and whether it was generated.  
* Managing a set of properties (via `cmPropertyMap`) that can be set, removed, or queried.  
* Holding compile‑time options, definitions, and include directories.  
* Providing helper functions to resolve the file’s full path, detect its language, and maintain a list of its dependencies.  
* Exposing a `cmCustomCommand` that may be associated with the file.  

The interface gives convenience wrappers (`SetProperty`, `GetProperty`, `AppendProperty`) and a small set of helpers (`IsGenerated`, `ResolveFullPath`).  
The file also defines a few regex constants for file‑type detection.

@l./Source/cmSourceFileLocation.cxx.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmSourceFileLocation.cxx.body: The source file defines the `cmSourceFileLocation` class, which encapsulates a source file’s directory, name, and flags that indicate whether the directory or extension are ambiguous. Its constructors resolve paths against the current makefile context, collapse relative paths, and determine whether a file’s extension is a known compiler‑specific type. The class offers utilities to update an existing location with new information, to resolve ambiguous paths to the current source or binary tree, and to compare two locations for equivalence while accounting for ambiguous extensions and directories.

@l./Source/cmSourceFileLocation.h.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmSourceFileLocation.h.body: The header defines a small helper class that records how much of a source file’s path is known at any moment. When a source file is first referenced it is instantiated with an initial name; the class then stores whether the directory part of that path is still ambiguous and whether the file‑extension is known. The API lets callers mark that the file is known to reside in either the source tree or the build tree and offers predicates to test whether two such records could refer to the same file (the “Matches” test). Finally, the class exposes helpers for retrieving the best‑known directory, name, and fully‑qualified path, plus access to the owning makefile instance that created the record.

@l./Source/cmSourceFileLocationKind.h.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmSourceFileLocationKind.h.body: The header defines a small enum used throughout the project to tag source file locations. The two values indicate whether a file’s exact location is user‑supplied and thus potentially ambiguous, or whether it’s confirmed at a known absolute path. All other modules refer to this enum to decide whether to resolve or guess a file path during build or run time.

@l./Source/cmSourceGroup.cxx.author: AI Short Overview

@l./Source/cmSourceGroup.h.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmSourceGroup.h.body:
The header defines a `cmSourceGroup` type that tracks a named set of source files.  
Internally it keeps a name, a regular‑expression for matching file names, a list of explicitly added file names, and a vector of child groups. The class exposes helpers to add files and children, to look up a child by name, to check whether a file name matches the group’s own list or regex (and recursively in children), and to assign a `cmSourceFile` instance to the group.  It also provides accessors to return the full group name, the list of assigned source files, and the vector of child groups.

@l./Source/cmSourceGroupCommand.cxx.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmSourceGroupCommand.cxx.body: This file implements the `cmSourceGroupCommand` command, parsing supplied arguments to determine a source group name, optional regex, and a tree‑style hierarchy of files. It tokenizes the tree path, collapses paths relative to the current source directory, validates that all target paths share the same prefix, and then adds each file to the appropriate source‑group objects (creating any needed groups). The code handles short‑syntax “TREE” forms, prefix options, and optional regexes, ensuring proper error reporting and proper registration of source files in the makefile’s internal group structures.

@l./Source/cmSourceGroupCommand.h.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmSourceGroupCommand.h.body:
A single function declaration in the header provides a thin wrapper around the command‑processing logic used by the build system.  
The `cmSourceGroupCommand` function returns a `bool` indicating success or failure, accepts a read‑only vector of command‑line arguments, and writes a `cmExecutionStatus` object that reports error details and exit status.  
The header also forward‑declares `cmExecutionStatus` and pulls in the minimal standard types needed for string handling and vector storage.

@l./Source/cmStandardLevel.h.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmStandardLevel.h.body: The header supplies a tiny wrapper type that stores an integer index and offers an accessor plus an ordering comparison. It’s meant for lightweight ordering in container logic, and you can make the comparison operator constexpr and verify the use of std::size_t for safety.

@l./Source/cmStandardLevelResolver.cxx.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmStandardLevelResolver.cxx.body: The file implements a small framework that maps language names (C, CXX, CUDA, etc.) to their supported standard levels and uses that mapping to compute what compile‑flag is needed to request a particular standard on a given target. It contains a helper class, `StandardLevelComputer`, that holds a language’s list of standard numbers and their string forms; its methods examine the target’s current standard property, the compiler’s defaults, policy status (CMP0128), and whether extensions are requested, and produce the correct compile‑option string (e.g., `CMAKE_C_STANDARD_99_EXTENSIONS_COMPILE_OPTION`). The public resolver class, `cmStandardLevelResolver`, exposes methods that translate a target and language into either the effective standard string or the compile‑option string, and also check if a particular compile‑feature is supported by a compiler.

@l./Source/cmStandardLevelResolver.h.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmStandardLevelResolver.h.body: The header defines a helper class that works with a makefile to discover which C/C++ standard level a target must use.  It exposes utilities to ask for the appropriate compile option string for a language‑feature‑config trio, verify that a target supports a requested feature, and compute whether a new standard is required when a feature change occurs.  The class relies on `cm::optional` to represent an absent standard and returns errors via optional string outputs.

@l./Source/cmStandardLexer.h.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmStandardLexer.h.body: The file sets up a set of compile‑time macros and type aliases that smooth over platform differences, pulls in the required system headers, and silences a handful of compiler warnings on MSVC and GCC, so that other parts of the lexer can rely on a stable set of types and flags.

@l./Source/cmState.cxx.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmState.cxx.body: The file implements the core runtime state machine for the *cmake* build system. It stores global and per‑directory variable scopes, caches, and command definitions. It loads and writes cache files, exposes a cache API (add/remove entries, query types), and manages built‑in and script‑defined commands, including flow‑control and disallowed commands. It supports enabling language features, handling of policy scopes, and tracks directories and file lists used during processing. The state object also provides snapshots for nested scopes (buildsystem, functions, macros, includes, inlining) and allows restoring to previous snapshots. Internally it maintains a policy stack, property definitions, and global properties used by the build system.

@l./Source/cmState.h.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmState.h.body: cmState represents the core runtime engine that holds the entire build‑state of a project. It stores and retrieves cache entries (including typed values, strings, and booleans), offers an API for defining and querying custom properties, and keeps track of which languages are enabled. The class owns a set of built‑in and user‑defined commands (including flow‑control ones) and can also register script‑based commands. Snapshot objects allow temporary capture and restoration of the current state, and the engine can create snapshots for specific file inclusions or nested calls. The object is also responsible for persisting the state to disk (loading and saving the cache) and for cooperating with a dependency provider for dependency analysis.

@l./Source/cmStateDirectory.cxx.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmStateDirectory.cxx.body: A `cmStateDirectory` object stores and manages the mutable data for a single build‑system directory: its own source/binary directories, child directories, target lists, and a set of property values. It keeps an in‑memory snapshot of the current property values and a back‑trace of where that snapshot originated. The class offers helpers to set or clear each property, to push back‑lists of include, compile, link options, and to serialize those lists for later serialization or reporting. The implementation relies on a small helper set of `Append`, `Set`, and `Clear` routines that maintain the internal vectors and keep the snapshot index in sync. The class also supports retrieving a property value by name, optionally following the chain of parents, and can list all available property keys.

@l./Source/cmStateDirectory.h.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmStateDirectory.h.body:
cmStateDirectory is a helper that holds the current directory’s configuration in the build‑system snapshot.  
It keeps a pointer to the tree node that represents the directory and a Snapshot_ of that state.  
Through its public interface it exposes getters/setters for the current source and binary paths, the lists of include directories, compile‑time definitions, compile and link options, and link directories.  
The class also stores arbitrary properties (strings mapped to cmValue) and exposes helper functions to add normal or imported target names.  
Internally it uses BT (a generic vector wrapper) to copy and store vectors of strings, and the back‑trace object (cmListFileBacktrace) to record where the property was added.

@l./Source/cmStatePrivate.h.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmStatePrivate.h.body: Defines internal snapshot structures for policy and directory state management. It introduces `SnapshotDataType`, a container of tree iterators and scope information; `PolicyStackEntry`, a lightweight wrapper of `cmPolicies::PolicyMap` with a weak‑flag; and `BuildsystemDirectoryStateType`, which holds directory paths, include/compile/link lists, target names, and properties. These types underpin the state‑snapshot logic used throughout the project.

@l./Source/cmStateSnapshot.cxx.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmStateSnapshot.cxx.body:
`cmStateSnapshot` encapsulates a position in the CMake state tree, providing navigation, policy handling, and variable resolution. Key responsibilities:

- **Navigation** – methods expose the current scope’s directory, its parent, and the surrounding call‑stack hierarchy.
- **Policy stack** – policy push/pop and status queries work with the snapshot’s policy chain; queried policies search upward through the directory stack until a definition is found.
- **Variable resolution** – definitions can be localized, lifted, or queried in the current or parent scope; closure keys and definition checks rely on the internal `cmDefinitions` helper.
- **Initialization helpers** – default host‑specific macros (`WIN32`, `UNIX`, `APPLE`…) and the platform‑independent CMake version are injected into the snapshot upon creation.

@l./Source/cmStateSnapshot.h.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmStateSnapshot.h.body: The header declares the `cmStateSnapshot` class, a lightweight handle that records the current state of a `cmState` at a specific position in the build graph. The snapshot exposes an API for inspecting and manipulating that snapshot: retrieving variable definitions, testing initialization, adding or removing definitions, and raising scopes. It also centralizes policy handling, allowing policies to be queried, pushed, or popped in the snapshot’s scope. Finally, the class provides navigation helpers—methods to walk up or down the call‑stack and to enumerate child snapshots—so a caller can traverse the snapshot tree during a recursive build or a nested command execution.

@l./Source/cmStateTypes.h.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmStateTypes.h.body:
The file supplies a small set of value‑classes that the rest of the
cmake plumbing uses to describe the state of a build:  

* `SnapshotDataType` lives in `cmStateDetail` and is wrapped in a
`cmLinkedTree` iterator (`PositionType`) to walk snapshot trees.  
* In `cmStateEnums` the code declares a handful of enums that
categorise the kinds of snapshots (`BaseType … InlineListFileType`), the
different target kinds (`EXECUTABLE … UNKNOWN_LIBRARY`), cache entries
(`BOOL, PATH, … UNINITIALIZED`), and artifact types (`RuntimeBinary…`).  
* `cmTraceEnums::TraceOutputFormat` defines a small list of trace output
formats (`Human`, `JSONv1`).

These types are the building blocks used elsewhere in the
build‑state and trace‑generation logic.

@l./Source/cmString.cxx.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmString.cxx.body:
The file implements a lightweight wrapper around a shared‑string buffer that can lazily materialise a stable std::string copy. The wrapper keeps a small string_view pointing into the underlying buffer; when an operation that requires a null‑terminated string is requested, it materialises a std::string that holds the data in a freshly allocated copy. The key methods in the file expose

* the view (`view()`) that gives a `string_view` over the current content,
* a `copy()` that copies a requested slice into a destination buffer,
* `substr()`, `insert()`, and `erase()` which each rebuild the internal buffer via temporary `std::string` objects,
* and a global `operator<<` and `operator+=` that forward to the underlying `std::string` view.

The implementation uses `std::shared_ptr<std::string>` (`string_`) to share owned buffers among copies, and a private `stabilize()` to force a copy‑on‑write when necessary.

@l./Source/cmString.hxx.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmString.hxx.body:
`cmString.hxx` defines a lightweight, view‑based string type (`cm::String`) that can either own a `std::string` or borrow a buffer. A value‑type (`string_view`) is used for the view.  

The file implements two compile‑time traits: `IntoString` (converts arbitrary types into an owned string or a view) and `AsStringView` (converts arbitrary types into a `string_view`).  

`cm::String` supports construction from any type that satisfies `IntoString`, copying, moving, and borrowing. It keeps an internal `std::shared_ptr<std::string>` for owned buffers and a `string_view` for the view.  

Operations cover comparison, concatenation (including `StringOpPlus` utilities), comparison operators, replacement, insertion, erasing, resizing, and standard string operations (`substr`, `find`, `rfind`, etc.) while keeping the implementation efficient by building temporary `std::string` buffers only when mutation is required.

@l./Source/cmStringAlgorithms.cxx.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmStringAlgorithms.cxx.body: Provides helper routines for manipulating text strings: trimming spaces, stripping surrounding quotes, escaping quotation marks, tokenising a string by a separator, and building string representations of numbers. It also offers a set of `cmAlphaNum` overloads that format integers and floating‑point values into views, and utilities for concatenating multiple string views with reserved buffers.  It includes generic joiners that accept ranges of strings and a separator, and utility conversion helpers (`cmStrToLong`, `cmStrToULong`, etc.) that wrap standard C conversion routines with error handling.

@l./Source/cmStringAlgorithms.h.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmStringAlgorithms.h.body: Provides a compact toolbox for manipulating string data in C++ – functions for trimming whitespace, stripping quotes, escaping quotes, joining iterable ranges into single strings (with optional prefixes/suffixes), tokenising by separators, and detecting prefixes/suffixes. It also supplies a small helper type (cmAlphaNum) to embed literal numbers into string concatenations, and helper routines for converting textual numbers to integral types. The utilities are type‑safe, template‑based, and aim for easy, efficient string handling in codebases.

@l./Source/cmStringCommand.cxx.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmStringCommand.cxx.body: The file implements a command‑driven string helper that registers a set of sub‑commands (e.g. `REGEX`, `REPLACE`, `MD5`, `TOUPPER`, `COMPARE`, `ASCII`, `HEX`, `CONFIGURE`, `LENGTH`, `APPEND`, `PREPEND`, `CONCAT`, `JOIN`, `SUBSTRING`, `STRIP`, `REPEAT`, `RANDOM`, `FIND`, `TIMESTAMP`, `MAKE_C_IDENTIFIER`, `GENEX_STRIP`, `UUID`, `JSON`). Each handler manipulates a string according to its semantics (regex matching/replace, hashing, case conversion, string comparison, ASCII/hex code generation, string configuration, length query, appending/prepending, concatenation, joining, substring extraction, trimming, repetition, random‑generation, position finding, timestamp creation, C‑identifier sanitisation, generator‑expression stripping, UUID generation, JSON path extraction). All operations ultimately store the resulting string in the current makefile via `cmMakefile::AddDefinition`. The file pulls in a broad set of utilities (regular expressions, system tools, string utilities, UUID and JSON handling) and wires them together under a single entry point `cmStringCommand`.

@l./Source/cmStringCommand.h.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmStringCommand.h.body:
The header declares a single helper routine that analyses a list of command‑line arguments supplied to the build system. It pulls in the build‑time configuration header (`cmConfigure.h` via an IWYU pragma), and pulls in the standard `<string>` and `<vector>` headers for string manipulation.  
The interface is:

```cpp
bool cmStringCommand(const std::vector<std::string>& args, cmExecutionStatus& status);
```

The `cmExecutionStatus` type is forward‑declared here; its definition lives elsewhere in the project. This routine returns a `bool` indicating whether the supplied arguments were successfully parsed/processed, and it reports any status information via the `status` reference. The file therefore serves as a thin wrapper around the core string‑parsing logic used across the project.

@l./Source/cmStringReplaceHelper.cxx.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmStringReplaceHelper.cxx.body:
The helper constructs a `cmStringReplaceHelper` with a regex pattern and a replacement expression.  
During construction it parses the replacement expression into literal parts and back‑reference tokens (e.g., “\1”, “\n”, “\\”).  
`Replace()` scans an input string for matches to the regex, and for each match constructs an output string by appending non‑matched substrings plus the corresponding parts of the replacement expression (plain literals or captured groups). It also records each match in a `cmMakefile` object if supplied. If the replacement expression contains an out‑of‑range reference, or if a capture group would exceed the input bounds, the method returns false and sets an error message.

@l./Source/cmStringReplaceHelper.h.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmStringReplaceHelper.h.body: The header declares a small helper that, given a regular‑expression pattern and a replacement pattern, parses the latter into literal and back‑reference parts and then uses the built‑in engine to apply those replacements to a string. The helper keeps the compiled regex and the parsed replacement chunks in a private vector, checks validity flags, and exposes a single `Replace` method that fills a caller‑supplied output string.

@l./Source/cmSubcommandTable.cxx.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmSubcommandTable.cxx.body:
The file implements a tiny lookup table that maps string keys to callable command objects.  
During construction the initializer list is sorted by key so that `operator()` can perform a binary‑search (`std::lower_bound`) in `operator()` to find a matching entry quickly; if found it invokes the command with the supplied arguments, otherwise it records an error in the status object.

@l./Source/cmSubcommandTable.h.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmSubcommandTable.h.body:
cmSubcommandTable implements a lookup table that maps string keys to callbacks that take a vector of strings and a mutable status object.  
The constructor takes an initializer list of pairs of static string views and function pointers; these are stored in an internal vector.  
When operator() is invoked, it searches this vector for an entry whose key matches the supplied string view, and if found executes the associated function, passing the supplied arguments and status reference.  
The design is meant to give a lightweight dispatch mechanism for sub‑commands in the larger cmake system, providing a single entry point for command resolution and execution.

@l./Source/cmSubdirCommand.cxx.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmSubdirCommand.cxx.body: The file implements the `cmSubdirCommand` routine. It receives a list of directory names and a status object, interprets the list, and registers each entry as a sub‑directory in the build system. The routine first inspects the arguments for special switches: `EXCLUDE_FROM_ALL` turns on an exclusion flag, and the `PREORDER` flag is ignored. For each argument it distinguishes between a relative path (relative to the current source directory) and an absolute path. It tests whether the path refers to an actual directory. On success it builds the corresponding binary‑directory path and invokes `mf.AddSubDirectory` to record the mapping. If any supplied path does not exist, the routine records an error via `status.SetError` and returns `false`; otherwise it returns `true` once all entries have been processed.

@l./Source/cmSubdirCommand.h.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmSubdirCommand.h.body: The header declares a helper that interprets a list of command‑line arguments and produces a sub‑directory‑specific command, reporting success or failure via a supplied `cmExecutionStatus` reference. It pulls in the project configuration header and exposes a boolean return flag to callers.

@l./Source/cmSubdirDependsCommand.cxx.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmSubdirDependsCommand.cxx.body: The file implements a single helper function that, when called, unconditionally returns `true`. It accepts a vector of strings (probably representing sub‑directories or arguments) and a reference to a `cmExecutionStatus` object, and performs no actual logic beyond the simple return. The implementation is essentially a stub that signals success without performing any work.

@l./Source/cmSyntheticTargetCache.h.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmSyntheticTargetCache.h.body: cmSyntheticTargetCache is a lightweight holder that keeps a single `std::map` mapping string identifiers to pointers to `cmGeneratorTarget` objects.  It is declared in a header with the usual `#pragma once` guard and pulls in `"cmConfigure.h"`, `<map>`, and `<string>`.  The map is the only member of the struct and provides a straightforward lookup from module names to the corresponding target objects that are used by other parts of the system.

@l./Source/cmSystemTools.cxx.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmSystemTools.cxx.body: The file implements the *cmSystemTools* namespace that bundles a large set of helper routines used throughout the project: file‑ and directory manipulation (creating, renaming, copying, symlinking), environment variable handling, and running external commands with detailed handling of stdout/stderr redirection. It also provides tar‑archive facilities (create, list, extract) and a small argument‑parsing class *cmSystemToolsArgV*. A few lightweight callbacks and a small struct (*cmSystemToolsRPathInfo*) are used for path rewrites and diagnostics. All of the 133 public functions are essentially wrappers around low‑level POSIX APIs or convenience helpers for common tasks.

@l./Source/cmSystemTools.h.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmSystemTools.h.body: Provides a collection of helper routines for file and path handling, process control, environment manipulation, and archive (tar) utilities, covering both Unix and Windows systems.

@l./Source/cmTarget.cxx.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmTarget.cxx.body: cmTarget.cxx implements the core target abstraction for the CMake build system, offering mechanisms for managing target properties, file sets, compile and link options, import handling, and utility functions. It defines classes and helper functions to lookup and manipulate properties, file sets, and imported modules.

@l./Source/cmTarget.h.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmTarget.h.body: The header defines a `cmTarget` class that represents a target loaded from a makefile. It exposes a rich API for querying and setting target properties, compile/link options, include directories, and dependency information, as well as handling custom commands, utilities and installation rules.

@l./Source/cmTargetCompileDefinitionsCom.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmTargetCompileDefinitionsCom.body:
The file implements the `cmTargetCompileDefinitionsCommand` command.  
It defines a helper class `TargetCompileDefinitionsImpl` that inherits from `cmTargetPropCommandBase`. The class overrides three key virtual functions:  

* **HandleMissingTarget** – emits a fatal error when a target is referenced that isn’t part of the project.  
* **HandleDirectContent** – appends a joined string of definitions to the target’s `COMPILE_DEFINITIONS` property (note the miss‑spelling).  
* **Join** – concatenates supplied definitions, removing an leading “-D” from each argument and separating the rest with semicolons.  

The public entry function `cmTargetCompileDefinitionsCommand` simply creates an instance of the implementation class and forwards the supplied arguments to it.

@l./Source/cmTargetCompileDefinitionsCom.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmTargetCompileDefinitionsCom.body: The header declares a helper that takes a vector of strings describing compiler‑definition options (e.g. `-DNAME=value`) and a reference to a status object. It parses those arguments, applies them to the current build configuration, and reports success or failure via the returned boolean and the status ref.

@l./Source/cmTargetCompileFeaturesComman.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmTargetCompileFeaturesComman.body: Handles the “COMPILE_FEATURES” command by resolving feature names and attaching them to a target that is being built. It validates each feature through `cmStandardLevelResolver::AddRequiredTargetFeature`, reports any error via the make‑file message system, and on success writes the list of features back as a comma‑separated string through `cmList::to_string`.

@l./Source/cmTargetCompileFeaturesComman.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmTargetCompileFeaturesComman.body:
This header defines an interface for invoking the compile‑features helper.  
The main symbol is the function `cmTargetCompileFeaturesCommand`, which accepts a list of string arguments and a mutable status object and reports via the returned bool whether the operation succeeded.  
Internally it relies on a small `cmExecutionStatus` type (presumably holding success/failure flags and diagnostic messages) and pulls in the common configuration bits from `cmConfigure.h`. The surrounding code that calls this routine expects it to orchestrate the actual feature‑resolution logic and propagate any errors back through the status reference.

@l./Source/cmTargetCompileOptionsCommand.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmTargetCompileOptionsCommand.body:
The file implements the **cmTargetCompileOptionsCommand** command.  
At its core, it defines a class that derives from the base property‑command class.  
When invoked, it checks for a missing target and reports a fatal error if the target isn’t belong to the project.  
Otherwise it takes the supplied option strings, optionally prepends them, and inserts them into the target’s compile‑options list while respecting the CMP0101 policy. The public function simply forwards the arguments to this helper class.

@l./Source/cmTargetCompileOptionsCommand.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmTargetCompileOptionsCommand.body: This header declares a helper routine that receives a vector of command‑line arguments and a reference to a status tracker. The routine parses the supplied options, updates the build system’s configuration state, and records success or failure in the supplied status object. It is used wherever compile‑time options need to be altered programmatically.

@l./Source/cmTargetDepend.h.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmTargetDepend.h.body:
The file defines a lightweight wrapper for an edge in the target‑dependency graph.  
It stores a pointer to a `cmGeneratorTarget` and keeps three mutable flags—`Link`, `Util`, and `Cross`—along with a back‑trace list.  
The public interface lets callers mark the edge type, attach a back‑trace, and query its state; the comparison operator enables ordered insertion into a `std::set` that holds `cmTargetDepend` objects.

@l./Source/cmTargetExport.h.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmTargetExport.h.body: The header guards and forward declarations keep the implementation details out of other files. The class holds the name of a target, a pointer to the target itself, and pointers to a series of generator objects that produce archives, runtimes, libraries, bundles, headers, and other artifacts. The mapping of file‑sets to their dedicated generators lets the system assemble the right outputs for each file group. The `NamelinkOnly` flag indicates whether only the name should be exported, without linking.

@l./Source/cmTargetIncludeDirectoriesCom.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmTargetIncludeDirectoriesCom.body: The file defines a command that expands a list of include‑directory arguments for a target. It implements a helper class derived from `cmTargetPropCommandBase`. The helper joins arguments into a semicolon‑separated string, adding those that are relative paths by prefixing them with the current source directory. It records the back‑trace for error reporting and distinguishes between normal and system includes. The public interface routine `cmTargetIncludeDirectoriesCommand` creates an instance of this helper and invokes `HandleArguments` with the supplied arguments and the three processing flags (before, after, system). The implementation also provides a `HandleMissingTarget` override that emits a fatal message if the target cannot be found.

@l./Source/cmTargetIncludeDirectoriesCom.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmTargetIncludeDirectoriesCom.body:
The header declares the entry point for the *Target‑Include‑Directories* command.  
It pulls in the core configuration support (`cmConfigure.h`) and gives the function signature

```cpp
bool cmTargetIncludeDirectoriesCommand(const std::vector<std::string>& args,
                                      cmExecutionStatus& status);
```

which examines a list of directories (provided via command‑line style arguments), applies them to the current target, and reports success or failure through the supplied `cmExecutionStatus` object.

@l./Source/cmTargetLinkDirectoriesComman.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmTargetLinkDirectoriesComman.body: The file implements a command that attaches link‑directories to a target. It defines a helper class derived from cmTargetPropCommandBase that parses the arguments supplied by the “LINK_DIRECTORIES” command, normalises each path to a full path (adding the current source directory when necessary), and then inserts the resulting directory list into the target via InsertLinkDirectory. The command’s public entry point is the function cmTargetLinkDirectoriesCommand that invokes the helper’s HandleArguments routine with the parsed arguments.

@l./Source/cmTargetLinkDirectoriesComman.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmTargetLinkDirectoriesComman.body:
The header defines a helper routine used by the build‑system code to set up the link‑time search path for a target.  
- **Signature:** `bool cmTargetLinkDirectoriesCommand(const std::vector<std::string>& args, cmExecutionStatus& status);`  
  * `args` is expected to contain directory paths that should be added to the linker's search path.  
  * `status` is updated to indicate whether the operation succeeded or failed.  
- **Return value:** `true` on success, `false` otherwise.  
- **Usage context:** The function is invoked from various parts of the build engine when a target needs its link‑directories configured before invoking the linker.

@l./Source/cmTargetLinkLibrariesCommand..author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmTargetLinkLibrariesCommand..body: The file implements the `target_link_libraries` command, parsing its arguments, validating the target, handling interface/linking keywords (e.g., `LINK_INTERFACE_LIBRARIES`, `LINK_PUBLIC`, `PRIVATE`), and updating the target’s properties accordingly while respecting CMake policies for remote linking and interface handling.

@l./Source/cmTargetLinkLibrariesCommand..author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmTargetLinkLibrariesCommand..body:
The header declares the entry point for the *link‑libraries* command in the build system. It pulls in the core configuration and defines a single helper:

```cpp
bool cmTargetLinkLibrariesCommand(const std::vector<std::string>& args,
                                 cmExecutionStatus& status);
```

When invoked, the function consumes a list of library names supplied on the command line, validates them against the current configuration, and initiates the linking pass. The `cmExecutionStatus` object is populated with any diagnostic information or error codes that arise during this process. The header’s guard and the `#pragma once` ensure the declaration is emitted only once, while the included `"cmConfigure.h"` supplies the necessary context for the configuration engine that orchestrates the actual link invocation.

@l./Source/cmTargetLinkLibraryType.h.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmTargetLinkLibraryType.h.body: The header supplies an enum that distinguishes three linking modes—default, debug, and optimized—used by the build system to tag libraries accordingly.

@l./Source/cmTargetLinkOptionsCommand.cx.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmTargetLinkOptionsCommand.cx.body: The source implements a target‑specific command that adds a list of link options to a target. It derives from a generic property‑command base, overriding the three hooks: on‑missing‑target it emits a fatal error; on‑direct‑content it concatenates the supplied strings (using cmList::to_string) and inserts the result into the target’s link option list, optionally at the front; on‑join it simply merges the argument list into one string. The public helper function simply creates a TargetLinkOptionsImpl instance and forwards the supplied arguments to its HandleArguments routine, which then validates and records the options.

@l./Source/cmTargetLinkOptionsCommand.h.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmTargetLinkOptionsCommand.h.body: The header declares a helper routine that parses a collection of string arguments intended for a target‑level linking operation. The routine is expected to populate a `cmExecutionStatus` object with the outcome of the processing and signal success/failure via its boolean return value. The file’s purpose is to provide a single, reusable entry point that other parts of the code can invoke when they need to interpret and apply link‑options supplied by the user or build system.

@l./Source/cmTargetPrecompileHeadersComm.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmTargetPrecompileHeadersComm.body: The file implements the internal logic for the `PRECOMPILE_HEADERS` command in cmake. It resolves a list of header files supplied by the user, converting any relative paths into absolute ones based on the current source directory and then appends those absolute paths as a comma‑separated string to the target’s `PRECOMPILE_HEADERS` property. It also checks that the target actually exists in the current project and emits a fatal error message if not. The implementation is split into helper routines (`ConvertToAbsoluteContent`, `HandleDirectContent`, `HandleInterfaceContent`) and a public entry point (`cmTargetPrecompileHeadersCommand`) that parses the command arguments and delegates to the helper class.

@l./Source/cmTargetPrecompileHeadersComm.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmTargetPrecompileHeadersComm.body: This header declares the interface for a pre‑compile‑headers helper command. It exposes a single function that receives a list of arguments and a status object, performs the header pre‑compilation step for a target, and returns a success flag. The implementation details—such as parsing the arguments, invoking the header compiler, and populating the `cmExecutionStatus` object—are defined in the corresponding source file.

@l./Source/cmTargetPropCommandBase.cxx.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmTargetPropCommandBase.cxx.body: The file implements the core logic for a target‑property command. It parses a list of arguments, validates that the target exists and that the requested property can be applied to that target type, and then iterates over the argument list to build property values. It supports PUBLIC/PRIVATE/INTERFACE scopes, handles prepend/append semantics, and also implements special handling for pre‑compile‑header reuse and system‑specific settings. The class ultimately populates the target’s property map (e.g., INTERFACE_… or the property itself) with the constructed value string.

@l./Source/cmTargetPropCommandBase.h.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmTargetPropCommandBase.h.body: The header declares a base class that propagates property values to a target in a CMake‑style build system. It holds the property key, a target pointer, and a makefile reference, while forwarding an execution status reference. Derived classes override virtual handlers such as HandleInterfaceContent, PopulateTargetProperties, HandleMissingTarget, HandleDirectContent, and Join, and use the supplied flags to decide whether content is merged before or after existing data, whether it applies to system targets, or whether it may be reused from another target. The class also parses argument lists and joins string vectors for the final property value.

@l./Source/cmTargetPropertyComputer.cxx.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmTargetPropertyComputer.cxx.body: The file implements the logic that decides whether a target can be queried for its LOCATION property. It inspects the current policy state (CMP0026), and based on that state emits either a warning or a fatal error. It builds an explanatory message that explains the restriction and then forwards it to the surrounding make‑file object through its IssueMessage interface. The routine returns a Boolean flag that indicates whether the operation succeeded (i.e., whether a fatal error was avoided).

@l./Source/cmTargetPropertyComputer.h.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmTargetPropertyComputer.h.body: The header declares a helper that, given a target object and a property name, returns the corresponding `cmValue` by computing or looking up values such as the target’s location or its source list. It also contains logic for properties that depend on configuration names (e.g., `LOCATION_<CONFIG>` or `<CONFIG>_LOCATION`) and enforces a policy that prevents importing or incorrect use of policies. The implementation is template‑based so it works with any target type that exposes the required interface.

@l./Source/cmTargetSourcesCommand.cxx.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmTargetSourcesCommand.cxx.body: The file implements the `SOURCES` command for CMake: it parses command arguments, supports the `FILE_SET` syntax for grouping source files into file‑sets, validates file‑set names, types, and visibility, and then appends the resolved source files and directories into the target’s properties (such as `SOURCES`, `INCLUDE_DIRECTORIES`, or `INTERFACE_INCLUDE_DIRECTORIES`).

@l./Source/cmTargetSourcesCommand.h.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmTargetSourcesCommand.h.body: The header declares the `cmTargetSourcesCommand` entry point that takes a list of argument strings and a status object, parses the arguments, and populates the status flag to report success or failure. It relies on the common `cmConfigure.h` infrastructure and uses standard containers (`std::vector`/`std::string`). The function returns `true` on successful processing and `false` on error, signalling the calling code what went wrong. The file also shows that this routine is referenced from several other modules, indicating it serves as a central command‑handling routine in the build system.

@l./Source/cmTest.cxx.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmTest.cxx.body: The `cmTest` class encapsulates a test case inside the build system. It keeps a reference to the owning makefile, records the test’s name and command list, and tracks whether the old test‑style syntax is in use. Property values are resolved through its internal property map, with fallback logic that checks the owning makefile for chained properties under the `TEST` scope. When a property is requested, the class first queries its own map; if not found, it queries the owning makefile’s state for a chained property; if still absent, it returns `nullptr`. The class also exposes whether command lists should be automatically expanded during command execution.

@l./Source/cmTest.h.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmTest.h.body: cmTest.h declares a small class that represents a test instance. It stores the test’s name, command line, and a property map, providing setters/getters to manipulate these attributes, query whether the test uses the old syntax or list expansion, and to retrieve the owning makefile and back‑trace information.

@l./Source/cmTestGenerator.cxx.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmTestGenerator.cxx.body: The file implements a test‑generation helper that emits CMake test commands. It wraps policy checks (CMP0110) to decide whether a test name must be quoted with `[==…==]` brackets, computing the required number of `=` characters. It handles per‑configuration test generation: if a test is configuration‑aware it emits separate `add_test` and `set_tests_properties` invocations; otherwise it produces a single invocation in the old style. It expands argument lists, deals with cross‑compilation emulation and translates back‑traces into a `_BACKTRACE_TRIPLES` string. It also provides helpers to evaluate command‑line arguments, escape them for CMake, and emits internal properties for each test.

@l./Source/cmTestGenerator.h.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmTestGenerator.h.body: The `cmTestGenerator` class is a thin wrapper around a test‑object that turns its configuration data into a ready‑to‑run install script. It stores a pointer to the originating `cmTest` and to a local‑generator context, and in `Compute()` emits the proper script fragments by walking the test’s configuration list. The helper methods `GenerateScriptForConfig`, `GenerateScriptNoConfig`, and `GenerateScriptConfigs` take care of the various script sections, while `GenerateInternalProperties` writes out the test’s internal metadata. Public helpers such as `TestsForConfig()` and `GetTest()` expose the test’s identity and its applicability to a specific configuration. The class purposefully deletes copy semantics to enforce unique ownership and uses `override` on the virtual functions it provides.

@l./Source/cmTimestamp.cxx.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmTimestamp.cxx.body:
Provides helpers for formatting timestamps from epoch values, including current wall‑clock and file modification times.  
The code pulls timestamps from libuv, converts them to UTC if requested, and emits a string according to a format string.  
It parses custom format codes (e.g. %a, %b, %f…) and handles special cases on AIX and MinGW.  
When the environment variable `SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH` is set, it substitutes that epoch so builds are reproducible.  
The implementation takes care to restore any modified TZ or XPG_SUS_ENV variables that affect time‑zones.

@l./Source/cmTimestamp.h.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmTimestamp.h.body:
cmTimestamp.h supplies a lightweight helper that returns timestamps formatted as strings.  
Its public interface offers helpers for the current clock, a file’s mtime, or for building a timestamp from a raw `time_t`.  
Each routine accepts a format string (e.g. `%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S`) and a flag that controls whether UTC or local time is used.  
Internally the helper converts a `tm` structure to an UTC‐based `time_t` and then assembles the final string piece‑by‑piece.

@l./Source/cmTransformDepfile.cxx.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmTransformDepfile.cxx.body: The source implements a utility that reads a GCC‑generated dependency file, optionally adjusts paths relative to the top‑level binary directory, and then emits a new dependency file in one of three supported formats (plain GCC, Make‑style, or MSBuild AdditionalInputs). The key routine, `cmTransformDepfile`, orchestrates this conversion: it loads the original file, normalises paths, writes properly escaped filenames, and inserts “phony” targets when the Make format is requested. The implementation also handles MSBuild specific details such as writing a UTF‑8 BOM and normalising path separators.

@l./Source/cmTransformDepfile.h.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmTransformDepfile.h.body: The header declares an enum of supported dependency‑file formats (GCC, Make, MSBuild) and exposes a single helper routine that, given an input file, a target format, and a local generator object, produces a new dependency file in the chosen format. The routine is used by other modules to read existing dep files and rewrite them for the chosen build system.

@l./Source/cmTryCompileCommand.cxx.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmTryCompileCommand.cxx.body: The file implements the CMake `try_compile()` command: it parses the supplied arguments, selects the target type (executable or static library) from `CMAKE_TRY_COMPILE_TARGET_TYPE`, invokes `cmCoreTryCompile` to attempt compilation, logs the outcome, and, if requested, cleans up generated files unless debug‑try‑compile is enabled.

@l./Source/cmTryCompileCommand.h.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmTryCompileCommand.h.body: The header exposes a single API: `cmTryCompileCommand`, which accepts a list of command‑line arguments and a status object that receives diagnostics. It returns `true` when the command is successfully compiled, otherwise `false`. The implementation is defined elsewhere; this file only declares the interface and pulls in the necessary configuration headers.

@l./Source/cmTryRunCommand.cxx.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmTryRunCommand.cxx.body: The file implements the `try_run()` command in CMake. It parses the arguments supplied to `try_run`, compiles the target program (using the core try‑compile logic), and, if compilation succeeds, runs the resulting executable. It captures stdout/stderr, stores the output in optional cache variables, and records the exit code. The logic distinguishes normal and cross‑compiling contexts—cross‑compile mode uses stubbed results and writes a “TryRunResults.cmake” file that records the outcome and output contents for later use. The `TryRunCommandImpl` class inherits from `cmCoreTryCompile` and drives the whole flow, emitting detailed CMake‑style logs via `WriteTryRunEvent` when requested. The helper functions `RunExecutable` and `DoNotRunExecutable` take care of the actual run, of the emulator handling, and of cleaning up after a try‑run. The command returns success status via a `cmExecutionStatus` object.

@l./Source/cmTryRunCommand.h.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmTryRunCommand.h.body: The header declares a helper for invoking external tools: the routine `cmTryRunCommand` accepts a list of command‑line tokens (`args`) and a `cmExecutionStatus` object to be filled with run‑results. It returns `true` when the command runs successfully (exit status 0 and status‑flags set accordingly). The implementation is expected to be agnostic to the specific tool; callers supply the full token sequence. The interface is intentionally minimal—no side‑effects beyond filling `status`—so callers can inspect the execution result and decide on‑retry or error handling.

@l./Source/cmUVHandlePtr.cxx.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmUVHandlePtr.cxx.body:
This file implements a small RAII‑style wrapper around libuv handles.  
Each handle type (e.g. `uv_async_t`, `uv_signal_t`, `uv_pipe_t`, etc.) has a dedicated deleter that knows how to free the underlying C struct safely; for types that need special shutdown logic (like async or signal) the deleter acquires a mutex to guard against concurrent close/send races. The generic `uv_handle_ptr_base_<T>` template handles allocation with `calloc` and reset logic, storing a `std::unique_ptr` with the appropriate deleter. Convenience wrappers (`uv_async_ptr`, `uv_signal_ptr`, etc.) expose `init`, `start`, `stop`, `spawn` methods that internally call the corresponding libuv functions through the stored pointer. The file also defines explicit instantiations for each handle type via macro `UV_HANDLE_PTR_INSTANTIATE_EXPLICIT`.

@l./Source/cmUVHandlePtr.h.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmUVHandlePtr.h.body:
The header supplies a generic RAII smart‑pointer wrapper around libuv handle types.  
A base template owns a `shared_ptr` to the underlying C struct, offers `init`, `reset` and cast operators, and is specialized by derived types (`uv_async_ptr`, `uv_pipe_ptr`, `uv_process_ptr`, etc.).  
Move semantics and in‑place reset logic keep handles alive until libuv closes them, while helper constructors/overloads make handling of specific handle types concise and type‑safe.

@l./Source/cmUVProcessChain.cxx.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmUVProcessChain.cxx.body: It implements a fluent builder that lets a caller list command sequences; each command becomes a child process whose standard streams can be redirected to existing pipes, to other processes in the chain, or to the caller’s own descriptors. When the chain is started, it allocates a libuv event loop, spawns every child process, wiring the input, output, and error streams according to the builder’s “builtin”, “external”, “none” settings. Each child is wrapped in a small wrapper that stores its exit code and termination signal; the wrapper’s callback records the exit status and marks the child finished, so the chain can report whether all processes have terminated. The public API lets a client query the exit information of each child, wait for completion with a timeout, and cleanly shut down the loop when the chain finishes.

@l./Source/cmUVProcessChain.h.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmUVProcessChain.h.body:
The header defines a fluent API for assembling a pipeline of commands.  
A `cmUVProcessChainBuilder` collects process arguments and stream configurations (stdin, stdout, stderr) and can redirect them to pipes, file descriptors, or the parent process.  
Calling `Start()` produces a `cmUVProcessChain` that runs the configured chain, providing status monitoring, waiting, and cleanup.  
The chain exposes a small status API (`GetStatus`, `Finished`, `Wait`) and a set of exception codes that map errors during process spawning or execution.

@l./Source/cmUVStream.h.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmUVStream.h.body: The header implements a thin C++ wrapper that turns libuv streams into standard iostreams. It exposes a template‑driven `cmBasicUVIStream` that holds a `cmBasicUVStreambuf` buffer and forwards open/close operations. A convenience `cmBasicUVPipeIStream` derives from it to wrap an `uv_pipe` handle, allowing construction with a loop and file descriptor. The helper `cmUVStreamRead` helper creates a read‑callback holder (`cmUVStreamReadHandle`) that stores user‑supplied read and finish callbacks, assigns the handle to the stream’s `data` field, and hooks the libuv read callbacks to invoke those callbacks when data arrives or EOF is reached.

@l./Source/cmUVStreambuf.h.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmUVStreambuf.h.body: The header implements a C++ stream buffer that wraps a libuv stream into the standard stream‑buffer interface. It inherits from `std::basic_streambuf`, holds a pointer to a `uv_stream_t`, and provides `open()`/`close()` to attach or detach the stream. Internally it buffers incoming data in a `std::vector` and uses libuv callbacks to refill the buffer on underflow, allowing code to read the stream as if it were a normal `std::istream`.

@l./Source/cmUnsetCommand.cxx.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmUnsetCommand.cxx.body:
The file implements a helper that processes an *unset* request.  
When called, it verifies that the caller supplied one or two arguments; any other count triggers an error in the returned status.  

The first argument is interpreted as the name of the entity to remove. Three cases are distinguished:

1. **Environment variable** – if the string begins with the literal prefix `ENV{`, the code extracts the name that follows the brace and, unless compiled with `CMAKE_BOOTSTRAP`, calls the system‑level routine to unset that environment variable.

2. **Makefile definition** – if only one argument is supplied, the routine removes the variable’s definition from the current makefile context.

3. **Makefile cache / parent‑scope entries** – a second argument may be the literal strings `CACHE` or `PARENT_SCOPE`. In these cases the routine removes the variable from the cached values or demotes it to the parent scope, respectively.

If the arguments do not match any of these patterns the function records an error in the `cmExecutionStatus` object and returns `false`.

@l./Source/cmUnsetCommand.h.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmUnsetCommand.h.body: The header declares a helper that accepts a list of argument strings and a status object, clearing a named CMAKE variable and reporting success via a boolean.

@l./Source/cmUseMangledMesaCommand.cxx.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmUseMangledMesaCommand.cxx.body: The code implements a helper routine that, when invoked with two arguments, copies every *.h file from a specified Mesa source tree into a target directory while adjusting any `#include` directives that refer to the original header files. The routine first checks that the required `gl.h` file exists in the source tree and then enumerates all header files found by `cmSystemTools::Glob`. For each file it opens the source file, scans each line, and rewrites any `#include` that points to a `gl/` or `GL/` path by redirecting the include to the new destination directory. The updated header file is written to a temporary file and finally moved into place if it differs from any pre‑existing copy. Errors are reported via `cmSystemTools::Error`, and status is communicated through a `cmExecutionStatus` object.

@l./Source/cmUtilitySourceCommand.cxx.author: AI Short Overview
@l./Source/cmUtilitySourceCommand.cxx.body: The function `cmUtilitySourceCommand` validates an invocation of a CMake utility by checking that a cached executable path exists.
